Storage backends for the transitions log.\\n//!\\n//! The transactions layer only needs three things from its log: append\\n//! one entry, read every entry back in write order, and make what has\\n//! been appended durable. [`TransitionLogStore`] captures exactly that,\\n//! so a consumer can plug in whichever log it already has.\\n//!\\n//! Two implementations ship with the library:\\n//!\\n//! * [`NamedTypesDecorator`] — the original sidecar *links* log, where\\n//!   each entry is the name of a freshly created link. Keeps the log in\\n//!   the same format the C# port uses.\\n//! * [`FileTransitionLog`] — a plain append-only text file, one entry\\n//!   per line, `fsync`ed on every append by default. Cheaper than a\\n//!   links database. An incomplete final line is discarded on open or\\n//!   before reusing a writer after an I/O error.\\n//!\\n//! Reading takes `&mut self` because the links-backed log resolves\\n//! names through [`NamedTypes::get_name`], which needs mutable access\\n//! to its own caches.\\n\\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\\nuse std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\\n\\nuse crate::error::LinkError;\\nuse crate::named_types::{NamedTypes, NamedTypesDecorator};\\n\\n/// Append-only store of serialized transitions and recovery markers.\\npub trait TransitionLogStore {\\n    /// Appends one entry. Entries never contain newlines.\\n    fn append_log_entry(&mut self, entry: &str) -> Result<(), LinkError>;\\n\\n    /// Reads every entry back, oldest first.\\n    fn read_log_entries(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<String>, LinkError>;\\n\\n    /// Makes every appended entry durable.\\n    fn flush_log(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError>;\\n\\n    /// Whether flush requests persistent storage. Custom/volatile logs default\\n    /// to false; this describes an adapter, not the reliability of its hardware.\\n    fn supports_durable_flush(&self) -> bool {\\n        false\\n    }\\n}\\n\\nfn storage_error(error: anyhow::Error) -> LinkError {\\n    LinkError::StorageError(format!(\\\"{error:#}\\\"))\\n}\\n\\nimpl TransitionLogStore for NamedTypesDecorator {\\n    fn supports_durable_flush(&self) -> bool {\\n        !self.links().database_path().as_os_str().is_empty()\\n    }\\n    fn append_log_entry(&mut self, entry: &str) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\\n        // Always allocate a fresh link so entries never overwrite one\\n        // another (mirrors C# `CreateAndUpdate(Null, Null)`).\\n        let link = self.create(0, 0);\\n        self.set_name(link, entry).map_err(storage_error)?;\\n        Ok(())\\n    }\\n\\n    fn read_log_entries(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<String>, LinkError> {\\n        let mut addresses: Vec<u32> = self.all().into_iter().map(|link| link.index).collect();\\n        addresses.sort_unstable();\\n        let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(addresses.len());\\n        for address in addresses {\\n            if let Some(name) = NamedTypes::get_name(self, address).map_err(storage_error)? {\\n                entries.push(name);\\n            }\\n        }\\n        Ok(entries)\\n    }\\n\\n    fn flush_log(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\\n        crate::LinksStorage::flush(self)\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Append-only, line-oriented transitions log backed by a single file.\\n///\\n/// # Durability\\n///\\n/// With `sync_on_append` enabled (the default) every\\n/// [`append_log_entry`](TransitionLogStore::append_log_entry) returns\\n/// only after the entry has reached stable storage, which is what makes\\n/// the write-ahead ordering of the transactions layer meaningful: a\\n/// transition is always durable before the data-store write it\\n/// describes is reported as committed. A failed retry read retains ownership too. C# retries finish\nsynchronously even through `CommitAsync`.\nExplicit and automatic version owners retain admission until their checkpoint\nand branch publication succeed, including named writes. Automatic row writes\ncreate an implicit version owner before mutation. Pre-commit write/callback/log\nerrors undo through that owner; a failed undo keeps it for cleanup retry. After\na commit attempt, cleanup resolves that attempt and finishes publication instead\nof undoing a possibly durable decision. A checkpoint marker must follow durable data; staging avoids exposing partial transactions. |\n| [PostgreSQL isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html) | [predicate.c](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/backend/storage/lmgr/predicate.c) | Snapshot isolation permits write skew. A whole-store revision check is conservative but safe. |\n| [RocksDB transactions](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/wiki/Transactions) | [optimistic_transaction.cc](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/utilities/transactions/optimistic_transaction.cc), [pessimistic_transaction.cc](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/utilities/transactions/pessimistic_transaction.cc) | Offer pessimistic exclusion and optimistic validation explicitly. Locks, version tracking, retries, and history have different costs. |\n| [Redis replication](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/replication/) | [replication.c](https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/unstable/src/replication.c) | Asynchronous primary/follower copies improve read scale. Waiting for replica acknowledgements alone does not provide consensus or safe automatic failover. |\n| [etcd API guarantees](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/learning/api_guarantees/) | [raft.go](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/main/raft.go) | Quorum intersection, a fenced leader, ordered durable logs, and safe membership changes are necessary for consensus. A fan-out log must not advertise Raft guarantees. |\n| [TiKV transactions](https://tikv.github.io/sig-transaction/doc/tikv/index.html) | [transaction](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/tree/master/src/storage/txn) | Cross-shard atomic writes require coordination and recovery beyond per-shard atomicity. Raw and transactional writes cannot be mixed safely. |\n| [FoundationDB transactions](https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/developer-guide.html), [read/write path](https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/read-write-path.html) | [NativeAPI.cpp](https://github.com/apple/foundationdb/blob/dbf079f58df53df898eee906738a506cb80a21a6/fdbclient/NativeAPI.cpp), [ConflictSet.cpp](https://github.com/apple/foundationdb/blob/dbf079f58df53df898eee906738a506cb80a21a6/fdbserver/resolver/ConflictSet.cpp) | Track observed reads, including absent keys, and validate against intervening writes. Optional local point-read validation permits disjoint edits; scans remain conservative whole-revision predicates. No FoundationDB protocol or range index is copied. |\n| [Apache Iceberg optimistic concurrency](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/#optimistic-concurrency) | [format specification](https://apache.googlesource.com/iceberg/+/HEAD/format/spec.md), optimistic concurrency and filesystem operations | Immutable data plus atomic metadata publication separates data storage from the serialization point. The partitioned journal decorator stages objects in independent groups, then compares all selected catalog generations before publishing pointers. Data files and table formats are not copied. |\n| [MySQL/InnoDB redo architecture](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/PAGE_INNODB_REDO_LOG.html), [doublewrite](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/innodb-doublewrite-buffer.html) | [log0write.cc](https://github.com/mysql/mysql-server/blob/561753af986c3c006c4b6c7caa8359748fb55b22/storage/innobase/log/log0write.cc#L1058) | A requested log position, OS-written position and durable position are distinct. One flush can release several commit waiters. Doublewrite repairs torn data pages; checksums alone only detect damage. Group commit and page repair are separate optional designs, not supplied by revision compression. |\n| [MongoDB write concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern/) | [replication_coordinator_impl.cpp](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/7a45cb24e938fa1a18dad3b1969444d5d80f8d09/src/mongo/db/repl/replication_coordinator_impl.cpp#L2194) | Durable acknowledgements and applied replica state differ. Write-concern timeout does not undo the primary's write. Preserve explicit uncertain outcomes and discover publication before retrying; a replica counter does not copy MongoDB's replication protocol. |\n| [Cassandra Dynamo architecture](https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/architecture/dynamo.html), [hints](https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/managing/operating/hints.html) | [StorageProxy.java](https://github.com/apache/cassandra/blob/05853eaeab006bd1e834331ac8b1dfdc464d1f31/src/java/org/apache/cassandra/service/StorageProxy.java#L978) | Ordinary writes use consistency-level response handlers and timestamp reconciliation. Hints are best effort; anti-entropy remains necessary. Quorum intersection alone is not a complete transaction isolation protocol. Our fixed-primary log replication does not implement Dynamo repair or timestamp conflict resolution. |\n| [Cassandra 6.0 / Accord](https://cassandra.apache.org/_/events/20261011-community-over-code-glasgow.html) | [transaction dispatch](https://github.com/apache/cassandra/blob/05853eaeab006bd1e834331ac8b1dfdc464d1f31/src/java/org/apache/cassandra/service/StorageProxy.java#L1269), [CoordinateTransaction.java](https://github.com/apache/cassandra-accord/blob/ce855de13902e7e3ebfa4356d265f0c49be1bb8e/accord-core/src/main/java/accord/coordinate/CoordinateTransaction.java#L123) | Current Cassandra includes an Accord route as well as ordinary writes. Accord chooses transaction paths using quorum responses, dependencies, timestamps and topology epochs. Our atomic catalog provides one serialization point; it does not supply Accord's leaderless protocol or its latency properties. |\n\n## Existing reusable components\n\nThe project already depends on `doublets` / `Platform.Data.Doublets` for raw\nlinks, allocation, uniqueness, and cascade policies. Its storage traits and\n`INamedTypesLinks` are extension seams. `FileTransitionLog`, advisory locks,\nTCP `RemoteLinks`, and the JS client transport contract should be reused.\nThe optional staged layer can compose validation, history, and replication\nwithout imposing their allocations or I/O on a bare in-memory cache.\n\nFor production consensus, existing maintained implementations such as\n[etcd/raft](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft),\n[OpenRaft](https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft), and\n[DotNext Raft](https://dotnet.github.io/dotNext/features/cluster/raft.html)\nprovide election and log-replication machinery. They are not interchangeable\nwith a replica acknowledgement counter. JavaScript's client transport should\nadvertise backend guarantees rather than inventing them client-side.\n\n## Source observations, pinned for reproducibility\n\nSource was downloaded through GitHub's contents API; the functions below were\nread. [2026-10-25T10:52:07.167Z] [STDOUT] {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_101","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc 'cat rust/src/transactions/log.rs; cat rust/src/transactions/replay.rs; cat rust/src/transactions/operations.rs'","aggregated_output":"//! Storage backends for the transitions log.\n//!\n//! The transactions layer only needs three things from its log: append\n//! one entry, read every entry back in write order, and make what has\n//! been appended durable. [`TransitionLogStore`] captures exactly that,\n//! so a consumer can plug in whichever log it already has.\n//!\n//! Two implementations ship with the library:\n//!\n//! * [`NamedTypesDecorator`] — the original sidecar *links* log, where\n//!   each entry is the name of a freshly created link. Keeps the log in\n//!   the same format the C# port uses.\n//! * [`FileTransitionLog`] — a plain append-only text file, one entry\n//!   per line, `fsync`ed on every append by default. Cheaper than a\n//!   links database. An incomplete final line is discarded on open or\n//!   before reusing a writer after an I/O error.\n//!\n//! Reading takes `&mut self` because the links-backed log resolves\n//! names through [`NamedTypes::get_name`], which needs mutable access\n//! to its own caches.\n\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse crate::error::LinkError;\nuse crate::named_types::{NamedTypes, NamedTypesDecorator};\n\n/// Append-only store of serialized transitions and recovery markers.\npub trait TransitionLogStore {\n    /// Appends one entry. Entries never contain newlines.\n    fn append_log_entry(&mut self, entry: &str) -> Result<(), LinkError>;\n\n    /// Reads every entry back, oldest first.\n    fn read_log_entries(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<String>, LinkError>;\n\n    /// Makes every appended entry durable.\n    fn flush_log(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError>;\n\n    /// Whether flush requests persistent storage. Custom/volatile logs default\n    /// to false; this describes an adapter, not the reliability of its hardware.\n    fn supports_durable_flush(&self) -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n}\n\nfn storage_error(error: anyhow::Error) -> LinkError {\n    LinkError::StorageError(format!(\"{error:#}\"))\n}\n\nimpl TransitionLogStore for NamedTypesDecorator {\n    fn supports_durable_flush(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.links().database_path().as_os_str().is_empty()\n    }\n    fn append_log_entry(&mut self, entry: &str) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n        // Always allocate a fresh link so entries never overwrite one\n        // another (mirrors C# `CreateAndUpdate(Null, Null)`).\n        let link = self.create(0, 0);\n        self.set_name(link, entry).map_err(storage_error)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn read_log_entries(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<String>, LinkError> {\n        let mut addresses: Vec<u32> = self.all().into_iter().map(|link| link.index).collect();\n        addresses.sort_unstable();\n        let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(addresses.len());\n        for address in addresses {\n            if let Some(name) = NamedTypes::get_name(self, address).map_err(storage_error)? {\n                entries.push(name);\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(entries)\n    }\n\n    fn flush_log(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n        crate::LinksStorage::flush(self)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Append-only, line-oriented transitions log backed by a single file.\n///\n/// # Durability\n///\n/// With `sync_on_append` enabled (the default) every\n/// [`append_log_entry`](TransitionLogStore::append_log_entry) returns\n/// only after the entry has reached stable storage, which is what makes\n/// the write-ahead ordering of the transactions layer meaningful: a\n/// transition is always durable before the data-store write it\n/// describes is reported as committed. Disabling it trades that\n/// guarantee for throughput — the log is then durable only as far as\n/// the last [`flush_log`](TransitionLogStore::flush_log).\n///\n/// An interrupted append can leave a partial final line. Opening the log,\n/// or reading, appending or flushing after a writer I/O error, repairs that\n/// suffix before proceeding. A failed repair is retried on the next operation.\n/// Complete records remain intact, including records written before an error\n/// was returned; callers must discover an uncertain transaction's outcome\n/// rather than blindly retry it. Repair scans backwards with an 8 KiB buffer;\n/// successful operations do not rescan. This framing protocol assumes storage\n/// honors flush and does not prove device-sector atomicity after power loss.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct FileTransitionLog {\n    path: PathBuf,\n    file: File,\n    sync_on_append: bool,\n    tail_may_be_torn: bool,\n    _lock: Option<crate::FileLock>,\n}\n\nimpl FileTransitionLog {\n    /// Opens (creating if needed) the log at `path`, discarding a\n    /// trailing entry left half-written by a crash.\n    pub fn open<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<Self, LinkError> {\n        let path = path.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {\n            if !parent.as_os_str().is_empty() && !parent.exists() {\n                std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;\n            }\n        }\n        // The torn tail is trimmed through a dedicated read/write handle:\n        // Windows grants an append-only handle `FILE_APPEND_DATA` without\n        // `FILE_WRITE_DATA`, so `set_len` on it fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`.\n        let repair = OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create(true)\n            .truncate(false)\n            .open(&path)?;\n        truncate_torn_tail(&repair)?;\n        drop(repair);\n        let file = OpenOptions::new().read(true).append(true).open(&path)?;\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        File::open(\n            path.parent()\n                .filter(|p| !p.as_os_str().is_empty())\n                .unwrap_or(Path::new(\".\")),\n        )?\n        .sync_all()?;\n        Ok(Self {\n            path,\n            file,\n            sync_on_append: true,\n            tail_may_be_torn: false,\n            _lock: None,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Holds the conventional sidecar lock until drop. Value types and serialization helpers for the transactions layer.\n//!\n//! Every type here is generic over the doublets address type `T` so the\n//! transactions layer can be reused with `usize`- or `u64`-addressed\n//! stores. The `u32` specialisations ([`DoubletLink`], [`Transition`])\n//! are what the `clink` CLI itself uses.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\n\nuse anyhow::{anyhow, bail, Result};\nuse doublets::data::LinkReference;\n\nuse crate::error::LinkError;\nuse crate::link::GenericLink;\n\n/// The kind of write operation recorded by a [`Transition`].\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub enum TransitionKind {\n    Create,\n    Update,\n    Delete,\n}\n\nimpl TransitionKind {\n    pub fn as_u8(self) -> u8 {\n        match self {\n            TransitionKind::Create => 0,\n            TransitionKind::Update => 1,\n            TransitionKind::Delete => 2,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_u8(value: u8) -> Option<Self> {\n        match value {\n            0 => Some(TransitionKind::Create),\n            1 => Some(TransitionKind::Update),\n            2 => Some(TransitionKind::Delete),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Sync flushes data-store side-effects before `commit` returns.\n///\n/// Async durably persists the transitions then applies the data-store\n/// side-effects on a background-friendly path (already-applied\n/// side-effects are the common case for in-process inner stores).\n///\n/// The Rust port runs both modes synchronously on the calling thread\n/// for predictability; the distinction is preserved for parity with C#\n/// and for future expansion.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub enum CommitMode {\n    #[default]\n    Sync,\n    Async,\n}\n\n/// Retention policy for the transitions log.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub enum LogRetentionPolicy {\n    /// Keep every transition forever (default).\n    #[default]\n    Infinite,\n    /// Drop the oldest completed transitions once the live log exceeds\n    /// `max_transitions`. Optional staged engine\n\nThe existing `LinkStorage` / `NamedTypesDecorator` path remains the cache and\ncompatibility path. It does not gain isolation merely by acquiring a file lock.\nThe optional Rust `engine::Engine`, C# `Engine.LinksEngine<T>`, and JS/TS\n`WasmEngine` keep a session's writes private until commit. Sessions implement\nthe existing raw links and names interfaces. Choose the policies at construction.\nJS runs the Rust implementation through WASM; it does not duplicate the\ntransaction algorithm.\n\n## Choose a configuration\n\n| Scenario | Construction | Acknowledgement and cost |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Disposable cache | Existing bare in-memory links store | No journal, retained snapshots, transaction validation, replica work or disk flush is added. |\n| Isolated volatile state | Staged engine + `MemoryLog` / `MemoryCommitLog` | Atomic publication within one engine, rollback, configurable isolation. Process exit loses it. |\n| Early point-write conflict detection | Select pessimistic admission | Reserve individual written addresses until session end; competing writes fail immediately. [Configuration and costs](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md). |\n| Durable single writer | Staged engine + exclusive file log, require durable flush | One authoritative, checksummed complete revision is appended and flushed before publication. Storage must honor flush; one writer owns the log. |\n| Bounded time travel | Set Rust `HistoryPolicy::Last(n)`, C# `HistoryLimit = n`, JS `history: n` | Retain up to n revisions including current. Active sessions and previously returned snapshots pin their versions independently. |\n| Complete time travel | Rust `HistoryPolicy::All`, C# `HistoryLimit = null`, JS `history: 'all'` | Every replayed/committed revision remains addressable in memory. |\n| Independent branch | Rust `Engine::fork`, C# `LinksEngine.Fork`, JS `WasmEngine.fork` | Seed and flush a separate journal; edit privately and merge committed changes atomically into the parent. |\n| Asynchronous copies | Wrap a log with replicated log, async policy | Commit waits for primary only. Call synchronize under the engine's log mutex to catch up followers. A primary loss can lose uncopied commits. |\n| Synchronous copies | Replicated log, acknowledgements k including primary | Commit waits for primary and enough successful follower flushes. Failure can leave a committed primary or partial set of copies; outcome discovery is mandatory. |\n| Serializable independent point edits | Select `SerializableValidation::ReadSet` / `SerializableValidation.ReadSet` / `serializableValidation: 'read-set'` | Track observed addresses and validate concurrent changes at commit; scans still check the whole revision. [Recipe and costs](ENGINE-VALIDATION.md). |\n| Localized journal edits | Optional `DeltaLog` / `DeltaCommitLog` around the selected log | Store a checksummed changed span between periodic full checkpoints; engine cloning and replay remain O(N). See [format, composition and examples](ENGINE-DELTA.md). |\n\n`supports_durable_flush` / `SupportsDurableFlush` / `supportsDurableFlush` is\nan adapter contract. Memory logs declare false. An unknown adapter defaults to\nfalse in Rust; explicit durability requirements reject it. A durable external\nadapter must actually flush its storage before returning. Replicated durability\nrequires durable primary and, conservatively, every eligible follower when\nmore than one acknowledgement is requested. A copy count alone says nothing\nabout independent failure domains, fencing, power-loss protection, or elections.\n\n## Concurrency and isolation\n\nOptimistic admission permits multiple sessions. Validation and publication use\none engine mutex, so two commits cannot validate the same state concurrently.\nExclusive admission fails immediately when another session is active; rollback,\ndrop/dispose, and completed attempts release admission. A session belongs to\none caller; share engine handles between threads instead of sharing a session.\n\nOptional [pessimistic point writes](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md) reserve written addresses\nand reject competing writes before staging. Independent addresses remain concurrent;\nisolation and serializable validation remain separately selected. Cluster engines\nreject this local-only strategy.\n\n| Isolation | Reads | Conflict checks |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Read committed | Each operation sees current committed state plus its own writes | A written address changed after begin aborts. Reads can change and scans can gain rows. |\n| Snapshot | Begin-time immutable state plus own writes | Same write/write check. Disjoint write skew is allowed. |\n| Serializable, revision validation (default) | Begin-time immutable state plus own writes | Any intervening database revision aborts the session, including scans and read-only commits. This conservative check prevents predicate anomalies but can abort unrelated work. |\n\nOptional serializable read-set validation accepts disjoint point reads/writes while\nchecking their observed addresses, including missing rows. Scans and name searches\nstill check the whole revision. It requires serializable isolation; default\nrevision validation is unchanged. See [configuration and tradeoffs](ENGINE-VALIDATION.md).\n\nThere are no dirty reads or dirty writes between sessions of the same engine.\nThese properties do not apply to independent writers or direct mutation of an\nadapter behind the engine. Retry conflicts with a **new** session. A failed\ncommit attempt closes its session and discards its staged writes. Allocations\ncan leave gaps after rollback. An optional references, unique pairs or unique\nnames constraint validates the whole proposed state at commit. Raw mutation\nnever silently merges duplicate pairs or cascades deletes: select an existing\nusages/uniqueness decorator if that policy is wanted. Legacy CLI backends retain\ntheir established merge and cascading behavior.\n\n## Commit, recovery and errors\n\nA write commit encodes the complete next revision, appends its record, flushes\nthe log, then publishes the immutable state. The log is authoritative; there\nis no separately acknowledged data checkpoint. This avoids mixed mapped data\nand journal visibility. Full revision records are deliberately simple, not a\nspace-efficient WAL implementation. The optional [delta journal](ENGINE-DELTA.md)\ncompresses physical records without changing this logical commit boundary.\n\nAn append or flush error is an **indeterminate commit**: data may have reached\nthe log even if the caller got an error. The engine then rejects further\nwrites and engine snapshots. Close/reopen using the same authoritative log to\ndiscover the outcome. Do not blindly retry an uncertain business operation;\nuse an application idempotency key or inspect recovered state first. JS reports\n`LinksError.outcome === 'unknown'`; validation conflicts are `failed`.\nReplication does not change these rules. Followers can contain an unacknowledged\ncommit and must not be promoted automatically.\n\nThe exclusive file adapters discard an incomplete final line on open and before\nread, append or flush after a writer I/O error. Failed repair keeps further\noperations fenced until repair succeeds. Complete records remain intact, even\nwhen an error followed their write; this does not authorize retrying an uncertain\nbusiness operation. A repair scans backwards with an 8 KiB buffer. Successful\noperations only check a flag, with no rescan. C# disables its managed write\nbuffer so failed buffered bytes cannot reappear during repair; append therefore\nperforms a file write immediately. These costs belong to the selected file log.\nComplete corrupt records are rejected. Recovery checks checksum, UTF-8 names,\naddress bounds, unique addresses, contiguous revisions, nondecreasing allocator\nand selected constraints.\nChecksums detect accidental corruption, not malicious tampering. Establish the\ndatabase directory and protect its metadata before depending on power-loss\nrecovery. Filesystem/device failure outside the adapter's flush contract is not\nproven by ordinary process crash tests.\n\nThe legacy transaction decorators have a different architecture: their commit\nmarker is flushed before acknowledging commit, data is flushed before an applied\nmarker, and replay errors propagate. They still mutate the underlying store\nwhile a transaction is open; use the staged engine for session isolation.\nTheir legacy row journal does not undo or version ordinary named writes; staged\nsessions include names in atomic revisions. Named-write admission fences do not\nadd names to that legacy journal.\nSized and chunked retention discard completed rollback records without replaying\ntheir writes. Chunk archives contain committed changes only; pending records\nremain in the live log. Live C# retention checkpoints current inline effects\nwhen an older committed record lacks an applied marker, preserving newer edits.\nRetention limits the in-memory list, while the durable\nsidecar still keeps recovery markers. Optional diagnostic I/O failures preserve\nthe operation's outcome; storage and journal errors retain their error semantics.\n\nLegacy Rust transaction IDs exclude every recovered commit and abort decision,\neven if the wall clock repeats after a process restart. Explicit and automatic\nowners use the same allocation check. It uses the existing decision hash sets:\n\nThe staged implementation clones the current rows for each write commit and\nwrites a complete logical revision: O(N + W) memory/work plus O(N) journal bytes for N\nrows and W staged writes. A scan currently materializes its view. History adds\nup to O(HN) retained row memory. The allocator is shared. Optimistic read-committed\nand snapshot sessions, plus serializable read-set sessions, track per-address changes only while another session can\nbe stale, retaining deleted-address tombstones to detect delete/recreate races.\nThe final session validates before reclaiming that map. Opening an engine,\nexclusive admission and optimistic whole-revision serializable validation do not build\nper-row generations. A continuously overlapping set of sessions can still retain\nmany changed addresses; end sessions promptly. Pessimistic admission additionally\ntracks reserved write addresses and generations under all isolation levels; its\n[separate cost description](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md) explains ownership and cleanup.\nRecovery reads the full log; retention bounds in-memory history, not log size.\nOptional single-span delta encoding reduces physical bytes for localized changes\nand adds an O(N) comparison; it does not compact history or remove full-state work.\nReplication catch-up compares prefixes and copies missing complete revisions.\nThere is no background compaction or group commit. These limits matter for a\nlarge or frequently written database.\n\n| Competitor configuration | Closest available configuration | Material difference |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| SQLite WAL with synchronous commit | Exclusive file log + staged engine, serializable | Full-state records instead of page WAL, conservative validation, no SQLite locking/checkpoint implementation or performance equivalence. |\n| PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED / REPEATABLE READ | Read committed / snapshot | Similar visibility choices; no SQL planner, row locks or PostgreSQL vacuum. |\n| PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE | Serializable revision/read-set validation | Whole-revision scans or point dependencies replace SSI dependency tracking; unrelated predicates can still conflict. |\n| FoundationDB conflict sets | Serializable read-set validation | Local address sets and whole-revision scans; no range index, distributed resolver, snapshot-read bypass or FoundationDB protocol. |\n| RocksDB optimistic transactions | Optimistic admission + snapshot/serializable | No LSM tree, key-range locks, parallel validation, compaction or RocksDB performance parity. |\n| RocksDB pessimistic transactions | Pessimistic point writes + selected isolation | Immediate busy errors, engine-local ownership and snapshot validation; no waiting, deadlock detector, range locks, LSM tree or performance equivalence. |\n| InnoDB synchronous redo/group commit | Durable staged journal with explicit flush | No group commit, page WAL, buffer pool or doublewrite repair. [2026-10-25T11:26:58.781Z] [STDERR] *** Add File: /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1792924568628/docs/ENGINE-GROUP-COMMIT.md
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.783Z] [STDERR] +# Independent sessions with one durability flush
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.786Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.788Z] [STDERR] +`Engine::commit_group`, `LinksEngine.CommitGroup` and `WasmEngine.commitGroup`
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.790Z] [STDERR] +are opt-in operations on existing staged sessions. The caller chooses a bounded
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.791Z] [STDERR] +group. No worker, queue, timer or grouping delay is added to ordinary commits or
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.797Z] [STDERR] +bare stores. This supplies the independent-session flush sharing described in
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.804Z] [STDERR] +the [InnoDB source study](case-studies/issue-138/RESEARCH.md); it does not supply
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.807Z] [STDERR] +InnoDB's page WAL, doublewrite repair or performance characteristics.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.810Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.812Z] [STDERR] +The coordinator holds the engine gate, validates each member in input order
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.814Z] [STDERR] +against private tentative state, appends each accepted write's separate revision,
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.816Z] [STDERR] +and flushes once. Only then does it publish the resulting state and history.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.818Z] [STDERR] +Unchanged read-only sessions need no record; empty and entirely aborted groups
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.820Z] [STDERR] +do no log I/O. Every member retains the selected isolation, constraints, conflict
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.821Z] [STDERR] +generations and point ownership rules. Whole-revision serializable validation
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.822Z] [STDERR] +can abort overlapping members even when their writes are disjoint. Select
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.824Z] [STDERR] +snapshot isolation or serializable point-read validation when appropriate.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.826Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.827Z] [STDERR] +```javascript
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.829Z] [STDERR] +const first = engine.begin(), second = engine.begin();
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.831Z] [STDERR] +const a = await first.create(0n, 0n);
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.832Z] [STDERR] +await second.create(a.index, 0n);
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.837Z] [STDERR] +const outcomes = await engine.commitGroup([first, second]);
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.840Z] [STDERR] +// Under snapshot isolation: two committed revisions, one adapter flush.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.843Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.844Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.846Z] [STDERR] +Results follow input order. `Committed(revision)` / status `committed` is an
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.848Z] [STDERR] +acknowledgement after the shared flush. `Aborted(error)` / `aborted` is a known
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.850Z] [STDERR] +validation failure before that member appends. Later valid members can still
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.851Z] [STDERR] +commit and aborted members do not consume revision numbers. Allocation can leave
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.853Z] [STDERR] +address gaps, as with individual rollback.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.855Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.857Z] [STDERR] +An append or flush error returns `Indeterminate(error)` / `indeterminate` for
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.860Z] [STDERR] +**every provisionally accepted member**, including read-only members. Known
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.866Z] [STDERR] +aborts remain aborted. The coordinator retains the old visible state, closes
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.869Z] [STDERR] +the group members and fences the engine. Reopen its authoritative log to discover
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.876Z] [STDERR] +the valid persisted prefix before retrying business operations. The group is
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.879Z] [STDERR] +not an atomic transaction: after an error or crash, zero, some or all accepted
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.881Z] [STDERR] +revisions may exist. An error does not undo a completed append. Retained snapshots
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.890Z] [STDERR] +and outside read-committed sessions never expose private tentative revisions.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.892Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.893Z] [STDERR] +Rust consumes a vector of sessions. A foreign member causes an outer error
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.895Z] [STDERR] +before I/O; dropping the consumed vector rolls back its open members. C# and JS
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.897Z] [STDERR] +reject null, duplicate, foreign or invalid arguments before consuming any member.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.899Z] [STDERR] +Already closed C# or Rust members yield known aborts. JS requires open transport
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.901Z] [STDERR] +handles, reserves them synchronously, drains requests/controls already queued,
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.903Z] [STDERR] +and transfers ownership to the native group. Later requests and controls reject
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.905Z] [STDERR] +with `outcome: 'not-sent'`. `close()` waits for the transfer and never frees a
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.907Z] [STDERR] +consumed native handle twice. The group owns an engine clone, so closing the
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.909Z] [STDERR] +engine wrapper while queues drain cannot invalidate it. Freeing an uncommitted
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.911Z] [STDERR] +native group rolls back its members. Group results are values, rather than a
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.913Z] [STDERR] +single `LinksError`, because different members may have different outcomes.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.914Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.916Z] [STDERR] +## Durable and replicated construction
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.918Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.919Z] [STDERR] +Rust's `FileTransitionLog` defaults to syncing on append. Set
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.920Z] [STDERR] +`set_sync_on_append(false)` **before** wrapping/opening it to amortize sync calls;
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.922Z] [STDERR] +the group still performs a durable `flush_log` before acknowledging. C# and JS
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.923Z] [STDERR] +file commit logs already separate append from durable flush. Set
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.924Z] [STDERR] +`require_durable_flush` / `RequireDurableFlush` / `requireDurableFlush` when
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.926Z] [STDERR] +durability is required. Memory adapters remain volatile.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.928Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.929Z] [STDERR] +Optional delta encoding composes outside the selected file/replicated log.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.931Z] [STDERR] +Each independent revision remains decodable; a delta references its preceding
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.932Z] [STDERR] +revision. Fixed-primary synchronous replication flushes the primary once, copies
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.934Z] [STDERR] +the complete missing prefix and flushes each follower once before counting it.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.937Z] [STDERR] +Explicit catch-up still flushes the primary before reading its prefix. Replica
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.939Z] [STDERR] +acknowledgements retain their existing unknown-outcome and membership semantics.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.941Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.944Z] [STDERR] +Runnable durable examples, each with optional `--delta`:
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.946Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.948Z] [STDERR] +- Rust: `cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_group_commit -- /tmp/group-rust.log`
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.950Z] [STDERR] +- C#: `dotnet run --project examples/group-commit-csharp -- /tmp/group-csharp.log`
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.953Z] [STDERR] +- JS: `CLINK_WASM=/path/to/web-package node js/client/examples/engine-group-commit.mjs /tmp/group-js.log`
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.956Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.960Z] [STDERR] +The native examples and JS example use the same portable journal format. Use
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.963Z] [STDERR] +separate paths for independent databases. One writer owns each file; close all
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.967Z] [STDERR] +handles before another implementation opens the same journal.
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.971Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.974Z] [STDERR] +## Costs and verification
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.983Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.986Z] [STDERR] +For K accepted writes, preparation still clones/validates/encodes each full
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.991Z] [STDERR] +revision: O(sum(N_i + W_i)) work plus existing ordered-map costs and encoded name
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.995Z] [STDERR] +bytes. It copies retained history and conflict/ownership metadata, and buffers
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.996Z] [STDERR] +the K logical records until publication. C# also pins each accepted member's
[2026-10-25T11:26:58.998Z] [STDERR] +snapshot so its closed handle retains ordinary committed-read behavior. The
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.003Z] [STDERR] +extra memory therefore includes full encoded revisions and retained snapshots,
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.006Z] [STDERR] +not just K small queue entries. Use bounded groups; there is one serialization
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.007Z] [STDERR] +gate through preparation, append, flush and publication. This reduces flush
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.008Z] [STDERR] +calls; it does not remove full-state CPU work, implement parallel validation,
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.011Z] [STDERR] +compact journals, or promise a throughput multiplier.
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.012Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.014Z] [STDERR] +Portable contracts cover separate revisions, constraints, conflicts, read
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.016Z] [STDERR] +dependencies, history, admission and uncertain prefixes. Native tests exercise
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.017Z] [STDERR] +real exclusive files, delta journals, two durable replicas, following commits
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.019Z] [STDERR] +and a bounded blocked flush. Actual-WASM tests inject synchronous JS journal
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.021Z] [STDERR] +faults; Node/Bun/Deno conformance exercises real wasm-bindgen handle transfer and
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.022Z] [STDERR] +queued requests. Finite fault images test the declared journal contract rather
[2026-10-25T11:26:59.023Z] [STDERR] +than claiming physical device power-loss coverage.

Preserve nested fork cutoffs, per-branch heads and\nroot-to-leaf replay order, including empty histories and subsequent edits.\n# @link-foundation/link-cli-client\n\nA small JavaScript/TypeScript client for link-cli links stores. It offers one\ncontract over several backends:\n\n| Backend | Entry point | Runtimes | Reaches |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| TCP | `@link-foundation/link-cli-client/tcp` | Node.js, Bun, Deno | a running `clink --serve` (Rust or C#) |\n| CLI process | `@link-foundation/link-cli-client/process` | Node.js, Bun, Deno | a `clink --serve` the client starts and stops |\n| WebAssembly | `@link-foundation/link-cli-client` | browsers, Node.js, Bun, Deno | an in-process `Clink` store from `rust/wasm` |\n\nIt is the JS counterpart of `RemoteLinks` in the other ports (C#\n`INamedTypesLinks<uint>`, Rust `NamedTypeLinks`). Code written against\n`LinksClient` works the same whether the store is local (WebAssembly) or\nremote (TCP), and `LinksDecorator` wraps any of them, so you can swap one for\nthe other.\n\nThe package has no runtime dependencies. The main entry point imports nothing\nfrom `node:`, and nothing here needs React or a browser.\n\n## Use\n\n```js\nimport { connectTcp } from '@link-foundation/link-cli-client/tcp';\n\nconst links = await connectTcp('127.0.0.1:7878', { timeout: 5000 });\ntry {\n  const link = await links.create(1n, 1n);       // { index, source, target } as BigInt\n  await links.setName(link.index, 'Hà Nội');\n  console.log(await links.getByName('Hà Nội'));  // link.index\n  console.log(await links.count(['*', link.index])); // links whose target is link.index\n} finally {\n  await links.close();                           // closes only this connection\n}\n```\n\nStart and own a server process (the executable and its arguments go to argv\nas separate entries, with no shell, so paths with spaces need no quoting):\n\n```js\nimport { connectProcess } from '@link-foundation/link-cli-client/process';\n\nawait using links = await connectProcess({\n  command: '/opt/link cli/clink',     // or command: 'dotnet', args: ['clink.dll']\n  db: '/data/my links/db.links',\n  capabilities: { duplicateLinks: true }, // what you know about this server\n});\n// leaving the scope closes the connection, then stops this server process\n```\n\nUse the in-process WebAssembly store (browser or server). Build `rust/wasm`\n(`clink-wasm` 2.4.0 or later, which has `Clink.request`) with\n`wasm-pack build --target web`:\n\n```js\nimport init, { Clink } from './pkg/clink_wasm.js';\nimport { createWasmClient } from '@link-foundation/link-cli-client';\n\nawait init();\nconst links = createWasmClient(new Clink(), { owned: true }); // close() frees it\n```\n\n## Contract\n\nEvery method resolves to plain data and takes `{ signal, deadline, timeout }`\nas its last argument:\n\n| Method | Resolves to |\n| --- | --- |\n| `count(restriction?)` | `bigint` |\n| `each(restriction?)` | `{ index, source, target }[]` in address order |\n| `create(source, target)` | the created link, or `null` when the backend merged it into an equal link |\n| `update(index, source, target)` / `delete(index)` | the net change of every link touched, `{ before, after }[]` |\n| `getName(index)` / `getByName(name)` | `string \\| null` / `bigint \\| null` |\n| `setName(index, name)` / `removeName(index)` | the address the backend answers / nothing |\n| `query(text)` | changes of a LiNo substitution query, references as the backend wrote them |\n| `exportLinks()` | every link, with names in place of named references |\n| `batch(operations, { window })` | per operation `ok`, `failed`, `unknown` or `not-sent`, and `completed` |\n| `requestText(text)` / `request(document)` | raw protocol access |\n| `require(...guarantees)` | throws `UnsupportedError` unless the backend offers them all |\n| `close()` / `[Symbol.asyncDispose]()` | releases what this client owns |\n\nA restriction is `[]` (every link), `[index]`, `[index, source, target]` or\n`[source, target]`; `'*'` (`ANY`) matches anything.\n\n**Addresses** are `bigint` going out and coming back. Safe-integer numbers are\naccepted as input. Anything a `number` cannot hold exactly, or the backend\ncannot store, is refused before sending with `AddressRangeError`. The servers\nand the WebAssembly store use `u32` addresses (`capabilities.maxAddress` is\n2^32 - 1). The client itself is not limited to 32 bits: the unit tests drive a\n64-bit backend with addresses above 2^53.\n\n**Errors** are `LinksError` subclasses. Each carries `outcome`, which tells\nyou what you can know about the request:\n\n- `not-sent`: the request never left the client (abort or deadline before\n  sending, a limit, an address out of range, a closed connection, a missing\n  capability).\n- `failed`: the backend answered `(error: ...)` (`RemoteError`). Nothing\n  changed.\n- `unknown`: the request was sent but its answer is lost (abort or deadline\n  while in flight, a lost connection, an oversized reply). Read the store\n  back before retrying.\n\nOther subclasses: `ProtocolMismatchError` (the peer is not a links server, or\nit refuses the text protocol), `MalformedMessageError`, `LimitExceededError`,\n`ConnectionClosedError`, `AbortError` and `DeadlineExceededError`.\n\n**Cancellation.** `signal` is an `AbortSignal`. `deadline` is absolute (a\n`Date` or epoch milliseconds), and `timeout` becomes `Date.now() + timeout`;\n//! Opt-in coordination of independent sessions at one durability boundary.\nuse super::{error, Engine, EngineTransaction, MemoryLog, State};\nuse crate::{LinkError, TransitionLogStore};\nuse doublets::data::LinkReference;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\n/// One independent session's result, in the caller's input order.\npub enum GroupCommitOutcome {\n    /// Acknowledged after the shared flush (or no journal I/O was necessary).\n    Committed(u64),\n    /// Validation failed before this session appended any physical record.\n    Aborted(String),\n    /// No acknowledgement: reopening must discover which prefix persisted.\n    Indeterminate(String),\n}\n\nimpl<T: LinkReference, L: TransitionLogStore> Engine<T, L> {\n    /// Consume independent sessions and share one flush across accepted writes.\n    /// Validation follows input order and retains the configured isolation rules.\n    /// Each write session retains its own revision; this is not an atomic batch.\n    /// An uncertain append/flush fences the engine and retains its old visible\n    /// state. All provisionally accepted members then return `Indeterminate`,\n    /// including read-only members that may depend on a tentative revision.\n    ///\n    /// Foreign sessions cause an outer error before I/O; consumed sessions are\n    /// rolled back on that path. A log that syncs on every append still performs\n    /// those syncs; select buffered append with durable flush to amortize them.\n    /// Private preparation retains history/map metadata and full accepted\n    /// revision records until publication. Ordinary commits keep their own path.\n    pub fn commit_group(\n        &self,\n        mut sessions: Vec<EngineTransaction<T, L>>,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<GroupCommitOutcome>, LinkError> {\n        if sessions\n            .iter()\n            .any(|tx| !Arc::ptr_eq(&self.state, &tx.engine.state))\n        {\n            return Err(error(\"group sessions must belong to the same engine\"));\n        }\n        let mut state = self.lock()?;\n        let mut options = state.options.clone();\n        options.trace = false;\n        let mut working = State {\n            log: MemoryLog::default(),\n            current: state.current.clone(),\n            history: state.history.clone(),\n            changed: state.changed.clone(),\n            write_owners: state.write_owners.clone(),\n            next: state.next,\n            committed_next: state.committed_next,\n            active: state.active,\n            poisoned: false,\n            options,\n        };\n        let mut outcomes = Vec::with_capacity(sessions.len());\n        for tx in &mut sessions {\n            let base = tx.base.clone();\n            let outcome = match tx.commit_locked(&mut working) {\n                Ok(revision) => GroupCommitOutcome::Committed(revision),\n                Err(cause) => GroupCommitOutcome::Aborted(cause.to_string()),\n            };\n            tx.base = base;\n            outcomes.push(outcome);\n        }\n        // Only ownership/admission cleanup is real until durability succeeds.\n        // Read-committed sessions outside this group must retain the old view\n        // if the physical log fails after writing an unknown prefix.\n        state.active = working.active;\n        state.write_owners = working.write_owners;\n        let persisted = (|| {\n            for record in &working.log.entries {\n                state.log.append_log_entry(record)?;\n            }\n            if !working.log.entries.is_empty() {\n                state.log.flush_log()?;\n            }\n            Ok::<(), LinkError>(())\n        })();\n        if let Err(cause) = persisted {\n            state.poisoned = true;\n            if state.active == 0 {\n                state.changed.clear();\n            }\n            let message = format!(\"indeterminate group commit: {cause}; reopen the engine\");\n            for outcome in &mut outcomes {\n                if matches!(outcome, GroupCommitOutcome::Committed(_)) {\n                    *outcome = GroupCommitOutcome::Indeterminate(message.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            return Ok(outcomes);\n        }\n        state.current = working.current;\n        state.history = working.history;\n        state.changed = working.changed;\n        state.committed_next = working.committed_next;\n        if state.options.trace && !working.log.entries.is_empty() {\n            crate::diagnostics::stderr!(\n                \"[Engine] group committed revision={} records={}\",\n                state.current.revision,\n                working.log.entries.len()\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(outcomes)\n    }\n}\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

[2026-10-25T11:28:18.085Z] [STDERR] ### Optional isolated engine
[2026-10-25T11:28:18.086Z] [STDERR] `WasmEngine` wraps the compiled Rust staged engine with the same asynchronous
[2026-10-25T11:28:18.095Z] [STDERR] links methods on each session. Create a session with `engine.begin()`, issue
[2026-10-25T11:28:18.098Z] [STDERR] several requests, then `await session.commit()` or `await session.rollback()`.
[2026-10-25T11:28:18.104Z] [STDERR] Closing an uncommitted session rolls it back. Commit shares the request queue,
[2026-10-25T11:28:18.107Z] [STDERR] so it cannot overtake an earlier write. Defaults are optimistic admission,

The caller chooses a bounded\ngroup. No worker, queue, timer or grouping delay is added to ordinary commits or\nbare stores. This supplies the independent-session flush sharing described in\nthe [InnoDB source study](case-studies/issue-138/RESEARCH.md); it does not supply\nInnoDB's page WAL, doublewrite repair or performance characteristics.\n\nThe coordinator holds the engine gate, validates each member in input order\nagainst private tentative state, appends each accepted write's separate revision,\nand flushes once. Only then does it publish the resulting state and history.\nUnchanged read-only sessions need no record; empty and entirely aborted groups\ndo no log I/O. Every member retains the selected isolation, constraints, conflict\ngenerations and point ownership rules. Whole-revision serializable validation\ncan abort overlapping members even when their writes are disjoint. Select\nsnapshot isolation or serializable point-read validation when appropriate.\n\n```javascript\nconst first = engine.begin(), second = engine.begin();\nconst a = await first.create(0n, 0n);\nawait second.create(a.index, 0n);\nconst outcomes = await engine.commitGroup([first, second]);\n// Under snapshot isolation: two committed revisions, one adapter flush.\n```\n\nResults follow input order. `Committed(revision)` / status `committed` is an\nacknowledgement after the shared flush. `Aborted(error)` / `aborted` is a known\nvalidation failure before that member appends. Later valid members can still\ncommit and aborted members do not consume revision numbers. Allocation can leave\naddress gaps, as with individual rollback.\n\nAn append or flush error returns `Indeterminate(error)` / `indeterminate` for\n**every provisionally accepted member**, including read-only members. Known\naborts remain aborted. The coordinator retains the old visible state, closes\nthe group members and fences the engine. Reopen its authoritative log to discover\nthe valid persisted prefix before retrying business operations. The group is\nnot an atomic transaction: after an error or crash, zero, some or all accepted\nrevisions may exist. An error does not undo a completed append. Retained snapshots\nand outside read-committed sessions never expose private tentative revisions.\n\nRust consumes a vector of sessions. A foreign member causes an outer error\nbefore I/O; dropping the consumed vector rolls back its open members. C# and JS\nreject null, duplicate, foreign or invalid arguments before consuming any member.\nAlready closed C# or Rust members yield known aborts. JS requires open transport\nhandles, reserves them synchronously, drains requests/controls already queued,\nand transfers ownership to the native group. Later requests and controls reject\nwith `outcome: 'not-sent'`. `close()` waits for the transfer and never frees a\nconsumed native handle twice. The group owns an engine clone, so closing the\nengine wrapper while queues drain cannot invalidate it. Freeing an uncommitted\nnative group rolls back its members. Group results are values, rather than a\nsingle `LinksError`, because different members may have different outcomes.\n\n## Durable and replicated construction\n\nRust's `FileTransitionLog` defaults to syncing on append. Memory adapters remain volatile.\n\nOptional delta encoding composes outside the selected file/replicated log.\nEach independent revision remains decodable; a delta references its preceding\nrevision. Fixed-primary synchronous replication flushes the primary once, copies\nthe complete missing prefix and flushes each follower once before counting it.\nExplicit catch-up still flushes the primary before reading its prefix. Replica\nacknowledgements retain their existing unknown-outcome and membership semantics.\n\nRunnable durable examples, each with optional `--delta`:\n\n- Rust: `cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_group_commit -- /tmp/group-rust.log`\n- C#: `dotnet run --project examples/group-commit-csharp -- /tmp/group-csharp.log`\n- JS: `CLINK_WASM=/path/to/web-package node js/client/examples/engine-group-commit.mjs /tmp/group-js.log`\n\nThe native examples and JS example use the same portable journal format. One writer owns each file; close all\nhandles before another implementation opens the same journal.\n\n## Costs and verification\n\nFor K accepted writes, preparation still clones/validates/encodes each full\nrevision: O(sum(N_i + W_i)) work plus existing ordered-map costs and encoded name\nbytes. It copies retained history and conflict/ownership metadata, and buffers\nthe K logical records until publication. C# also pins each accepted member's\nsnapshot so its closed handle retains ordinary committed-read behavior. The\nextra memory therefore includes full encoded revisions and retained snapshots,\nnot just K small queue entries. Storage abstraction shared by every links backend.\n//!\n//! [`LinksStorage`] is the trait the transactions layer is written\n//! against, so any doublets-compatible store — the CLI's own\n//! [`LinkStorage`](crate::LinkStorage), a file-mapped\n//! [`DoubletsStorage`](super::DoubletsStorage), or an externally owned\n//! `doublets::unit::Store` wrapped with\n//! The trait is generic over the doublets address type `T`, so external\n//! consumers using `usize`-addressed stores are first-class.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\nuse doublets::data::LinkReference;\n\nuse crate::error::LinkError;\nuse crate::link::GenericLink;\n\n/// Cheap fingerprint of a database file, used to answer\n/// \"has anyone else written since I last looked?\" without reparsing.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub struct StorageRevision {\n    /// Size of the database file in bytes (0 when it does not exist).\n    pub len: u64,\n    /// Last modification time in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.\n    pub modified_nanos: u128,\n}\n\nimpl StorageRevision {\n    /// Reads the current revision of `path`.\n    ///\n    /// A missing file is reported as [`StorageRevision::default`] rather\n    /// than an error, so callers can fingerprint a database before it\n    /// has been created.\n    pub fn of<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<Self, LinkError> {\n        let metadata = match fs::metadata(path.as_ref()) {\n            Ok(metadata) => metadata,\n            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n                return Ok(Self::default())\n            }\n            Err(error) => return Err(LinkError::Io(error)),\n        };\n        let modified_nanos = metadata\n            .modified()\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|time| time.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).ok())\n            .map(|duration| duration.as_nanos())\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n        Ok(Self {\n            len: metadata.len(),\n            modified_nanos,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// A store of links addressed by `T`, expressed in terms of owned\n/// [`GenericLink<T>`] values so that both in-memory maps and\n/// memory-mapped doublets stores can implement it.\npub trait LinksStorage<T: LinkReference> {\n    /// Creates a link and returns its address. Transactions need these callbacks to distinguish a new\n    /// allocation from a duplicate resolved into an existing link.\n    ///\n    /// The default is for backends that create one row atomically. Backends\n    /// with cascades or partial writes must override it with their callbacks,\n    /// as for [`Self::update_link_observed`].\n    fn create_link_observed(\n        &mut self,\n        source: T,\n        target: T,\n        observer: &mut dyn FnMut(GenericLink<T>, GenericLink<T>),\n    ) -> Result<T, LinkError> {\n        let index = self.create_link(source, target)?;\n        let after = self\n            .get_link(index)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| GenericLink::new(index, source, target));\n        observer(GenericLink::null(), after);\n        Ok(index)\n    }\n\n    /// Ensures a link exists at `index`, creating placeholders as needed.\n    fn ensure_link_created(&mut self, index: T) -> Result<T, LinkError>;\n\n    /// [`Self::ensure_link_created`], reporting every placeholder it creates.\n    ///\n    /// Backends differ in whether intermediate addresses remain allocated.\n    /// This default compares rows before/after the operation, including partial\n    /// changes on error, so a transaction can undo either backend's behavior.\n    /// It costs O(N log N) time and O(N) rows; backends may override it with\n    /// allocation callbacks. The built-in map adapters avoid this copy.\n    fn ensure_link_created_observed(\n        &mut self,\n        index: T,\n        observer: &mut dyn FnMut(GenericLink<T>, GenericLink<T>),\n    ) -> Result<T, LinkError> {\n        let before: std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _> = self\n            .all_links()\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|row| (row.index, row))\n            .collect();\n        let outcome = self.ensure_link_created(index);\n        let mut after: std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _> = self\n            .all_links()\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|row| (row.index, row))\n            .collect();\n        for (id, previous) in before {\n            let next = after.remove(&id).unwrap_or_else(GenericLink::null);\n            if previous != next {\n                observer(previous, next);\n            }\n        }\n        for (_, row) in after {\n            observer(GenericLink::null(), row);\n        }\n        outcome\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the link stored at `index`, if any.\n    fn get_link(&self, index: T) -> Option<GenericLink<T>>;\n\n    /// Returns `true` when a link exists at `index`.\n    fn link_exists(&self, index: T) -> bool {\n        self.get_link(index).is_some()\n    }\n\n    /// Repoints `index` at `source`/`target`, returning the previous state.\n    fn update_link(&mut self, index: T, source: T, target: T) -> Result<GenericLink<T>, LinkError>;\n\n    /// Deletes `index`, returning the link that was removed.\n    fn delete_link(&mut self, index: T) -> Result<GenericLink<T>, LinkError>;\n\n    /// [`Self::update_link`], reporting every `(before, after)` change it made.\n    ///\n    /// A store that resolves duplicate doublets turns one write into a cascade\n    /// of changes, and the transactions layer has to log each of them or a\n    /// rollback cannot restore what the write actually did. This is the\n    /// equivalent of the `WriteHandler` the C# decorators forward to.\n    ///\n    /// The default implementation reports the single change a store without any\n    /// policy of its own makes, so implementors only override it when they\n    /// really can cascade.\n    fn update_link_observed(\n//! Optional transactions layer for the Rust link-cli.\n//!\n//! Mirrors the C# `TransactionsDecorator` in\n//! `csharp/Foundation.Data.Doublets.Cli.Library/TransactionsDecorator.cs`.\n//!\n//! The decorator records every `create` / `update` / `delete` as a\n//! reversible [`GenericTransition`] in a sidecar log. Recovery\n//! replays committed-but-unapplied transitions and undoes logged uncommitted\n//! changes, reporting replay and flush failures.\n//!\n//! [2026-10-25T12:51:42.078Z] [STDERR] +

[2026-10-25T12:51:42.112Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.115Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.117Z] [STDERR] +The first seven fields retain the row codec's meanings, with `v2` as the
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.119Z] [STDERR] +version. Mode `n` means names only, requiring an update and empty rows. Mode
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.121Z] [STDERR] +`r` replays a row and its associated name state. Name changes are sorted by

[2026-10-25T12:51:42.132Z] [STDERR] +so delimiters, NULs, newlines and Unicode never change record boundaries.

[2026-10-25T12:51:42.139Z] [STDERR] +unpaired UTF-16 string domain; Rust rejects those values before replay.

[2026-10-25T12:51:42.143Z] [STDERR] +

[2026-10-25T12:51:42.148Z] [STDERR] +reject v2 transaction payloads; upgrade readers before writing named history.
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.151Z] [STDERR] +Existing v1 records contain no historical names, which cannot be reconstructed.
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.153Z] [STDERR] +Chunk archives and movement intents preserve complete v2 records. Recovery
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.155Z] [STDERR] +validates all recognized records before replacing live history or changing
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.157Z] [STDERR] +rows or names, including conflicting payloads at the same sequence.

[2026-10-25T12:51:42.163Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.167Z] [STDERR] +Explicit name writes append and flush their complete undo record before

[2026-10-25T12:51:42.180Z] [STDERR] +the complete payload. Fault images and actual finite process exits test these
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.183Z] [STDERR] +boundaries. Filesystem flush contracts remain dependent on the configured
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.188Z] [STDERR] +adapter and hardware. The existing row mutation before its observer-journal
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.191Z] [STDERR] +append remains an unfinished crash window; name journaling does not resolve it.
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.196Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.197Z] [STDERR] +The selected transaction wrapper scans and decodes the named sidecar before
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.200Z] [STDERR] +each row or name operation to capture names of absent rows and cascade victims.
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.202Z] [STDERR] +Cost is O(sidecar rows plus decoded name bytes); name edits also clone the
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.203Z] [STDERR] +logical map, retain changed strings and add a pre-effect journal flush.
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.204Z] [STDERR] +Complete history snapshots copy retained name payloads. Row-only records use

[2026-10-25T12:51:42.210Z] [STDERR] +records before replaying their rows.
[2026-10-25T12:51:42.211Z] [STDERR] +

The trait is generic over the doublets address type `T`, so external\n//! consumers using `usize`-addressed stores are first-class.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\nuse doublets::data::LinkReference;\n\nuse crate::error::LinkError;\nuse crate::link::GenericLink;\n\n/// Cheap fingerprint of a database file, used to answer\n/// \"has anyone else written since I last looked?\" without reparsing.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]\npub struct StorageRevision {\n    /// Size of the database file in bytes (0 when it does not exist).\n    pub len: u64,\n    /// Last modification time in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.\n    pub modified_nanos: u128,\n}\n\nimpl StorageRevision {\n    /// Reads the current revision of `path`.\n    ///\n    /// A missing file is reported as [`StorageRevision::default`] rather\n    /// than an error, so callers can fingerprint a database before it\n    /// has been created.\n    pub fn of<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<Self, LinkError> {\n        let metadata = match fs::metadata(path.as_ref()) {\n            Ok(metadata) => metadata,\n            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n                return Ok(Self::default())\n            }\n            Err(error) => return Err(LinkError::Io(error)),\n        };\n        let modified_nanos = metadata\n            .modified()\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|time| time.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).ok())\n            .map(|duration| duration.as_nanos())\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n        Ok(Self {\n            len: metadata.len(),\n            modified_nanos,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// A store of links addressed by `T`, expressed in terms of owned\n/// [`GenericLink<T>`] values so that both in-memory maps and\n/// memory-mapped doublets stores can implement it.\npub trait LinksStorage<T: LinkReference> {\n    /// Creates a link and returns its address. A uniqueness resolver may return\n    /// an existing link after removing the temporary allocation.\n    fn create_link(&mut self, source: T, target: T) -> Result<T, LinkError>;\n\n    /// [`Self::create_link`], reporting every change, including partial changes\n    /// before an error. Transactions need these callbacks to distinguish a new\n    /// allocation from a duplicate resolved into an existing link.\n    ///\n    /// The default is for backends that create one row atomically. Backends\n    /// with cascades or partial writes must override it with their callbacks,\n    /// as for [`Self::update_link_observed`].\n    fn create_link_observed(\n        &mut self,\n        source: T,\n        target: T,\n        observer: &mut dyn FnMut(GenericLink<T>, GenericLink<T>),\n    ) -> Result<T, LinkError> {\n        let index = self.create_link(source, target)?;\n        let after = self\n            .get_link(index)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| GenericLink::new(index, source, target));\n        observer(GenericLink::null(), after);\n        Ok(index)\n    }\n\n    /// Ensures a link exists at `index`, creating placeholders as needed.\n    fn ensure_link_created(&mut self, index: T) -> Result<T, LinkError>;\n\n    /// [`Self::ensure_link_created`], reporting every placeholder it creates.\n    ///\n    /// Backends differ in whether intermediate addresses remain allocated.\n    /// This default compares rows before/after the operation, including partial\n    /// changes on error, so a transaction can undo either backend's behavior.\n    /// It costs O(N log N) time and O(N) rows; backends may override it with\n    /// allocation callbacks. The built-in map adapters avoid this copy.\n    fn ensure_link_created_observed(\n        &mut self,\n        index: T,\n        observer: &mut dyn FnMut(GenericLink<T>, GenericLink<T>),\n    ) -> Result<T, LinkError> {\n        let before: std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _> = self\n            .all_links()\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|row| (row.index, row))\n            .collect();\n        let outcome = self.ensure_link_created(index);\n        let mut after: std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _> = self\n            .all_links()\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|row| (row.index, row))\n            .collect();\n        for (id, previous) in before {\n            let next = after.remove(&id).unwrap_or_else(GenericLink::null);\n            if previous != next {\n                observer(previous, next);\n            }\n        }\n        for (_, row) in after {\n            observer(GenericLink::null(), row);\n        }\n        outcome\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the link stored at `index`, if any.\n    fn get_link(&self, index: T) -> Option<GenericLink<T>>;\n\n    /// Returns `true` when a link exists at `index`.\n    fn link_exists(&self, index: T) -> bool {\n        self.get_link(index).is_some()\n    }\n\n    /// Repoints `index` at `source`/`target`, returning the previous state.\n    fn update_link(&mut self, index: T, source: T, target: T) -> Result<GenericLink<T>, LinkError>;\n\n    /// Deletes `index`, returning the link that was removed.\n    fn delete_link(&mut self, index: T) -> Result<GenericLink<T>, LinkError>;\n\n    /// [`Self::update_link`], reporting every `(before, after)` change it made.\n    ///\n    /// A store that resolves duplicate doublets turns one write into a cascade\n    /// of changes, and the transactions layer has to log each of them or a\n    /// rollback cannot restore what the write actually did. This is the\n    /// equivalent of the `WriteHandler` the C# decorators forward to.\n    ///\n    /// The default implementation reports the single change a store without any\n    /// policy of its own makes, so implementors only override it when they\n    /// really can cascade.\n    fn update_link_observed(\n        &mut self,\n        index: T,\n        source: T,\n        target: T,\n        observer: &mut dyn FnMut(GenericLink<T>, GenericLink<T>),\n    ) -> Result<GenericLink<T>, LinkError> {\n        let previous = self.update_link(index, source, target)?;\n        let after = self\n            .get_link(index)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| GenericLink::new(index, source, target));\n        observer(previous, after);\n        Ok(previous)\n    }\n\n    /// [`Self::delete_link`], reporting every `(before, after)` change it made.\n    ///\n    /// See [`Self::update_link_observed`]; a cascading delete removes every link\n    /// that still referenced `index`.\n    fn delete_link_observed(\n        &mut self,\n        index: T,\n        observer: &mut dyn FnMut(GenericLink<T>, GenericLink<T>),\n    ) -> Result<GenericLink<T>, LinkError> {\n        let deleted = self.delete_link(index)?;\n        observer(deleted, GenericLink::null());\n        Ok(deleted)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns every link in the store.\n    fn all_links(&self) -> Vec<GenericLink<T>>;\n\n    /// Returns every link matching the (optional) index/source/target pattern.\n    fn query_links(\n        &self,\n        index: Option<T>,\n        source: Option<T>,\n        target: Option<T>,\n    ) -> Vec<GenericLink<T>> {\n        self.all_links()\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|link| {\n                index.is_none_or(|value| value == link.index)\n                    && source.is_none_or(|value| value == link.source)\n                    && target.is_none_or(|value| value == link.target)\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Finds the address of a link with the given source and target.\n    fn search_link(&self, source: T, target: T) -> Option<T> {\n        self.all_links()\n            .into_iter()\n            .find(|link| link.source == source && link.target == target)\n            .map(|link| link.index)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the address of an existing `(source, target)` link,\n    /// creating it when it does not exist yet.\n    fn get_or_create_link(&mut self, source: T, target: T) -> Result<T, LinkError> {\n        match self.search_link(source, target) {\n            Some(index) => Ok(index),\n            None => self.create_link(source, target),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Number of links currently stored.\n    fn links_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.all_links().len()\n    }\n\n    /// Optional logical name snapshot for transactional undo. Unnamed stores\n    /// return None without allocation. Include names of absent/external rows.\n    fn capture_names(\n        &mut self,\n    ) -> Result<Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<T, String>>, LinkError> {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n\n    /// Changes one logical name without recording. A named adapter must restore\n    /// external-reference names even when their row currently does not exist.\n    fn set_link_name(&mut self, _index: T, _name: Option<&str>) -> Result<T, LinkError> {\n        Err(LinkError::StorageError(\n            \"storage does not support names\".into(),\n        ))\n    }\n\n    /// Makes every write durable on disk.\n    ///\n    /// Implementations that keep state in memory write it out here;\n    /// memory-mapped implementations `fsync` the backing file. Callers\n    /// that need crash-consistency guarantees must call this — see the\n    /// durability notes on each implementation.\n    fn flush(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError>;\n\n    /// Cheap check for \"did another process write to this database since\n    /// we last read or wrote it?\".\n    ///\n    /// The default implementation reports `false`, which is correct for\n    /// stores that are not shared through the filesystem.\n    fn has_external_changes(&self) -> Result<bool, LinkError> {\n        Ok(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Re-reads the database from disk, discarding cached state.\n    ///\n    /// The default implementation is a no-op for stores that always read\n    /// through to their backing storage.\n    fn reload(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extension implemented by stores that keep links resident in memory and\n/// can therefore lend out references instead of copies.\n///\n/// Memory-mapped stores deliberately do **not** implement this: their\n/// links are decoded from raw memory on read, so there is no stable\n/// `&GenericLink<T>` to borrow.\npub trait LinksStorageRef<T: LinkReference>: LinksStorage<T> {\n    /// Borrows the link stored at `index`.\n    fn get_link_ref(&self, index: T) -> Option<&GenericLink<T>>;\n\n    /// Borrows every link in the store.\n    fn all_link_refs(&self) -> Vec<&GenericLink<T>>;\n\n    /// Borrows every link matching the (optional) index/source/target pattern.\n    fn query_link_refs(\n        &self,\n        index: Option<T>,\n        source: Option<T>,\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
