u128) -> LinkError {\n    LinkError::InvalidFormat(format!(\n        \"transaction {owner:032x} has both commit and rollback decisions\"\n    ))\n}\n# Names in ordinary transactions and version history\n\nThe ordinary Rust and C# transaction decorators record `SetName`/`set_name`\nand `RemoveName`/`remove_name`. Rollback restores names, including both owners\nwhen assigning a unique name moves it. Undoing deletion restores the row's\nname and names removed by cascading deletion. Names assigned to absent rows,\naddress zero and empty strings retain their distinct meanings.\n\nThe ordinary version decorator publishes name-only changes as versions.\nCheckout and branch switching replay complete row/name records. Pending or\nfailed commit, undo, recovery and movement owners fence further named writes\nuntil cleanup succeeds. A logical no-op name assignment adds no version.\n\nRun the persistent examples with separate directories:\n\n```sh\ncargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example transaction_names -- /tmp/rust-names\ndotnet run --project examples/transaction-names-csharp -- /tmp/csharp-names\n```\n\nThe staged engine already includes names in its immutable revisions; its\nRust, C# and Rust-backed JS/WASM sessions retain those APIs and guarantees.\nSee [engine strategies](ENGINE-STRATEGIES.md) for cache, persistent and\ndistributed configurations.\n\n## Complete journal payload\n\nThe existing Rust `GenericTransition<T>` remains `Copy`. C#'s `Transition<T>`\nretains its original fields. Their row-only v1 serialization and public\n`log()` / `Log` snapshots remain available. A name-only transition projects to\nan update with empty before/after rows. That row projection cannot restore\nnames: use `journal()` / `Journal` and `JournalRecord` for complete history,\nor `apply_record` / `ApplyRecord` and their revert counterparts for unlogged\nreplay. The same admission rules apply to these complete replay methods.\n\nRecords without name metadata still serialize exactly as v1. Complete records\nuse nine pipe-separated fields:\n\n```text\nv2|owner|sequence|unixMilliseconds|kind|beforeRow|afterRow|mode|names\n```\n\nThe first seven fields retain the row codec's meanings, with `v2` as the\nversion. Mode `n` means names only, requiring an update and empty rows. Mode\n`r` replays a row and its associated name state. Name changes are sorted by\nnumeric address, separated by semicolons, and encoded as\n`address,beforeName,afterName`. `-` means absent; an empty field means a\npresent empty string. Names use uppercase four-digit UTF-16 code-unit hex,\nso delimiters, NULs, newlines and Unicode never change record boundaries.\nThe complete codec requires canonical fields, unique sorted addresses and\ntimestamps representable by C# `DateTimeOffset`. C# preserves its existing\nunpaired UTF-16 string domain; Rust rejects those values before replay.\n[Shared fixtures](protocol/transaction-name-vectors.json) specify both cases.\n\nNew readers accept v1 journals and old row-only movement intents. Old readers\nreject v2 transaction payloads; upgrade readers before writing named history.\nExisting v1 records contain no historical names, which cannot be reconstructed.\nChunk archives and movement intents preserve complete v2 records. Recovery\nvalidates all recognized records before replacing live history or changing\nrows or names, including conflicting payloads at the same sequence.\n\n## Persistence and cost\n\nExplicit name writes append and flush their complete undo record before\nchanging the name sidecar. Commit still requires the journal decision and\ndata/name checkpoint; an uncertain decision retains its cleanup owner.\nRecovery redoes committed records and undoes unfinished name writes using\nthe complete payload. Fault images and actual finite process exits test these\nboundaries. Filesystem flush contracts remain dependent on the configured\nadapter and hardware. The existing row mutation before its observer-journal\nappend remains an unfinished crash window; name journaling does not resolve it.\n\nThe selected transaction wrapper scans and decodes the named sidecar before\neach row or name operation to capture names of absent rows and cascade victims.\nSorting costs O(N log N) for N sidecar rows, plus decoded name bytes and\nlogical-map insertion costs; name edits also clone the\nlogical map, retain changed strings and add a pre-effect journal flush.\nComplete history snapshots copy retained name payloads. Row-only records use\nan empty name collection. Bare stores do not run this bookkeeping. Rust\nunnamed adapters return `None` without a name-map allocation and reject named\nrecords before replaying their rows.\n\nC# custom `INamedTypesLinks<T>` implementations inherit row-based name capture.\nAdapters supporting names of absent rows must override `CaptureNames()` to\ninclude them. `ReassignsNames` defaults to unique-name reassignment; adapters\nsupporting shared names override it to `false`, as `NamedLinksDecorator` does.\nBoth existing built-in name policies are preserved.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Our atomic catalog provides one serialization point; it does not supply Accord's leaderless protocol or its latency properties. |\n\n## Existing reusable components\n\nThe project already depends on `doublets` / `Platform.Data.Doublets` for raw\nlinks, allocation, uniqueness, and cascade policies. Its storage traits and\n`INamedTypesLinks` are extension seams. `FileTransitionLog`, advisory locks,\nTCP `RemoteLinks`, and the JS client transport contract should be reused.\nThe optional staged layer can compose validation, history, and replication\nwithout imposing their allocations or I/O on a bare in-memory cache.\n\nFor production consensus, existing maintained implementations such as\n[etcd/raft](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft),\n[OpenRaft](https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft), and\n[DotNext Raft](https://dotnet.github.io/dotNext/features/cluster/raft.html)\nprovide election and log-replication machinery. They are not interchangeable\nwith a replica acknowledgement counter. JavaScript's client transport should\nadvertise backend guarantees rather than inventing them client-side.\n\n## Source observations, pinned for reproducibility\n\nSource was downloaded through GitHub's contents API; the functions below were\nread. Recovery\n//! replays committed-but-unapplied transitions and undoes logged uncommitted\n//! changes, reporting replay and flush failures.\n//!\n//! This legacy observer adapter mutates the wrapped store before recording its\n//! callbacks. A process failure between a mutation and its journal append can\n//! leave changes without undo records; a cascade can affect several rows in\n//! that window. after: GenericLink<T>,\n) {\n    let zero = T::from_byte(0);\n    let key = if before.index != zero {\n        before.index\n    } else {\n        after.index\n    };\n    if key == zero {\n usize).cloned().collect();\n        // Rollback has already durably undone these writes. Reapplying them\n        // would resurrect aborted data; archives contain committed changes only.\n        let archived: Vec<_> = chunk\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|transition| !self.rolled_back.contains(&transition.transaction_id))\n            .cloned()\n            .collect();\n        for transition in &archived {\n            if !self.applied.contains(&transition.sequence) {\n                if !self.committed.contains(&transition.transaction_id) {\n                    return Ok(()); // Never apply or discard a pending chunk.\n                }\n                self.replaying = true;\n                let result = self.try_apply_record(transition, true);\n                self.replaying = false;\n                result?;\n                if !self.applied.contains(&transition.sequence) {\n                    return Ok(()); // never drop un-applied\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        if archived.is_empty() {\n            self.log.drain(0..chunk.len());\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(archive_directory).map_err(|error| {\n            LinkError::StorageError(format!(\n                \"failed to create archive dir {}: {error}\",\n                archive_directory.display()\n            ))\n        })?;\n        let timestamp = now_unix_ms();\n        // Independent journals may share this directory and restart their\n        // counters at the same realtime. The PR remains unmerged\nand is not ready for final approval.\n# Names in ordinary transactions and version history\n\nThe ordinary Rust and C# transaction decorators record `SetName`/`set_name`\nand `RemoveName`/`remove_name`. Rollback restores names, including both owners\nwhen assigning a unique name moves it. Undoing deletion restores the row's\nname and names removed by cascading deletion. Names assigned to absent rows,\naddress zero and empty strings retain their distinct meanings.\n\nThe ordinary version decorator publishes name-only changes as versions.\nCheckout and branch switching replay complete row/name records. Pending or\nfailed commit, undo, recovery and movement owners fence further named writes\nuntil cleanup succeeds. A logical no-op name assignment adds no version.\nRow records capture the actual resulting name. C# journals pending observed\nrows before a callback writes a name, so that name write follows its triggering\nrow during replay. Ordinary callbacks retain their existing coalescing and\ndelivery before journal errors. A failed post-effect name capture retains\nobserved row undo and fences an explicit owner until rollback completes.\n\nRun the persistent examples with separate directories:\n\n```sh\ncargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example transaction_names -- /tmp/rust-names\ndotnet run --project examples/transaction-names-csharp -- /tmp/csharp-names\n```\n\nThe staged engine already includes names in its immutable revisions; its\nRust, C# and Rust-backed JS/WASM sessions retain those APIs and guarantees.\nSee [engine strategies](ENGINE-STRATEGIES.md) for cache, persistent and\ndistributed configurations.\n\n## Complete journal payload\n\nThe existing Rust `GenericTransition<T>` remains `Copy`. C#'s `Transition<T>`\nretains its original fields. Their row-only v1 serialization and public\n`log()` / `Log` snapshots remain available. A name-only transition projects to\nan update with empty before/after rows. That row projection cannot restore\nnames: use `journal()` / `Journal` and `JournalRecord` for complete history,\nor `apply_record` / `ApplyRecord` and their revert counterparts for unlogged\nreplay. The same admission rules apply to these complete replay methods.\n\nRecords without name metadata still serialize exactly as v1. Complete records\nuse nine pipe-separated fields:\n\n```text\nv2|owner|sequence|unixMilliseconds|kind|beforeRow|afterRow|mode|names\n```\n\nThe first seven fields retain the row codec's meanings, with `v2` as the\nversion. Mode `n` means names only, requiring an update and empty rows. Mode\n`r` replays a row and its associated name state. Name changes are sorted by\nnumeric address, separated by semicolons, and encoded as\n`address,beforeName,afterName`. `-` means absent; an empty field means a\npresent empty string. Names use uppercase four-digit UTF-16 code-unit hex,\nso delimiters, NULs, newlines and Unicode never change record boundaries.\nThe complete codec requires canonical fields, unique sorted addresses and\ntimestamps representable by C# `DateTimeOffset`. C# preserves its existing\nunpaired UTF-16 string domain; Rust rejects those values before replay.\n[Shared fixtures](protocol/transaction-name-vectors.json) specify both cases.\n\nNew readers accept v1 journals and old row-only movement intents. Old readers\nreject v2 transaction payloads; upgrade readers before writing named history.\nExisting v1 records contain no historical names, which cannot be reconstructed.\nChunk archives and movement intents preserve complete v2 records. Recovery\nvalidates all recognized records before replacing live history or changing\nrows or names, including conflicting payloads at the same sequence.\n\n## Persistence and cost\n\nExplicit name writes append and flush their complete undo record before\nchanging the name sidecar. Commit still requires the journal decision and\ndata/name checkpoint; an uncertain decision retains its cleanup owner.\nRecovery redoes committed records and undoes unfinished name writes using\nthe complete payload. Fault images and actual finite process exits test these\nboundaries. Filesystem flush contracts remain dependent on the configured\nadapter and hardware. The existing row mutation before its observer-journal\nappend remains an unfinished crash window; name journaling does not resolve it.\n\nThe selected transaction wrapper scans and decodes the named sidecar before\neach row or name operation to capture names of absent rows and cascade victims.\nRow writes also capture the resulting names. C# callbacks that write names\ndrain their observed row batch and capture its names before that name write;\ntheir cost grows with the number of such writes as well as sidecar size.\nSorting costs O(N log N) for N sidecar rows, plus decoded name bytes and\nlogical-map insertion costs; name edits also clone the\nlogical map, retain changed strings and add a pre-effect journal flush.\nComplete history snapshots copy retained name payloads. Row-only records use\nan empty name collection. Bare stores do not run this bookkeeping. Rust\nunnamed adapters return `None` without a name-map allocation and reject named\nrecords before replaying their rows. Rust recovery probes this capability once\nfor a validated journal containing names, rather than scanning per record.\n\nC# custom `INamedTypesLinks<T>` implementations inherit row-based name capture.\nAdapters supporting names of absent rows must override `CaptureNames()` to\ninclude them. `ReassignsNames` defaults to unique-name reassignment; adapters\nsupporting shared names override it to `false`, as `NamedLinksDecorator` does.\nBoth existing built-in name policies are preserved.\nCustom capture methods return a detached snapshot. Each row records a primary reference, relevant source,\nand an implementation implication. Similar settings do not imply equivalent\nperformance, failure handling, or guarantees.\n\n| System / primary reference | Source seam inspected | Design and implication |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [SQLite atomic commit](https://www.sqlite.org/atomiccommit.html), [WAL](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html) | [wal.c](https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/blob/master/src/wal.c) | Journal persistence and database checkpoint ordering are separate boundaries. A checkpoint marker must follow durable data; staging avoids exposing partial transactions. |\n| [PostgreSQL isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html) | [predicate.c](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/backend/storage/lmgr/predicate.c) | Snapshot isolation permits write skew. Serializable validation must account for reads and predicates, not only written keys. A whole-store revision check is conservative but safe. |\n| [RocksDB transactions](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/wiki/Transactions) | [optimistic_transaction.cc](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/utilities/transactions/optimistic_transaction.cc), [pessimistic_transaction.cc](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/utilities/transactions/pessimistic_transaction.cc) | Offer pessimistic exclusion and optimistic validation explicitly. Locks, version tracking, retries, and history have different costs. |\n| [Redis replication](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/replication/) | [replication.c](https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/unstable/src/replication.c) | Asynchronous primary/follower copies improve read scale. Waiting for replica acknowledgements alone does not provide consensus or safe automatic failover. |\n| [etcd API guarantees](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/learning/api_guarantees/) | [raft.go](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/main/raft.go) | Quorum intersection, a fenced leader, ordered durable logs, and safe membership changes are necessary for consensus. A fan-out log must not advertise Raft guarantees. |\n| [TiKV transactions](https://tikv.github.io/sig-transaction/doc/tikv/index.html) | [transaction](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/tree/master/src/storage/txn) | Cross-shard atomic writes require coordination and recovery beyond per-shard atomicity. Raw and transactional writes cannot be mixed safely. |\n| [FoundationDB transactions](https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/developer-guide.html), [read/write path](https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/read-write-path.html) | [NativeAPI.cpp](https://github.com/apple/foundationdb/blob/dbf079f58df53df898eee906738a506cb80a21a6/fdbclient/NativeAPI.cpp), [ConflictSet.cpp](https://github.com/apple/foundationdb/blob/dbf079f58df53df898eee906738a506cb80a21a6/fdbserver/resolver/ConflictSet.cpp) | Track observed reads, including absent keys, and validate against intervening writes. Optional local point-read validation permits disjoint edits; scans remain conservative whole-revision predicates. No FoundationDB protocol or range index is copied. |\n| [Apache Iceberg optimistic concurrency](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/#optimistic-concurrency) | [format specification](https://apache.googlesource.com/iceberg/+/HEAD/format/spec.md), optimistic concurrency and filesystem operations | Immutable data plus atomic metadata publication separates data storage from the serialization point. The partitioned journal decorator stages objects in independent groups, then compares all selected catalog generations before publishing pointers. Data files and table formats are not copied. |\n| [MySQL/InnoDB redo architecture](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/PAGE_INNODB_REDO_LOG.html), [doublewrite](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/innodb-doublewrite-buffer.html) | [log0write.cc](https://github.com/mysql/mysql-server/blob/561753af986c3c006c4b6c7caa8359748fb55b22/storage/innobase/log/log0write.cc#L1058) | A requested log position, OS-written position and durable position are distinct. One flush can release several commit waiters. Doublewrite repairs torn data pages; checksums alone only detect damage. Group commit and page repair are separate optional designs, not supplied by revision compression. |\n| [MongoDB write concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern/) | [replication_coordinator_impl.cpp](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/7a45cb24e938fa1a18dad3b1969444d5d80f8d09/src/mongo/db/repl/replication_coordinator_impl.cpp#L2194) | Durable acknowledgements and applied replica state differ. Write-concern timeout does not undo the primary's write. Preserve explicit uncertain outcomes and discover publication before retrying; a replica counter does not copy MongoDB's replication protocol. |\n| [Cassandra Dynamo architecture](https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/architecture/dynamo.html), [hints](https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/managing/operating/hints.html) | [StorageProxy.java](https://github.com/apache/cassandra/blob/05853eaeab006bd1e834331ac8b1dfdc464d1f31/src/java/org/apache/cassandra/service/StorageProxy.java#L978) | Ordinary writes use consistency-level response handlers and timestamp reconciliation. Hints are best effort; anti-entropy remains necessary. Quorum intersection alone is not a complete transaction isolation protocol. Our fixed-primary log replication does not implement Dynamo repair or timestamp conflict resolution. |\n| [Cassandra 6.0 / Accord](https://cassandra.apache.org/_/events/20261011-community-over-code-glasgow.html) | [transaction dispatch](https://github.com/apache/cassandra/blob/05853eaeab006bd1e834331ac8b1dfdc464d1f31/src/java/org/apache/cassandra/service/StorageProxy.java#L1269), [CoordinateTransaction.java](https://github.com/apache/cassandra-accord/blob/ce855de13902e7e3ebfa4356d265f0c49be1bb8e/accord-core/src/main/java/accord/coordinate/CoordinateTransaction.java#L123) | Current Cassandra includes an Accord route as well as ordinary writes. Accord chooses transaction paths using quorum responses, dependencies, timestamps and topology epochs. Our atomic catalog provides one serialization point; it does not supply Accord's leaderless protocol or its latency properties. |\n\n## Existing reusable components\n\nThe project already depends on `doublets` / `Platform.Data.Doublets` for raw\nlinks, allocation, uniqueness, and cascade policies. Its storage traits and\n`INamedTypesLinks` are extension seams. `FileTransitionLog`, advisory locks,\nTCP `RemoteLinks`, and the JS client transport contract should be reused.\nThe optional staged layer can compose validation, history, and replication\nwithout imposing their allocations or I/O on a bare in-memory cache.\n\nFor production consensus, existing maintained implementations such as\n[etcd/raft](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft),\n[OpenRaft](https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft), and\n[DotNext Raft](https://dotnet.github.io/dotNext/features/cluster/raft.html)\nprovide election and log-replication machinery. They are not interchangeable\nwith a replica acknowledgement counter. JavaScript's client transport should\nadvertise backend guarantees rather than inventing them client-side.\n\n## Source observations, pinned for reproducibility\n\nSource was downloaded through GitHub's contents API; the functions below were\nread. The existing `Observed` policy remains the\ndefault. Bare stores acquire no transaction work. The staged\n[engine](ENGINE-STRATEGIES.md) already keeps private revisions until publication;\nits Rust-backed JS/WASM session does not need this ordinary-store option.\nThe Rust ordinary transaction policy also executes in actual WASM contracts.\n\n```rust\nuse link_cli::{GenericTransactionsDecorator, RowUndoPolicy};\n# fn select<T, S, L>(tx: GenericTransactionsDecorator<T, S, L>)\n# -> Result<GenericTransactionsDecorator<T, S, L>, link_cli::LinkError>\n# where T: doublets::data::LinkReference, S: link_cli::LinksStorage<T>, L: link_cli::TransitionLogStore {\nlet tx = tx.with_row_undo(RowUndoPolicy::WriteAheadImage)?;\n# Ok(tx)\n# }\n```\n\n```csharp\nusing var transactions = new TransactionsDecorator(\n    data, log, rowUndoPolicy: RowUndoPolicy.WriteAheadImage);\n```\n\nRust also permits `set_row_undo_policy` while idle; a rejected change preserves\nan existing owner. C# selects the policy at construction. Existing constructor\nsignatures remain available, including their default behavior. New readers\nalways recover image metadata, regardless of the policy for subsequent writes.\n\nRun persistent row/name rollback and version-checkout examples:\n\n```sh\ncargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example transaction_names -- /tmp/rust-undo --row-image\ndotnet run --project examples/transaction-names-csharp -- /tmp/csharp-undo --row-image\n```\n\n## Ordering and ownership\n\nBefore an owner'\"'s first row or name write, the decorator captures its complete\nlogical rows and names, appends a mandatory undo image and flushes the journal.\nOnly then can the adapter change data. The image remains attached to the owner\nthrough preparation errors, uncertain decisions and failed cleanup. Empty or\nunobserved writes cannot detach it. Explicit names still have their separate\npre-effect record barrier.\n\nSuccessful writes compare actual rows/names with the initial image plus all\npending records. Corrections describe effects omitted by adapter callbacks,\nincluding another owner's evicted name, deletion/allocation and names on absent\naddresses. The complete record batch is retained before its first append.\nReconciliation finishes before automatic commit or version publication intent.\nComplete history therefore includes those effects for committed redo and version\nmovement. Callback delivery and ordinary coalescing remain available.\n\nRollback restores the image through logical storage methods: clear references,\nremove unknown allocations, reserve original addresses, remove allocator-created\nholes, restore rows and replace the full name map. It verifies the resulting\nimage before acknowledging cleanup. An error retains admission for retry.\nRecovery validates the entire journal before mutation, undoes unfinished images\nin descending base-sequence order with intervening ordinary pending records,\nand redoes the committed suffix that restoration could have overwritten.\nCheckpoint markers cannot skip that suffix. Repeated recovery and following\nedits are part of the regression contracts.\n\n## Adapter and persistence requirements\n\nOne writer must own both the data and journal. Concurrent direct writes to the\nwrapped store bypass this protocol. Enumerations and name capture must be\ncomplete, detached logical snapshots. Replay must permit empty placeholders,\nrecreating original addresses and restoring their contents/names. Custom\nadapters whose replay repeats unrelated side effects are incompatible; failed\nimage verification retains ownership rather than claiming successful rollback.\n\nDurability requires truthful journal and data/name flushes in persistent adapters.\nAn uncommitted image can restore readable logical rows after process loss,\nincluding a crash before any observer callback. It cannot make an unreadable or\ntorn physical storage file open successfully, or repair hardware that violates\nflush ordering. Finite process exits leave the OS alive. They do not simulate\nphysical power loss. The default observer policy retains its pre-callback crash\nwindow; choose the image policy or a staged engine for the corresponding\nlogical-write guarantee.\n\n## Cost and wire compatibility\n\nThe first write captures/sorts N logical rows and M names, retains their strings,\nand adds one journal append plus flush before effects. The encoded image and\nowner memory cost O(N + M + name bytes), with sorting/map work O(N log N + M log M).\nEvery selected write rebuilds predicted state from the image and K pending\nrecords, captures actual rows/names and computes corrections. Its work grows\nwith N, M, K and name bytes; this implementation does not provide a page-sized\nundo cost. Captures/temporary maps add the same order of transient memory.\nOnly missing logical effects add correction records. Long explicit owners\nrepeat that prediction work. Image rollback scans/restores the full logical\nstore. The physical sidecar retains mandatory images; sized/chunked policies\ncontinue to limit logical transition history and archives. Page undo and image\ncompaction remain separate unfinished efficiency work.\n\nImages occupy the existing \"'`__transactions:transition:` namespace, ensuring old\nrecord readers reject this mandatory protocol instead of ignoring it:\n\n```text\nv3|undo|owner|baseSequence|rows|names\n```\n\nThere are exactly six fields. Each row records a primary reference, relevant source,\nand an implementation implication. Similar settings do not imply equivalent\nperformance, failure handling, or guarantees.\n\n| System / primary reference | Source seam inspected | Design and implication |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [SQLite atomic commit](https://www.sqlite.org/atomiccommit.html), [WAL](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html) | [wal.c](https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/blob/master/src/wal.c) | Journal persistence and database checkpoint ordering are separate boundaries. A checkpoint marker must follow durable data; staging avoids exposing partial transactions. |\n| [PostgreSQL isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html) | [predicate.c](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/backend/storage/lmgr/predicate.c) | Snapshot isolation permits write skew. Serializable validation must account for reads and predicates, not only written keys. A whole-store revision check is conservative but safe. |\n| [RocksDB transactions](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/wiki/Transactions) | [optimistic_transaction.cc](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/utilities/transactions/optimistic_transaction.cc), [pessimistic_transaction.cc](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/utilities/transactions/pessimistic_transaction.cc) | Offer pessimistic exclusion and optimistic validation explicitly. Locks, version tracking, retries, and history have different costs. |\n| [Redis replication](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/replication/) | [replication.c](https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/unstable/src/replication.c) | Asynchronous primary/follower copies improve read scale. Waiting for replica acknowledgements alone does not provide consensus or safe automatic failover. |\n| [etcd API guarantees](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/learning/api_guarantees/) | [raft.go](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/main/raft.go) | Quorum intersection, a fenced leader, ordered durable logs, and safe membership changes are necessary for consensus. A fan-out log must not advertise Raft guarantees. |\n| [TiKV transactions](https://tikv.github.io/sig-transaction/doc/tikv/index.html) | [transaction](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/tree/master/src/storage/txn) | Cross-shard atomic writes require coordination and recovery beyond per-shard atomicity. Its storage traits and\n`INamedTypesLinks` are extension seams. `FileTransitionLog`, advisory locks,\nTCP `RemoteLinks`, and the JS client transport contract should be reused.\nThe optional staged layer can compose validation, history, and replication\nwithout imposing their allocations or I/O on a bare in-memory cache.\n\nFor production consensus, existing maintained implementations such as\n[etcd/raft](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft),\n[OpenRaft](https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft), and\n[DotNext Raft](https://dotnet.github.io/dotNext/features/cluster/raft.html)\nprovide election and log-replication machinery. Our fixed-primary log replication does not implement Dynamo repair or timestamp conflict resolution. |\n| [Cassandra 6.0 / Accord](https://cassandra.apache.org/_/events/20261011-community-over-code-glasgow.html) | [transaction dispatch](https://github.com/apache/cassandra/blob/05853eaeab006bd1e834331ac8b1dfdc464d1f31/src/java/org/apache/cassandra/service/StorageProxy.java#L1269), [CoordinateTransaction.java](https://github.com/apache/cassandra-accord/blob/ce855de13902e7e3ebfa4356d265f0c49be1bb8e/accord-core/src/main/java/accord/coordinate/CoordinateTransaction.java#L123) | Current Cassandra includes an Accord route as well as ordinary writes. [2026-10-25T16:04:40.571Z] [STDERR] *** Add File: /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1792924568628/docs/ENGINE-SHARED-STATE.md
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.573Z] [STDERR] +# Optional shared immutable engine state
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.576Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.582Z] [STDERR] +Select the engine's in-memory rows independently of concurrency, isolation,
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.587Z] [STDERR] +history, constraints, journal encoding and replication. Existing options default
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.591Z] [STDERR] +to `Flat`, which uses the existing sorted map. Bare stores acquire no engine
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.592Z] [STDERR] +state. `Shared` uses a persistent ordered tree: a candidate retains the immutable
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.595Z] [STDERR] +root and replaces paths to changed entries. Earlier snapshots remain immutable.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.598Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.601Z] [STDERR] +```rust
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.602Z] [STDERR] +use link_cli::engine::{Engine, EngineOptions, MemoryLog, StateStructure};
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.607Z] [STDERR] +let engine = Engine::<u64, _>::open(MemoryLog::default(), EngineOptions {
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.610Z] [STDERR] +    state_structure: StateStructure::Shared,
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.613Z] [STDERR] +    ..Default::default()
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.615Z] [STDERR] +})?;
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.616Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.618Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.619Z] [STDERR] +```csharp
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.623Z] [STDERR] +var engine = new LinksEngine<ulong>(new MemoryCommitLog(), new() {
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.624Z] [STDERR] +    StateStructure = StateStructure.Shared
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.626Z] [STDERR] +});
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.629Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.631Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.633Z] [STDERR] +```javascript
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.634Z] [STDERR] +const engine = new WasmEngine(binding, { stateStructure: 'shared' });
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.637Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.638Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.641Z] [STDERR] +The Rust-backed JS/TS/WASM option accepts `flat` and `shared`; unknown values
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.643Z] [STDERR] +fail before opening the engine. C# also rejects undefined enum values. Sessions
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.644Z] [STDERR] +keep the same links/names API, visibility, conflict validation, rollback and
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.646Z] [STDERR] +unknown-commit behavior. The choice changes allocation and update costs, without
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.647Z] [STDERR] +adding a worker, queue, timer or new durability guarantee.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.649Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.650Z] [STDERR] +## Composition and compatibility
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.653Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.655Z] [STDERR] +Both representations write the same complete `engine1` revisions. Existing
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.656Z] [STDERR] +journals reopen under either choice. During shared recovery, the full decoded
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.658Z] [STDERR] +revision is compared with the preceding revision; unchanged entries reuse its
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.660Z] [STDERR] +root paths. Recovery still reads, decodes and compares complete revisions.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.661Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.663Z] [STDERR] +History retention and active snapshot pinning remain separate choices. A
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.664Z] [STDERR] +read-only commit publishes no new root. Rollback discards the candidate. A
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.666Z] [STDERR] +failed append or flush preserves previously pinned snapshots and fences the
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.667Z] [STDERR] +engine until reopening discovers the journal's actual committed prefix.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.669Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.672Z] [STDERR] +Each branch selects its own representation. Forking between shared engines can
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.675Z] [STDERR] +retain the existing root; a fork to the other representation converts the rows.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.680Z] [STDERR] +Merge applies changed rows to the parent's selected map. Branch conflict checks,
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.689Z] [STDERR] +allocator recovery, saved merge bases and constraints retain their existing
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.693Z] [STDERR] +behavior. Group preparation uses the same choice for every accepted revision,
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.698Z] [STDERR] +while retaining separate outcomes and the shared flush boundary.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.702Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.705Z] [STDERR] +Rust `Snapshot.get` and `Snapshot.iter` borrow entries directly. `Snapshot.links`
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.707Z] [STDERR] +allocates the returned link vector. The existing `Snapshot.rows() -> &BTreeMap`
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.709Z] [STDERR] +API remains available: the first call on a shared snapshot materializes O(N)
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.712Z] [STDERR] +rows and names, cached for that snapshot and its clones. Mutated candidates have
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.714Z] [STDERR] +their own empty cache. Internal engine reads, validation, encoding, recovery,
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.716Z] [STDERR] +branch operations and WASM export use borrowed iteration and do not request this
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.721Z] [STDERR] +compatibility map. Use `iter` for allocation-sensitive native consumers.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.723Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.725Z] [STDERR] +C# `EngineSnapshot.Rows` keeps its `IReadOnlyDictionary` interface. Shared
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.726Z] [STDERR] +snapshots expose an immutable sorted dictionary; its `SetItem` and `Remove`
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.729Z] [STDERR] +methods return separate dictionaries. Flat snapshots retain a read-only wrapper.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.731Z] [STDERR] +JS snapshots are serialized values and retain their existing boundary copies.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.734Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.736Z] [STDERR] +## Selected costs
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.737Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.738Z] [STDERR] +Let N be the number of rows, W the staged writes, H retained revisions, and B
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.740Z] [STDERR] +the encoded row/name bytes. These costs describe the in-memory map; the complete
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.743Z] [STDERR] +journal encoder and optional constraints have their own costs.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.746Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.747Z] [STDERR] +| Operation | Flat, default | Shared, selected |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.749Z] [STDERR] +| --- | --- | --- |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.750Z] [STDERR] +| Snapshot handle / pin | O(1) | O(1) |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.751Z] [STDERR] +| Candidate root | O(N) row copies | O(1) root sharing |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.754Z] [STDERR] +| Apply W writes to candidate | O(W log N) | O(W log N) path copies and changed entries |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.759Z] [STDERR] +| Scan / name lookup | Copies a complete candidate, then scans | Shares a root, overlays W writes, then scans |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.762Z] [STDERR] +| Retain H small-edit revisions | Up to O(HN) map entries | Initial O(N), then O(W log N) additional paths per revision |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.765Z] [STDERR] +| Encode a committed revision | O(B) | O(B) |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.769Z] [STDERR] +| Recover a revision | Complete decode | Complete decode/comparison plus changed paths |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.771Z] [STDERR] +| First native Rust `rows()` | Existing borrowed map | O(N) compatibility copy, including row names |
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.774Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.780Z] [STDERR] +Rust uses the maintained MIT-licensed `rpds` ordered Arc-based map. Unchanged
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.785Z] [STDERR] +entries retain their allocation identities. C# uses .NET's immutable sorted
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.791Z] [STDERR] +dictionary; frozen AVL nodes share unchanged subtrees, and strings remain
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.797Z] [STDERR] +immutable references. Both components use logarithmic tree paths. Shared maps
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.800Z] [STDERR] +add reference-counted nodes and indirection; for tiny or write-heavy disposable
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.801Z] [STDERR] +states, the flat choice can be cheaper. No timing advantage is asserted without
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.805Z] [STDERR] +a workload measurement.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.807Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.810Z] [STDERR] +Complete journal serialization and selected constraint scans remain O(N/B).
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.815Z] [STDERR] +The delta decorator reduces physical bytes through a complete-record comparison;
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.818Z] [STDERR] +it does not turn this engine into a page WAL or LSM tree. Group preparation also
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.821Z] [STDERR] +buffers complete accepted records and copies history/conflict metadata. Sharing
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.823Z] [STDERR] +does not remove those costs or add physical torn-page repair.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.824Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.826Z] [STDERR] +## Runnable checks and evidence
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.827Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.828Z] [STDERR] +Add `--shared` to the existing examples, independently of `--delta`, `--read-set`
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.830Z] [STDERR] +and `--pessimistic`:
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.831Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.833Z] [STDERR] +```sh
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.834Z] [STDERR] +cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_strategies -- --shared
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.836Z] [STDERR] +dotnet run --project examples/engine-csharp -- --shared
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.837Z] [STDERR] +node js/client/examples/engine.mjs --shared
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.838Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.840Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.841Z] [STDERR] +The JS example uses the usual generated `js/pkg` binding; `CLINK_WASM` may select
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.843Z] [STDERR] +an independently generated web-package directory. Supply an exclusive journal
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.846Z] [STDERR] +path to each example to verify reopening. The journal representation can change
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.848Z] [STDERR] +on reopening without changing its records.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.849Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.852Z] [STDERR] +Finite allocation controls use 256 named rows and sixteen single-row commits.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.853Z] [STDERR] +The prior flat engine shares zero of 4,080 unchanged Rust row references; selected
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.855Z] [STDERR] +shared state retains all 4,080, while the default continues to share zero.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.857Z] [STDERR] +C# controls count actual immutable component nodes and require unchanged
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.860Z] [STDERR] +subtrees across live and replayed revisions. Neither check relies on timing.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.862Z] [STDERR] +Independent 96-step row/name oracles retain every earlier snapshot, and portable
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.864Z] [STDERR] +contracts cover admission/isolation choices, failures, constraints, history,
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.868Z] [STDERR] +mixed branch choices, group commits and existing wire vectors. Actual-WASM and
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.871Z] [STDERR] +Node/Bun/Deno checks exercise the same option through the JS boundary.
[2026-10-25T16:04:40.872Z] [STDERR] +

Shared callers\n  may invoke SetItem, which returns a separate map and cannot mutate a snapshot.\n- Add genuine no-op/read-only/rollback/copy materialization checks, both structure\n  choices in conflict/constraints/group/branch and independently persisted reopen\n  tests. Keep any allocation probe finite, non-timing and separately documented.\n\nBaseline measured before implementation: 256 rows, sixteen single-row commits,\nzero of 4,080 unchanged row references shared. The finite reusable probe is in\nexperiments/issue-138/state-copy-probe; full output is state-copy-before.log.\nThis observes allocation identity, not a timing or power-loss claim.\nrevision. Fixed-primary synchronous replication flushes the primary once, copies\nthe complete missing prefix and flushes each follower once before counting it.\nExplicit catch-up still flushes the primary before reading its prefix. Replica\nacknowledgements retain their existing unknown-outcome and membership semantics.\n\nRunnable durable examples, each with optional `--delta`:\n\n- Rust: `cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_group_commit -- /tmp/group-rust.log`\n- C#: `dotnet run --project examples/group-commit-csharp -- /tmp/group-csharp.log`\n- JS: `CLINK_WASM=/path/to/web-package node js/client/examples/engine-group-commit.mjs /tmp/group-js.log`\n\nThe native examples and JS example use the same portable journal format. Use\nseparate paths for independent databases. One writer owns each file; close all\nhandles before another implementation opens the same journal.\n\n## Costs and verification\n\nFor K accepted writes, preparation still clones/validates/encodes each full\nrevision: O(sum(N_i + W_i)) work plus existing ordered-map costs and encoded name\nbytes. It copies retained history and conflict/ownership metadata, and buffers\nthe K logical records until publication. C# also pins each accepted member's\nsnapshot so its closed handle retains ordinary committed-read behavior. The\nextra memory therefore includes full encoded revisions and retained snapshots,\nnot just K small queue entries. Use bounded groups; there is one serialization\ngate through preparation, append, flush and publication. This reduces flush\ncalls; it does not remove full-state CPU work, implement parallel validation,\ncompact journals, or promise a throughput multiplier.\n\nPortable contracts cover separate revisions, constraints, conflicts, read\ndependencies, history, admission and uncertain prefixes. Native tests exercise\nreal exclusive files, delta journals, two durable replicas, following commits\nand a bounded blocked flush. Ten abrupt child exits per native language cover\nsnapshot/delta logs before and after append/flush, with an acknowledged control,\ntwo actual reopenings, persisted allocation gaps and a following commit.\nActual-WASM tests inject synchronous JS journal\nfaults; Node/Bun/Deno conformance exercises real wasm-bindgen handle transfer and\nqueued requests. Finite fault images test the declared journal contract rather\nthan claiming physical device power-loss coverage.\n# Strategy research (2026-10-24)\n\nThis is a bounded survey of established designs, not a claim to have inspected\nevery successful DBMS. Each row records a primary reference, relevant source,\nand an implementation implication. Similar settings do not imply equivalent\nperformance, failure handling, or guarantees.\n\n| System / primary reference | Source seam inspected | Design and implication |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [SQLite atomic commit](https://www.sqlite.org/atomiccommit.html), [WAL](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html) | [wal.c](https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/blob/master/src/wal.c) | Journal persistence and database checkpoint ordering are separate boundaries. A checkpoint marker must follow durable data; staging avoids exposing partial transactions. |\n| [PostgreSQL isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html) | [predicate.c](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/backend/storage/lmgr/predicate.c) | Snapshot isolation permits write skew. Serializable validation must account for reads and predicates, not only written keys. A whole-store revision check is conservative but safe. |\n| [RocksDB transactions](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/wiki/Transactions) | [optimistic_transaction.cc](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/utilities/transactions/optimistic_transaction.cc), [pessimistic_transaction.cc](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/utilities/transactions/pessimistic_transaction.cc) | Offer pessimistic exclusion and optimistic validation explicitly. Locks, version tracking, retries, and history have different costs. |\n| [Redis replication](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/replication/) | [replication.c](https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/unstable/src/replication.c) | Asynchronous primary/follower copies improve read scale. Waiting for replica acknowledgements alone does not provide consensus or safe automatic failover. |\n| [etcd API guarantees](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/learning/api_guarantees/) | [raft.go](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft/blob/main/raft.go) | Quorum intersection, a fenced leader, ordered durable logs, and safe membership changes are necessary for consensus. A fan-out log must not advertise Raft guarantees. |\n| [TiKV transactions](https://tikv.github.io/sig-transaction/doc/tikv/index.html) | [transaction](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/tree/master/src/storage/txn) | Cross-shard atomic writes require coordination and recovery beyond per-shard atomicity. Raw and transactional writes cannot be mixed safely. |\n| [FoundationDB transactions](https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/developer-guide.html), [read/write path](https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/read-write-path.html) | [NativeAPI.cpp](https://github.com/apple/foundationdb/blob/dbf079f58df53df898eee906738a506cb80a21a6/fdbclient/NativeAPI.cpp), [ConflictSet.cpp](https://github.com/apple/foundationdb/blob/dbf079f58df53df898eee906738a506cb80a21a6/fdbserver/resolver/ConflictSet.cpp) | Track observed reads, including absent keys, and validate against intervening writes. Optional local point-read validation permits disjoint edits; scans remain conservative whole-revision predicates. No FoundationDB protocol or range index is copied. |\n| [Apache Iceberg optimistic concurrency](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/#optimistic-concurrency) | [format specification](https://apache.googlesource.com/iceberg/+/HEAD/format/spec.md), optimistic concurrency and filesystem operations | Immutable data plus atomic metadata publication separates data storage from the serialization point. The partitioned journal decorator stages objects in independent groups, then compares all selected catalog generations before publishing pointers. Data files and table formats are not copied. |\n| [MySQL/InnoDB redo architecture](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/PAGE_INNODB_REDO_LOG.html), [doublewrite](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/innodb-doublewrite-buffer.html) | [log0write.cc](https://github.com/mysql/mysql-server/blob/561753af986c3c006c4b6c7caa8359748fb55b22/storage/innobase/log/log0write.cc#L1058) | A requested log position, OS-written position and durable position are distinct. One flush can release several commit waiters. Doublewrite repairs torn data pages; checksums alone only detect damage. Group commit and page repair are separate optional designs, not supplied by revision compression. |\n| [MongoDB write concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern/) | [replication_coordinator_impl.cpp](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/7a45cb24e938fa1a18dad3b1969444d5d80f8d09/src/mongo/db/repl/replication_coordinator_impl.cpp#L2194) | Durable acknowledgements and applied replica state differ. Write-concern timeout does not undo the primary's write. Preserve explicit uncertain outcomes and discover publication before retrying; a replica counter does not copy MongoDB's replication protocol. |\n| [Cassandra Dynamo architecture](https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/architecture/dynamo.html), [hints](https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/managing/operating/hints.html) | [StorageProxy.java](https://github.com/apache/cassandra/blob/05853eaeab006bd1e834331ac8b1dfdc464d1f31/src/java/org/apache/cassandra/service/StorageProxy.java#L978) | Ordinary writes use consistency-level response handlers and timestamp reconciliation. Hints are best effort; anti-entropy remains necessary. Quorum intersection alone is not a complete transaction isolation protocol. Our fixed-primary log replication does not implement Dynamo repair or timestamp conflict resolution. |\n| [Cassandra 6.0 / Accord](https://cassandra.apache.org/_/events/20261011-community-over-code-glasgow.html) | [transaction dispatch](https://github.com/apache/cassandra/blob/05853eaeab006bd1e834331ac8b1dfdc464d1f31/src/java/org/apache/cassandra/service/StorageProxy.java#L1269), [CoordinateTransaction.java](https://github.com/apache/cassandra-accord/blob/ce855de13902e7e3ebfa4356d265f0c49be1bb8e/accord-core/src/main/java/accord/coordinate/CoordinateTransaction.java#L123) | Current Cassandra includes an Accord route as well as ordinary writes. Accord chooses transaction paths using quorum responses, dependencies, timestamps and topology epochs. Our atomic catalog provides one serialization point; it does not supply Accord's leaderless protocol or its latency properties. |\n\n## Existing reusable components\n\nThe project already depends on `doublets` / `Platform.Data.Doublets` for raw\nlinks, allocation, uniqueness, and cascade policies. Its storage traits and\n`INamedTypesLinks` are extension seams. `FileTransitionLog`, advisory locks,\nTCP `RemoteLinks`, and the JS client transport contract should be reused.\nThe optional staged layer can compose validation, history, and replication\nwithout imposing their allocations or I/O on a bare in-memory cache.\n\nFor production consensus, existing maintained implementations such as\n[etcd/raft](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft),\n[OpenRaft](https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft), and\n[DotNext Raft](https://dotnet.github.io/dotNext/features/cluster/raft.html)\nprovide election and log-replication machinery. They are not interchangeable\nwith a replica acknowledgement counter. JavaScript's client transport should\nadvertise backend guarantees rather than inventing them client-side.\n\n## Source observations, pinned for reproducibility\n\nSource was downloaded through GitHub's contents API; the functions below were\nread. Line numbers apply to these commits. Design observations were reused;\nno competitor implementation was copied.\n\n| Repository / commit | Observed code | Consequence for this implementation |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `sqlite/sqlite` `c6536c6e60dfa0cc6b07e4458df374aaaf1dcdce` | `src/wal.c:4285–4325`, `walFrames`, gates commit syncing on synchronization flags, pads sectors when required, and returns synchronization errors. | Flush is an explicit commit boundary. The staged log is authoritative, so no data checkpoint gets ahead of the journal. It adds no automatic scheduling or InnoDB page WAL.\nPage WAL/doublewrite repair, Dynamo anti-entropy and Accord remain unfinished\nwithin the issue's broad strategy request. The existing checksummed journals,\nexplicit flushes, outcome discovery and atomic catalog each supply narrower guarantees.\nThey are reusable seams for further work, not evidence that the other algorithms\nor their performance have been reproduced. MySQL's durability also depends on\n[storage honoring flushes](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/innodb-init-startup-configuration.html);\na killed-process recovery test cannot establish real power-loss behavior.\n\n## Ordinary-store undo barrier audit (2026-10-25)\n\nRe-read SQLite's [atomic commit ordering](https://www.sqlite.org/atomiccommit.html)\nand [rollback/hot journals](https://www.sqlite.org/lockingv3.html), then inspected\n`src/pager.c` at the same pinned `c6536c6e60dfa0cc6b07e4458df374aaaf1dcdce`\ncommit used above. [`pager_write`, lines 6110–6189](https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/blob/c6536c6e60dfa0cc6b07e4458df374aaaf1dcdce/src/pager.c#L6110)\njournals original page contents before setting the writable flag; the sector\nvariant journals co-resident pages. [`syncJournal`, lines 4340–4445](https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/blob/c6536c6e60dfa0cc6b07e4458df374aaaf1dcdce/src/pager.c#L4340)\npropagates synchronization errors; commit phase one syncs the journal before\nwriting dirty pages (line 6674). The downloaded `pager.c` has SHA-256\n`96d7bb9c4a5a6da0909ce0ab4714311e1ffa5f13007dc4c69f028a2760104ba4`.\nA callback after mutation cannot substitute for this pre-effect boundary.\n\nOur adapter has logical row enumeration/replay, without pager hooks controlling\nall underlying page writes. The selected logical undo image uses those existing\nseams and verifies complete restoration. It adds full-store capture and per-write\nreconciliation costs; it does not implement SQLite's page/sector protocol.\nPhysical torn-page recovery and efficient page undo remain separate open work.\nSee [configuration, assumptions and costs](../../TRANSACTION-UNDO.md) and\n[the row-barrier plan](ROW-WAL-PLAN.md). Existing\njournals reopen under either choice. During shared recovery, the full decoded\nrevision is compared with the preceding revision; unchanged entries reuse its\nroot paths. Recovery still reads, decodes and compares complete revisions.\n\nHistory retention and active snapshot pinning remain separate choices. A\nread-only commit publishes no new root. Rollback discards the candidate. A\nfailed append or flush preserves previously pinned snapshots and fences the\nengine until reopening discovers the journal's actual committed prefix.\n\nEach branch selects its own representation. Forking between shared engines can\nretain the existing root; a fork to the other representation converts the rows.\nMerge applies changed rows to the parent's selected map. Branch conflict checks,\nallocator recovery, saved merge bases and constraints retain their existing\nbehavior. Group preparation uses the same choice for every accepted revision,\nwhile retaining separate outcomes and the shared flush boundary.\n\nRust `Snapshot.get` and `Snapshot.iter` borrow entries directly. `Snapshot.links`\nallocates the returned link vector. The existing `Snapshot.rows() -> &BTreeMap`\nAPI remains available: the first call on a shared snapshot materializes O(N)\nrows and names, cached for that snapshot and its clones. Mutated candidates have\ntheir own empty cache. Internal engine reads, validation, encoding, recovery,\nbranch operations and WASM export use borrowed iteration and do not request this\ncompatibility map. Use `iter` for allocation-sensitive native consumers.\n\nC# `EngineSnapshot.Rows` keeps its `IReadOnlyDictionary` interface. Shared\nsnapshots expose an immutable sorted dictionary; its `SetItem` and `Remove`\nmethods return separate dictionaries. Flat snapshots retain a read-only wrapper.\nJS snapshots are serialized values and retain their existing boundary copies.\n\n## Selected costs\n\nLet N be the number of rows, W the staged writes, H retained revisions, and B\nthe encoded row/name bytes. These costs describe the in-memory map; the complete\njournal encoder and optional constraints have their own costs.\n\n| Operation | Flat, default | Shared, selected |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Snapshot handle / pin | O(1) | O(1) |\n| Candidate root | O(N) row copies | O(1) root sharing |\n| Apply W writes to candidate | O(W log N) | O(W log N) path copies and changed entries |\n| Scan / name lookup | Copies a complete candidate, then scans | Shares a root, overlays W writes, then scans |\n| Retain H small-edit revisions | Up to O(HN) map entries | Initial O(N), then O(W log N) additional paths per revision |\n| Encode a committed revision | O(B) | O(B) |\n| Recover a revision | Complete decode | Complete decode/comparison plus changed paths |\n| First native Rust `rows()` | Existing borrowed map | O(N) compatibility copy, including row names |\n\nRust uses the maintained MIT-licensed `rpds` ordered Arc-based map. Unchanged\nentries retain their allocation identities. C# uses .NET's immutable sorted\ndictionary; frozen AVL nodes share unchanged subtrees, and strings remain\nimmutable references. Both components use logarithmic tree paths. Shared maps\nadd reference-counted nodes and indirection; for tiny or write-heavy disposable\nstates, the flat choice can be cheaper. No timing advantage is asserted without\na workload measurement.\n\nComplete journal serialization and selected constraint scans remain O(N/B).\nThe delta decorator reduces physical bytes through a complete-record comparison;\nit does not turn this engine into a page WAL or LSM tree. A primary loss can lose uncopied commits. |\n| Synchronous copies | Replicated log, acknowledgements k including primary | Commit waits for primary and enough successful follower flushes. Failure can leave a committed primary or partial set of copies; outcome discovery is mandatory. |\n| Serializable independent point edits | Select `SerializableValidation::ReadSet` / `SerializableValidation.ReadSet` / `serializableValidation: 'read-set'` | Track observed addresses and validate concurrent changes at commit; scans still check the whole revision. [Recipe and costs](ENGINE-VALIDATION.md). |\n| Localized journal edits | Optional `DeltaLog` / `DeltaCommitLog` around the selected log | Store a checksummed changed span between periodic full checkpoints; complete encoding and replay remain O(N). See [format, composition and examples](ENGINE-DELTA.md). |\n| Retain small-edit immutable states | Select shared state independently of the other options | Path-copy changed entries instead of cloning a complete row map. Full revision encoding remains; see [costs and examples](ENGINE-SHARED-STATE.md). |\n| Independent commits sharing a flush | Opt-in `commit_group` / `CommitGroup` / `commitGroup` | Preserve each accepted session's revision and share one durability boundary. [Ownership, failure outcomes and costs](ENGINE-GROUP-COMMIT.md). |\n\n`supports_durable_flush` / `SupportsDurableFlush` / `supportsDurableFlush` is\nan adapter contract. Memory logs declare false. An unknown adapter defaults to\nfalse in Rust; explicit durability requirements reject it. A durable external\nadapter must actually flush its storage before returning. Replicated durability\nrequires durable primary and, conservatively, every eligible follower when\nmore than one acknowledgement is requested. A copy count alone says nothing\nabout independent failure domains, fencing, power-loss protection, or elections.\n\n## Concurrency and isolation\n\nOptimistic admission permits multiple sessions. Validation and publication use\none engine mutex, so two commits cannot validate the same state concurrently.\nExclusive admission fails immediately when another session is active; rollback,\ndrop/dispose, and completed attempts release admission. A session belongs to\none caller; share engine handles between threads instead of sharing a session.\n\nOptional [pessimistic point writes](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md) reserve written addresses\nand reject competing writes before staging. Independent addresses remain concurrent;\nisolation and serializable validation remain separately selected. Cluster engines\nreject this local-only strategy.\n\n| Isolation | Reads | Conflict checks |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Read committed | Each operation sees current committed state plus its own writes | A written address changed after begin aborts. Reads can change and scans can gain rows. |\n| Snapshot | Begin-time immutable state plus own writes | Same write/write check. Disjoint write skew is allowed. |\n| Serializable, revision validation (default) | Begin-time immutable state plus own writes | Any intervening database revision aborts the session, including scans and read-only commits. This conservative check prevents predicate anomalies but can abort unrelated work. |\n\nOptional serializable read-set validation accepts disjoint point reads/writes while\nchecking their observed addresses, including missing rows. Scans and name searches\nstill check the whole revision. It requires serializable isolation; default\nrevision validation is unchanged. See [configuration and tradeoffs](ENGINE-VALIDATION.md).\n\nThere are no dirty reads or dirty writes between sessions of the same engine.\nThese properties do not apply to independent writers or direct mutation of an\nadapter behind the engine. Retry conflicts with a **new** session. A failed\ncommit attempt closes its session and discards its staged writes. Allocations\ncan leave gaps after rollback. An optional references, unique pairs or unique\nnames constraint validates the whole proposed state at commit. Raw mutation\nnever silently merges duplicate pairs or cascades deletes: select an existing\nusages/uniqueness decorator if that policy is wanted. Legacy CLI backends retain\ntheir established merge and cascading behavior.\n\n## Commit, recovery and errors\n\nA write commit encodes the complete next revision, appends its record, flushes\nthe log, then publishes the immutable state. The log is authoritative; there\nis no separately acknowledged data checkpoint. This avoids mixed mapped data\nand journal visibility. Full revision records are deliberately simple, not a\nspace-efficient WAL implementation. The optional [delta journal](ENGINE-DELTA.md)\ncompresses physical records without changing this logical commit boundary.\n\nAn append or flush error is an **indeterminate commit**: data may have reached\nthe log even if the caller got an error. The engine then rejects further\nwrites and engine snapshots. Close/reopen using the same authoritative log to\ndiscover the outcome. Do not blindly retry an uncertain business operation;\nuse an application idempotency key or inspect recovered state first. JS reports\n`LinksError.outcome === 'unknown'`; validation conflicts are `failed`.\nReplication does not change these rules. Followers can contain an unacknowledged\ncommit and must not be promoted automatically.\n\nThe exclusive file adapters discard an incomplete final line on open and before\nread, append or flush after a writer I/O error. Failed repair keeps further\noperations fenced until repair succeeds. Complete records remain intact, even\nwhen an error followed their write; this does not authorize retrying an uncertain\nbusiness operation. A repair scans backwards with an 8 KiB buffer. Successful\noperations only check a flag, with no rescan. C# disables its managed write\nbuffer so failed buffered bytes cannot reappear during repair; append therefore\nperforms a file write immediately. These costs belong to the selected file log.\nComplete corrupt records are rejected. Recovery checks checksum, UTF-8 names,\naddress bounds, unique addresses, contiguous revisions, nondecreasing allocator\nand selected constraints.\nChecksums detect accidental corruption, not malicious tampering. Establish the\ndatabase directory and protect its metadata before depending on power-loss\nrecovery. Filesystem/device failure outside the adapter's flush contract is not\nproven by ordinary process crash tests.\n\nThe legacy transaction decorators have a different architecture: their commit\nmarker is flushed before acknowledging commit, data is flushed before an applied\nmarker, and replay errors propagate. They still mutate the underlying store\nwhile a transaction is open; use the staged engine for session isolation.\nTheir complete journal records undo and version ordinary named writes, including\nunique-name moves and names removed by deletion. Name-only versions, archive\nreplay and movement recovery use the complete payload; row-only snapshots retain\ntheir original API. See [transaction names](TRANSACTION-NAMES.md) for codecs,\nreader compatibility, named-adapter requirements and the cost of sidecar scans\nand pre-effect journal flushes. Staged sessions include names in atomic revisions.\nSized and chunked retention discard completed rollback records without replaying\ntheir writes. Chunk archives contain committed changes only; pending records\nremain in the live log. Live C# retention checkpoints current inline effects\nwhen an older committed record lacks an applied marker, preserving newer edits.\nRetention limits the in-memory list, while the durable\nsidecar still keeps recovery markers. Optional diagnostic I/O failures preserve\nthe operation's outcome; storage and journal errors retain their error semantics.\n\nLegacy Rust transaction IDs exclude every recovered commit and abort decision,\neven if the wall clock repeats after a process restart. Explicit and automatic\nowners use the same allocation check. It uses the existing decision hash sets:\nexpected O(1) per candidate, with O(K) extra candidates when a restarted counter\nmeets K historical IDs at the same timestamp. The counter advances as collisions\nare skipped; no database scan, extra retained index or random dependency is added.\nThese are journal-local identities. This check does not repair older journals\nalready containing reused IDs or conflicting decisions.\n\nNative chunk archives claim a previously absent path atomically. Rust advances\nits candidate counter and retries occupied names, including existing symlinks;\nK collisions cost O(K) additional opens without scanning the directory. Other\nfilesystem errors retain committed cleanup for retry. C# uses random GUID names\nand exclusive creation too; a rejected optional archive leaves its records in\nthe live log, with a new candidate on a later retention attempt. Existing entries\nand symlink targets remain untouched. Both adapters keep the live journal as\nrecovery authority. Archive contents are not atomically published after a partial\nwrite, and these checks do not establish archive power-loss durability. Native\nfilesystem archives are unavailable in the linked WASM backend.\n\nLegacy Rust/C# transaction wrappers retain observed partial writes when a storage\noperation fails. Automatic operations undo those observations; explicit\ntransactions keep them for caller rollback. This requires the adapter's change\ncallbacks. Rust panic unwinding and unobserved mutations are outside this contract.\n\nPublic `ApplyTransition`/`RevertTransition` helpers (Rust `apply_transition`/\n`revert_transition`) also reject a live owner before touching data. (The SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to specify a different default.) Applications using WAL do not have to do anything in order for these checkpoints to occur. But if they want to, applications can adjust the automatic checkpoint threshold. Or they can turn off the automatic checkpoints and run checkpoints during idle moments or in a separate thread or process.\n\n## 2.2. Concurrency\n\nWhen a read operation begins on a WAL-mode database, it first remembers the location of the last valid commit record in the WAL. The wal-index greatly improves the performance of readers, but the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the same machine. This is why the write-ahead log implementation will not work on a network filesystem.\n\nWriters merely append new content to the end of the WAL file. Because writers do nothing that would interfere with the actions of readers, writers and readers can run at the same time. However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time.\n\nA checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file and transfers it back into the original database file. A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader. The checkpoint has to stop

[2026-10-25T16:49:55.934Z] [STDERR] ## Composition and compatibility
[2026-10-25T16:49:55.936Z] [STDERR] Both representations write the same complete `engine1` revisions. Existing
[2026-10-25T16:49:55.938Z] [STDERR] journals reopen under either choice. During shared recovery, the full decoded
[2026-10-25T16:49:55.940Z] [STDERR] revision is compared with the preceding revision; unchanged entries reuse its

Reopening accepts any valid mix of\ncheckpoints and deltas, independently of the newly selected interval.\n\nCompose `Engine(Delta(Replicated(primary, followers)))` to compress once and\nreplicate identical physical bytes. Alternatively,\n`Engine(Replicated(Delta(primary), [Delta(follower)]))` compares logical prefixes\nand lets each physical log choose its checkpoint interval independently. Both\norders retain the replication decorator's acknowledgement and failure semantics.\nOne writer must own and fence each physical log. Durability capability passes\nthrough unchanged; the decorator adds no flush or ownership mechanism. Cluster\njournal stores use a different atomic multi-key interface, and cannot be wrapped\nby this single-stream adapter.\n\nAlways reopen a physical delta stream **through the decorator**. A raw engine\nrejects its delta records. Append or flush errors fence the decorator: the write\nmay have happened, so create a fresh decorator and engine over the same physical\nlog to discover the outcome. Complete corrupt records fail closed. A failed\nreread requires successful revalidation before another append. File adapters\nretain their existing incomplete-final-line repair. Checksums detect accidental\ncorruption and do not authenticate writers.\n\n## Portable physical format\n\nThe [independently generated vectors](protocol/engine-delta-vectors.json) are\nconsumed by native Rust, C#, JS unit tests and actual Rust/WASM integration.\nFull checkpoints use canonical `engine1` records: decimal fields have no leading\nzeros, and checksums are lowercase. Existing engines emit this representation;\nthe decorator rejects noncanonical forms even where a legacy full-record decoder\ncould accept them. A delta is:\n\n```text\ndelta1|BASEHASH|REVISION|NEXT|PREFIX|SUFFIX|MIDDLE|NEWHASH|CHECKSUM\n```\n\nAll characters must be printable ASCII. `BASEHASH` is the immediately preceding\nlogical full record's 16-digit lowercase FNV-1a-64 checksum. `REVISION` is a\npositive u64 and `NEXT` a positive u128, both canonical decimal. `PREFIX` and\n`SUFFIX` are canonical unsigned u32 decimals describing nonoverlapping spans\nof the preceding full record's **row payload**, excluding its envelope. Name\npayloads are already UTF-8 hex, so byte and character offsets coincide.\nReconstruct the new row payload as old prefix + `MIDDLE` + old suffix.\n`NEWHASH` must verify the reconstructed\n`engine1|REVISION|NEXT|ROWS` record. `CHECKSUM` is lowercase FNV-1a-64 over every\npreceding field and separator in the physical delta. Validate the envelope and\nspan bounds before slicing. The first logical revision is 1; subsequent revisions\nmust increase by exactly one. The engine also validates rows, allocator\nmonotonicity, address range and configured constraints.\n\n## Costs and runnable evidence\n\nCompression scans the old and new row payloads for the longest common prefix,\nthen a nonoverlapping common suffix, capped at u32 spans. It retains one full\nrecord and constructs one candidate delta: O(N) time and transient space. The\nengine still encodes full states; optional [shared state](ENGINE-SHARED-STATE.md)\navoids the default full row-map cloning. Reading expands every retained revision\nand remains O(total logical history); checkpointing does not compact history or\nimplement an LSM tree. [2026-10-25T16:51:55.688Z] [STDERR] +# Incremental logical revision records
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.693Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.700Z] [STDERR] +`RevisionEncoding::Changes` (Rust), `RevisionEncoding.Changes` (C#), and
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.707Z] [STDERR] +`revisionEncoding: 'changes'` (JS/TS/WASM) select canonical `engine2` records.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.708Z] [STDERR] +The default `Snapshot` / `snapshot` still emits complete `engine1` records.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.710Z] [STDERR] +This setting is independent of state structure, isolation, validation, history,
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.712Z] [STDERR] +constraints, admission and physical log decorators. Readers accept mixed streams
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.713Z] [STDERR] +regardless of the encoding selected for following commits.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.714Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.717Z] [STDERR] +```text
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.719Z] [STDERR] +engine2|REVISION|BASE|NEXT|OPERATIONS|CHECKSUM
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.720Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.721Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.722Z] [STDERR] +`REVISION` and `BASE` are u64; `NEXT` is a positive u128 allocator high-water
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.724Z] [STDERR] +mark. All numbers use ASCII decimal without signs, whitespace or leading zeros
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.725Z] [STDERR] +(except the number zero). `BASE` must equal the preceding revision and
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.726Z] [STDERR] +`REVISION` must equal `BASE + 1`, without overflow. The initial predecessor is
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.726Z] [STDERR] +empty revision zero with allocator one. `NEXT` cannot decrease. It can exceed
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.727Z] [STDERR] +the consumer's address width: opening an exhausted allocator is permitted,
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.728Z] [STDERR] +while creating an out-of-range address fails. Existing addresses remain editable.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.729Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.733Z] [STDERR] +`OPERATIONS` is empty or a semicolon-separated list, sorted strictly by address:
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.735Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.742Z] [STDERR] +| Operation | Meaning |
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.746Z] [STDERR] +| --- | --- |
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.749Z] [STDERR] +| `+ID,SOURCE,TARGET,NAME` | Insert or replace the complete row and optional name |
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.752Z] [STDERR] +| `-ID` | Delete an existing row, including its name |
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.756Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.759Z] [STDERR] +Addresses must fit the consumer's unsigned link type. `ID` is nonzero and less
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.761Z] [STDERR] +than `NEXT`; sources and targets may be zero or external addresses unless a
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.765Z] [STDERR] +selected constraint disallows them. `NAME` is lowercase hexadecimal of valid
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.771Z] [STDERR] +UTF-8, with `-` for no name and an empty field for the empty name. This preserves
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.776Z] [STDERR] +delimiters, Unicode, NUL and newlines without physical record separators.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.778Z] [STDERR] +Duplicate/unsorted IDs, unknown operations, missing/extra fields, unchanged puts
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.782Z] [STDERR] +and absent tombstones are invalid. Encoders omit operations whose final row is
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.783Z] [STDERR] +identical to the preceding row. An empty operation list is valid: accepted
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.784Z] [STDERR] +identical-result writes and transient create/delete activity can still advance
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.787Z] [STDERR] +the revision or allocator. A read-only transaction still emits no record.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.792Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.794Z] [STDERR] +`CHECKSUM` is exactly sixteen lowercase hexadecimal digits of FNV-1a-64 over
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.798Z] [STDERR] +all UTF-8 bytes preceding its final separator. It detects accidental corruption,
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.813Z] [STDERR] +not malicious modification. Validate checksum, grammar, progression, address
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.815Z] [STDERR] +bounds and constraints before publishing a candidate. Invalid complete records
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.817Z] [STDERR] +fail closed without rewriting the supplied journal. File adapters retain their
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.818Z] [STDERR] +separate incomplete-final-line repair contract.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.820Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.822Z] [STDERR] +Recovery applies changes against the exact preceding state. Shared state clones
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.823Z] [STDERR] +its immutable root and applies changed paths, without first decoding a full flat
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.824Z] [STDERR] +map. Flat state retains its complete candidate-copy cost. Standalone branch
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.828Z] [STDERR] +merge-base exports remain `engine1` images; a dependent `engine2` record cannot
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.830Z] [STDERR] +serve as a saved base. Branch resume replays either format to attribute an
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.831Z] [STDERR] +evicted base before accepting the branch.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.832Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.833Z] [STDERR] +The physical delta decorator passes `engine2` records through unchanged and
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.834Z] [STDERR] +resets its complete-image compression chain. A following `engine1` record starts
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.837Z] [STDERR] +a new chain; a physical `delta1` cannot refer to an `engine2` base. Mixed streams
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.845Z] [STDERR] +retain exact logical records and contiguous revision checks. Older readers
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.852Z] [STDERR] +reject the new mandatory tag; reopen with a compatible reader before selecting
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.862Z] [STDERR] +this encoding. A complete `engine1` record inside a stream does not authorize
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.868Z] [STDERR] +discarding its preceding history. There is no journal compaction or checkpoint
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.870Z] [STDERR] +truncation API in this change.
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.875Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.878Z] [STDERR] +[Independent vectors](engine-change-vectors.json) cover valid/mixed streams,
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.887Z] [STDERR] +41 malformed u32 streams, physical delta composition and invalid compression
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.892Z] [STDERR] +bases. They are consumed by Rust, C# and actual WASM, including the public JS
[2026-10-25T16:51:55.916Z] [STDERR] +boundary. This is logical redo over immutable states; page WAL ordering,

[2026-10-25T16:51:56.045Z] [STDERR] +
