Independent application processes select named shards at transaction\nstart, work privately, and publish their changed journals in one atomic compare\nand exchange. Every selected shard's generation is checked, including read-only\nshards. This gives conservative serializable transactions within a selected\ngroup. Select every shard on which an application invariant depends. References\nare local to a shard; application-level cross-shard references include its name.\n\nRust implements `LinksStorage<T>` and `NamedTypeLinks`, C# implements\n`INamedTypesLinks<T>`, and JS returns a `LinksClient` per selected shard. Commit\nbelongs to the containing group. The bare cache and local engine APIs retain\nno network dependency. Network sessions currently support optimistic admission\nand serializable validation; requests for other policies fail explicitly.\n\n## Backends and costs\n\nThe replaceable `AtomicJournalStore` / `IAtomicJournalStore` contract requires\nlinearizable grouped reads, never-reused modification generations, atomic\ncomparison of every selected key, and atomic publication of all changed keys.\nZero denotes an absent key. A custom store must not silently weaken this contract.\nThe supplied `EtcdJournalStore` uses etcd's v3 HTTP JSON gateway. One Txn reads the\ngroup; one Txn validates and publishes. Read failures try each configured endpoint\nonce. A mutation is sent once. No follower-local or stale cached reads are served.\n\nThis backend stores full journals in etcd keys. Transaction start transfers and\nreplays each selected shard's complete journal; commit transfers the complete\nupdated journals. Defaults bound requests to 1 MiB, responses to 8 MiB, selected\nshards to 32, and names to 128 ASCII letters/digits/dots/underscores/dashes. Tune\nbyte bounds together with etcd's server request/quota limits. These limits are\nchecked in addition to engine journal integrity, allocator and constraint checks.\nThis is suitable for small datasets and coordination; it is not a high-throughput\nbulk storage design. One consensus group replicates every journal and limits\naggregate write throughput. More workers and separate shard namespaces spread\nprocessing. Use the optional partitioned decorator below to move journal data\nout of the catalog into independent stores and consensus groups.\n\n## Independent data stores\n\n`PartitionedJournalStore` implements the same atomic journal store contract in\nRust, C# and JS. Supply a catalog, a map of named data stores, and a function\nmapping each shard name to a data-store name. The stores can use separate etcd\ndeployments, disks, memberships and quotas. No application filesystem is shared.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  Workers[Application workers] --> Catalog[Atomic catalog: shard pointers]\n  Workers --> East[East group: immutable journals]\n  Workers --> West[West group: immutable journals]\n  Catalog -. points to .-> East\n  Catalog -. points to .-> West\n```\n\nAt begin, the decorator reads all selected catalog pointers in one linearizable\nsnapshot, then loads their immutable data objects. At commit it creates the\nchanged objects in their routed stores, verifies their complete contents, then\natomically compares every selected catalog generation and publishes the pointers.\nA failed comparison publishes none of the group. A data failure before catalog\npublication leaves only unreferenced objects. An unknown catalog response still\nrequires a fresh read. No data or catalog mutation is automatically retried.\n\nThe portable pointer is four strings: `blob1`, partition name, object key, and\nobject modification generation. Keys use a length-framed UTF-8 FNV-1a-64 index.\nCreation checks full contents and rejects a collision; existing objects are never\noverwritten. Reads verify both generation and index. This detects accidental\ncorruption and namespace misuse; it does not authenticate an untrusted backend.\nCatalog and data namespaces must be dedicated to this protocol. Keep each\npartition name bound to its original storage namespace, even when changing the\nrouter for future writes. Never delete or mutate objects: old readers may still\nhold pointers. This version retains old and orphan objects, so provision quotas\nand monitor growth. No concurrent garbage collector is supplied.\n\nThe catalog carries O(selected shards) bounded metadata per operation. Bulk\njournal writes and storage capacity are distributed across independent data\ngroups; each journal still stores and transfers complete revisions and history.\nCatalog metadata throughput and each individual data group's request/quota limits\nremain constraints. Split unrelated transaction domains into independent catalogs\nto scale metadata throughput; one transaction cannot span independent catalogs.\nThis does not promise linear throughput scaling or provide LSM compaction.\n`requireDurableFlush` requires the catalog and every configured data store to\ndeclare durable persistence. Injected stores remain caller-owned.\n\nFor example, with independent groups on ports 2379 (catalog), 3379 (east) and\n4379 (west), append the two data endpoints to any cluster example:\n\n```sh\ncargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --features etcd --example cluster -- http://localhost:2379 /partitioned/ http://localhost:3379 http://localhost:4379\ndotnet run --project examples/cluster-csharp -- http://localhost:2379 /partitioned/ http://localhost:3379 http://localhost:4379\n```\n\nThe JS constructor accepts the same `EtcdJournalStore` instances:\n\n```js\nconst journals = new PartitionedJournalStore(catalog, { east, west },\n  (shard) => shard === 'a' ? 'east' : 'west');\nconst engine = new ClusterEngine(binding, journals, { requireDurableFlush: true });\n```\n\nThe design follows the general immutable-data/atomic-metadata pattern described\nin [Apache Iceberg's specification](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/). The wire\nformat and engine implementation here are independent of Iceberg's table format.\n\n## Configuration and ownership\n\nRust enables HTTP/TLS dependencies only with Cargo feature `etcd`.\n`EtcdJournalStore::with_agent` accepts a configured `ureq::Agent`; `headers`\naccepts authorization headers. The default agent uses a finite ten-second global\ndeadline, HTTPS root validation and no redirects. Configure private trust roots,\nclient certificates and proxies through the agent. Cluster engines retain their\nstore through an `Arc<Mutex<_>>`; transactions own private engine handles.\n\nC# accepts an optional `HttpClient`, enabling custom TLS, authentication headers\nand proxies. The caller owns an injected client and the journal store; disposing\nthe store disposes only a client it created. `RequestTimeout` bounds the complete\nrequest and streamed response (default ten seconds). Default redirects are disabled.\nCluster transactions are single-threaded and must be disposed. A shared custom\nstore must make its own operations thread-safe.\n\nJS accepts `fetch`, `headers`, `timeoutMs`, `maxRequestBytes` and `maxResponseBytes`.\nThe universal entry point imports no Node APIs; the initialized WASM binding is\nsupplied by the caller. `await using` or `try/finally` closes transactions and frees\nall workspaces. Close waits for an in-flight commit and propagates its outcome.\nThe store remains caller-owned. Browser deployments need appropriate CORS support\nfrom a trusted gateway and must protect credentials.\n\n## Failures and durability\n\nA rejected comparison is a known conflict and publishes none of the group. Each\ncommit attempt ends its transaction. A lost response, HTTP error or malformed\nresponse after sending commit can have an unknown outcome. Open a new transaction\nto discover state; never automatically replay a mutation after an I/O error.\nOrdinary uncommitted disposal publishes nothing. An applied commit can survive a\nlost response; disposal cannot roll it back. Local validation errors occur before\nany coordinator mutation. The local workspaces use volatile journals; the shared\nstore is the durability boundary.\n\n`requireDurableFlush` checks the backend's declared capability. For etcd this\nrequires the operator to retain default durable fsync settings and reliable\nstorage. The adapter cannot verify disks, power-loss protection or a dishonest\ncustom adapter. With a healthy majority, etcd handles leader election and\nmembership; without a majority, fresh linearizable reads and commits fail. Use\netcd's own supported membership and backup/recovery tools, keeping engine keys\nintact. Never expire/delete keys or roll back the coordinator while applications\nare using its generations.\n\n## Reproduce verification\n\nThe [Rust and C# examples](../examples/cluster-csharp/README.md) and\n[JS example](../js/client/examples/cluster.mjs) use the same journal representation.\nThe bounded [integration runner](../experiments/issue-138/etcd-cluster.mjs) launches\na three-member catalog and two independent data groups, uses JS and optional\nnative writers, injects a lost commit response and a data-group outage, kills the\nelected catalog leader, verifies a surviving-majority commit, and then checks\nthat majority loss refuses a fresh read. The transactions layer only needs three things from its log: append\n//! one entry, read every entry back in write order, and make what has\n//! been appended durable. [`TransitionLogStore`] captures exactly that,\n//! so a consumer can plug in whichever log it already has.\n//!\n//! Two implementations ship with the library:\n//!\n//! * [`NamedTypesDecorator`] — the original sidecar *links* log, where\n//!   each entry is the name of a freshly created link. Keeps the log in\n//!   the same format the C# port uses.\n//! * [`FileTransitionLog`] — a plain append-only text file, one entry\n//!   per line, `fsync`ed on every append by default. Cheaper than a\n//!   links database. An incomplete final line is discarded on open or\n//!   before reusing a writer after an I/O error.\n//!\n//! [`TransitionLogStore`] captures exactly that,\n//! so a consumer can plug in whichever log it already has.\n//!\n//! Two implementations ship with the library:\n//!\n//! * [`NamedTypesDecorator`] — the original sidecar *links* log, where\n//!   each entry is the name of a freshly created link. Keeps the log in\n//!   the same format the C# port uses.\n//! * [`FileTransitionLog`] — a plain append-only text file, one entry\n//!   per line, `fsync`ed on every append by default. Cheaper than a\n//!   links database. An incomplete final line is discarded on open or\n//!   before reusing a writer after an I/O error.\n//!\n//! Reading takes `&mut self` because the links-backed log resolves\n//! names through [`NamedTypes::get_name`], which needs mutable access\n//! to its own caches.\n\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse crate::error::LinkError;\nuse crate::named_types::{NamedTypes, NamedTypesDecorator};\n\n/// Append-only store of serialized transitions and recovery markers.\npub trait TransitionLogStore {\n    /// Appends one entry. Entries never contain newlines.\n    fn append_log_entry(&mut self, entry: &str) -> Result<(), LinkError>;\n\n    /// Reads every entry back, oldest first.\n    fn read_log_entries(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<String>, LinkError>;\n\n    /// Makes every appended entry durable.\n    fn flush_log(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError>;\n\n    /// Whether flush requests persistent storage. Custom/volatile logs default\n    /// to false; this describes an adapter, not the reliability of its hardware.\n    fn supports_durable_flush(&self) -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n}\n\nfn storage_error(error: anyhow::Error) -> LinkError {\n    LinkError::StorageError(format!(\"{error:#}\"))\n}\n\nimpl TransitionLogStore for NamedTypesDecorator {\n    fn supports_durable_flush(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.links().database_path().as_os_str().is_empty()\n    }\n    fn append_log_entry(&mut self, entry: &str) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n        // Always allocate a fresh link so entries never overwrite one\n        // another (mirrors C# `CreateAndUpdate(Null, Null)`).\n        let link = self.create(0, 0);\n        self.set_name(link, entry).map_err(storage_error)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn read_log_entries(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<String>, LinkError> {\n        let mut addresses: Vec<u32> = self.all().into_iter().map(|link| link.index).collect();\n        addresses.sort_unstable();\n        let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(addresses.len());\n        for address in addresses {\n            if let Some(name) = NamedTypes::get_name(self, address).map_err(storage_error)? {\n                entries.push(name);\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(entries)\n    }\n\n    fn flush_log(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n        crate::LinksStorage::flush(self)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Append-only, line-oriented transitions log backed by a single file.\n///\n/// # Durability\n///\n/// With `sync_on_append` enabled (the default) every\n/// [`append_log_entry`](TransitionLogStore::append_log_entry) returns\n/// only after the entry has reached stable storage, which is what makes\n/// the write-ahead ordering of the transactions layer meaningful: a\n/// transition is always durable before the data-store write it\n/// describes is reported as committed. Disabling it trades that\n/// guarantee for throughput — the log is then durable only as far as\n/// the last [`flush_log`](TransitionLogStore::flush_log).\n///\n/// An interrupted append can leave a partial final line. Opening the log,\n/// or reading, appending or flushing after a writer I/O error, repairs that\n/// suffix before proceeding. A failed repair is retried on the next operation.\n/// Complete records remain intact, including records written before an error\n/// was returned; callers must discover an uncertain transaction's outcome\n/// rather than blindly retry it. Repair scans backwards with an 8 KiB buffer;\n/// successful operations do not rescan. This framing protocol assumes storage\n/// honors flush and does not prove device-sector atomicity after power loss.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct FileTransitionLog {\n    path: PathBuf,\n    file: File,\n    sync_on_append: bool,\n    tail_may_be_torn: bool,\n    _lock: Option<crate::FileLock>,\n}\n\nimpl FileTransitionLog {\n    /// Opens (creating if needed) the log at `path`, discarding a\n    /// trailing entry left half-written by a crash.\n    pub fn open<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<Self, LinkError> {\n        let path = path.as_ref().to_path_buf();\n        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {\n            if !parent.as_os_str().is_empty() && !parent.exists() {\n                std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;\n            }\n        }\n        // The torn tail is trimmed through a dedicated read/write handle:\n        // Windows grants an append-only handle `FILE_APPEND_DATA` without\n        // `FILE_WRITE_DATA`, so `set_len` on it fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`.\n        let repair = OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create(true)\n            .truncate(false)\n            .open(&path)?;\n        truncate_torn_tail(&repair)?;\n        drop(repair);\n        let file = OpenOptions::new().read(true).append(true).open(&path)?;\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        File::open(\n            path.parent()\n                .filter(|p| !p.as_os_str().is_empty())\n                .unwrap_or(Path::new(\".\")),\n        )?\n        .sync_all()?;\n        Ok(Self {\n            path,\n            file,\n            sync_on_append: true,\n            tail_may_be_torn: false,\n            _lock: None,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Holds the conventional sidecar lock until drop. Contention fails fast;\n    /// all writers must follow the same advisory locking convention.\n    pub fn open_exclusive<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<Self, LinkError> {\n        let lock =\n            crate::FileLock::try_acquire(crate::lock_file_path(&path), crate::LockMode::Exclusive)?\n                .ok_or_else(|| LinkError::Lock(\"journal writer is busy\".into()))?;\n        let mut log = Self::open(path)?;\n        log._lock = Some(lock);\n        Ok(log)\n    }\n\n    // An error may follow successful short writes. Keep the flag until both\n    // truncation and its durable flush succeed, so repeated I/O faults retry.\n    fn repair_if_needed(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n        if self.tail_may_be_torn {\n            let repair = OpenOptions::new().read(true).write(true).open(&self.path)?;\n            truncate_torn_tail(&repair)?;\n            // A previous failed repair may already have changed the length.\n            repair.sync_all()?;\n            self.tail_may_be_torn = false;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Path of the backing file.\n    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.path\n    }\n\n    /// Whether every append is `fsync`ed. Enabled by default.\n    pub fn sync_on_append(&self) -> bool {\n        self.sync_on_append\n    }\n\n    /// Turns per-append `fsync` on or off — see the durability notes.\n    pub fn set_sync_on_append(&mut self, value: bool) {\n        self.sync_on_append = value;\n    }\n}\n\nimpl TransitionLogStore for FileTransitionLog {\n    fn supports_durable_flush(&self) -> bool {\n        true\n    }\n    fn append_log_entry(&mut self, entry: &str) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n        if entry.contains('\\n') || entry.contains('\\r') {\n            return Err(LinkError::InvalidFormat(\n                \"transition log entries must not contain line breaks\".to_string(),\n            ));\n        }\n        self.repair_if_needed()?;\n        self.tail_may_be_torn = true;\n        writeln!(self.file, \"{entry}\")?;\n        self.file.flush()?;\n        if self.sync_on_append {\n            self.file.sync_data()?;\n        }\n        self.tail_may_be_torn = false;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn read_log_entries(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<String>, LinkError> {\n        self.repair_if_needed()?;\n        let mut contents = String::new();\n        File::open(&self.path)?.read_to_string(&mut contents)?;\n        // Only newline-terminated lines were fully written; a trailing\n        // fragment is the torn tail of a crashed append.\n        Ok(contents\n            .lines()\n            .take(contents.matches('\\n').count())\n            .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())\n            .map(|line| line.to_string())\n            .collect())\n    }\n\n    fn flush_log(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n        self.repair_if_needed()?;\n        self.tail_may_be_torn = true;\n        self.file.flush()?;\n        self.file.sync_data()?;\n        self.tail_may_be_torn = false;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Shrinks `file` to its last complete (newline-terminated) line.\n///\n/// A crash can leave the log ending in a fragment of an entry. Appending\n/// after that fragment would concatenate the next entry onto it, turning\n/// one lost transition into two, so the fragment is dropped when the log\n/// is opened or its live writer recovers from an I/O error.\nfn truncate_torn_tail(file: &File) -> Result<(), LinkError> {\n    let len = file.metadata()?.len();\n    if len == 0 {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    let mut file = file;\n    let mut end = len;\n    let mut buffer = [0u8; 8192];\n    while end > 0 {\n        let chunk = std::cmp::min(end, buffer.len() as u64);\n        let start = end - chunk;\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(start))?;\n        let slice = &mut buffer[..chunk as usize];\n        file.read_exact(slice)?;\n        if let Some(offset) = slice.iter().rposition(|byte| *byte == b'\\n') {\n            let complete = start + offset as u64 + 1;\n            if complete != len {\n                file.set_len(complete)?;\n                file.sync_all()?;\n            }\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        end = start;\n    }\n    // No newline anywhere: the whole file is one torn entry.\n    file.set_len(0)?;\n    file.sync_all()?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

[2026-10-25T17:50:28.861Z] [STDERR] +# Optional SQLite page-WAL journal
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.863Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.866Z] [STDERR] +Select SQLite at the existing ordered-log boundary when the staged engine needs
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.867Z] [STDERR] +a physical pager, checksummed page WAL, atomic SQL group commits and explicit
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.871Z] [STDERR] +checkpoint maintenance. The engine still supplies links, names, isolation,
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.873Z] [STDERR] +history, branches and logical revision encoding. The default store adds no
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.875Z] [STDERR] +SQLite provider. This component does not replace legacy mapped Doublets files.
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.879Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.884Z] [STDERR] +| Surface | Selected component | Unselected cost |
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.892Z] [STDERR] +| --- | --- | --- |
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.896Z] [STDERR] +| Rust | `sqlite` feature; `engine::sqlite::SqliteLog`; bundled rusqlite | No SQLite build/dependency |
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.898Z] [STDERR] +| C# | `SqliteCommitLog` takes an opened, dedicated `DbConnection` | Core adds no SQLite NuGet provider |
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.905Z] [STDERR] +| JS/TS | Separate `engine-sqlite-log` entry; synchronous `exec/prepare/all/run/close` connection | Universal entry imports no provider |
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.908Z] [STDERR] +| WASM | Existing JS commit-log bridge, with that JS connection | No bare-WASM filesystem/VFS durability claim |
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.910Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.912Z] [STDERR] +The common [storage protocol](protocol/sqlite-log.md) uses exact schema and
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.913Z] [STDERR] +identity versions, contiguous signed-i64 sequences and strict UTF-8 BLOBs.
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.915Z] [STDERR] +Empty strings, NUL, leading U+FEFF, Unicode and protocol delimiters round-trip.
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.917Z] [STDERR] +Malformed UTF-8, unpaired UTF-16 and physical CR/LF reject. SQLite record sequence
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.918Z] [STDERR] +numbers are independent of engine revision/address widths. Independent
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.920Z] [STDERR] +[vectors](protocol/sqlite-log-vectors.json) specify bytes and invalid controls.
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.922Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.924Z] [STDERR] +## Selecting the component
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.925Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.927Z] [STDERR] +```rust
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.929Z] [STDERR] +use link_cli::engine::sqlite::{SqliteLog, SqliteOptions};
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.932Z] [STDERR] +use link_cli::engine::{Engine, EngineOptions};
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.936Z] [STDERR] +let journal = SqliteLog::open("engine.db", SqliteOptions::default())?;
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.938Z] [STDERR] +let engine = Engine::<u64, _>::open(journal, EngineOptions {
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.941Z] [STDERR] +    require_durable_flush: true,
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.945Z] [STDERR] +    ..Default::default()
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.948Z] [STDERR] +})?;
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.952Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.954Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.957Z] [STDERR] +Enable Cargo feature `sqlite`. Rust owns its connection and rolls pending records
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.960Z] [STDERR] +back on drop. The native module is excluded from `wasm32` builds.
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.962Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.965Z] [STDERR] +```csharp
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.967Z] [STDERR] +using var connection = new Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteConnection(
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.971Z] [STDERR] +    "Data Source=engine.db;Pooling=False;Default Timeout=1");
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.973Z] [STDERR] +connection.Open();
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.979Z] [STDERR] +using var journal = new SqliteCommitLog(connection);
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.984Z] [STDERR] +var engine = new LinksEngine<ulong>(journal,
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.987Z] [STDERR] +    new() { RequireDurableFlush = true });
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.989Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.991Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.995Z] [STDERR] +The application selects its C# provider. The log takes ownership of the already
[2026-10-25T17:50:28.998Z] [STDERR] +open connection, including disposal on failed construction. Use a dedicated
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.009Z] [STDERR] +connection without an existing SQL transaction; do not mutate it externally.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.014Z] [STDERR] +Examples/tests disable pooling so disposal releases database files on every OS.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.015Z] [STDERR] +Every explicit command has a positive finite `CommandTimeoutSeconds` (default
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.016Z] [STDERR] +one). Microsoft.Data.Sqlite has its own busy/locked retries; zero command timeout
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.017Z] [STDERR] +means unlimited retries and is rejected. Custom SQLite busy waits are separately
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.019Z] [STDERR] +finite. These are component retry limits, without a hard scheduler deadline.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.020Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.022Z] [STDERR] +```js
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.023Z] [STDERR] +import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite';
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.025Z] [STDERR] +import { SqliteCommitLog } from '@link-foundation/link-cli-client/engine-sqlite-log';
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.027Z] [STDERR] +using journal = new SqliteCommitLog(new DatabaseSync('engine.db'));
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.028Z] [STDERR] +using engine = new WasmEngine(binding, { requireDurableFlush: true }, journal);
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.030Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.033Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.035Z] [STDERR] +Bun can pass `new (await import('bun:sqlite')).Database(path)`; Deno uses its
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.042Z] [STDERR] +`node:sqlite` compatibility module. The adapter imports neither provider. It
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.046Z] [STDERR] +requires synchronous statements with positional BLOB and BigInt bindings. A
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.051Z] [STDERR] +runtime SQLite version check rejects versions below 3.51.3, including an older
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.053Z] [STDERR] +system SQLite selected by a runtime. Core Node compatibility remains separate
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.055Z] [STDERR] +from the Node version/provider needed for this optional entry.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.058Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.060Z] [STDERR] +## Commit, recovery and maintenance
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.069Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.071Z] [STDERR] +First append starts `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and checks the cached expected tail while
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.075Z] [STDERR] +holding SQLite write ownership. Subsequent appends share the SQL transaction.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.078Z] [STDERR] +`Read` sees the owner's pending records; independent readers see committed
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.080Z] [STDERR] +records. `Flush` issues one SQL COMMIT for a pending group, with WAL/FULL checked
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.082Z] [STDERR] +before publication. An empty flush makes no durability request. Closing rolls
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.083Z] [STDERR] +pending appends back; it does not silently commit them.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.087Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.088Z] [STDERR] +SQLite's writer lock is held over a pending group, not the lifetime of an engine.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.090Z] [STDERR] +One engine must coordinate live sessions and immutable state. A second cached
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.097Z] [STDERR] +owner that observes a changed tail fails and fences itself. This is not a
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.100Z] [STDERR] +distributed engine, automatic cache refresh or cross-engine MVCC. Direct
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.105Z] [STDERR] +external mutation of the owned connection/table violates ownership.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.109Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.111Z] [STDERR] +Component I/O, malformed read data and stale ownership fence subsequent reads,
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.114Z] [STDERR] +appends, flushes and maintenance. A failed COMMIT may already have committed;
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.115Z] [STDERR] +best-effort rollback releases any remaining transaction without erasing committed
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.116Z] [STDERR] +rows. Close and reopen to discover the exact committed prefix before deciding
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.117Z] [STDERR] +whether to retry. Pure invalid append input and pending-checkpoint rejection do
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.119Z] [STDERR] +not poison an otherwise usable writer. A failed JS/C# provider close can be
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.120Z] [STDERR] +retried. No SQLite error is silently converted into a successful commit.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.121Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.123Z] [STDERR] +| Option/operation | Default and cost |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.127Z] [STDERR] +| --- | --- |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.129Z] [STDERR] +| Busy timeout | Rust/JS `0` ms; fail immediately on SQLite contention |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.131Z] [STDERR] +| C# command timeout | `1` second, in addition to provider/SQLite behavior |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.134Z] [STDERR] +| Automatic checkpoint | `1000` WAL pages; zero selects explicit maintenance |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.137Z] [STDERR] +| Open | Validate identity/schema and sequence aggregates, O(H) for H records, without materializing payloads |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.139Z] [STDERR] +| Read | O(H + payload bytes), materializes the journal for the existing engine replay boundary |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.141Z] [STDERR] +| First append | Writer admission plus indexed MAX-tail lookup and payload insertion |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.144Z] [STDERR] +| Following append | Insert into the same SQL transaction; payload/pager costs remain |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.146Z] [STDERR] +| Flush | One pending SQL COMMIT; SQLite determines actual WAL synchronization/checkpoint calls |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.148Z] [STDERR] +| Checkpoint | Work proportional to pages transferred; reader pins can block progress |
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.150Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.153Z] [STDERR] +Rust `checkpoint(CheckpointMode::...)`, C# `Checkpoint(SqliteCheckpointMode...)`
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.156Z] [STDERR] +and JS `checkpoint('passive'|'full'|'restart'|'truncate')` return actual busy,
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.161Z] [STDERR] +log-frame and checkpointed-frame counters. Default is passive. Pending appends
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.167Z] [STDERR] +reject maintenance before SQL I/O. A pinned reader can make truncate report
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.170Z] [STDERR] +busy; release it before retrying. Automatic and explicit checkpoints transfer
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.172Z] [STDERR] +physical pages; neither removes logical journal records. Database/replay costs
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.175Z] [STDERR] +still grow with retained history. Logical compaction is not implemented here.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.181Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.185Z] [STDERR] +WAL/FULL is requested and read back. FULL supplies SQLite's documented commit
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.193Z] [STDERR] +sync behavior only on a filesystem/VFS/device that honors locking and sync.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.197Z] [STDERR] +SQLite WAL requires same-host shared memory; a network filesystem is unsupported.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.202Z] [STDERR] +Keep database sidecars with their owner. Use a consistent SQLite backup procedure
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.205Z] [STDERR] +for a live database; copying only the main file can omit acknowledged WAL data.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.207Z] [STDERR] +This component adds no cross-host database-file protocol.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.208Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.209Z] [STDERR] +## Verification and source reuse
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.211Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.213Z] [STDERR] +The pre-implementation contracts cover all four actual providers. Native tests
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.214Z] [STDERR] +also cover stale/busy owners, pinned readers, setting drift, corrupt schemas and
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.216Z] [STDERR] +sequences, malformed payloads, before/after-COMMIT errors, bounded SQLITE_FULL,
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.217Z] [STDERR] +group pins, replication/delta composition and exact following writes. Each
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.219Z] [STDERR] +native language has forty finite actual process-exit controls across maps,
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.221Z] [STDERR] +logical encodings and physical delta selection. SQL pending groups recover as
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.223Z] [STDERR] +all-or-none. Copied-WAL controls separately compare an intact commit against a
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.225Z] [STDERR] +torn final frame and changed frame checksum, then run quick_check and a following
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.228Z] [STDERR] +commit. These are controlled frame/process tests, not physical power-loss tests.
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.230Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.231Z] [STDERR] +The persistent examples verify exact earlier row/name/revision data while
[2026-10-25T17:50:29.232Z] [STDERR] +Rust -> C# -> Node -> Bun -> Deno reopen the same database. Run

[2026-10-25T17:50:29.243Z] [STDERR] +The JS integration workflow executes the provider and interoperability controls.

[2026-10-25T17:50:53.566Z] [STDERR] ## Choose a configuration
[2026-10-25T17:50:53.569Z] [STDERR] | Scenario | Construction | Acknowledgement and cost |
[2026-10-25T17:50:53.573Z] [STDERR] | --- | --- | --- |
[2026-10-25T17:50:53.581Z] [STDERR] | Disposable cache | Existing bare in-memory links store | No journal, retained snapshots, transaction validation, replica work or disk flush is added. |
[2026-10-25T17:50:53.584Z] [STDERR] | Isolated volatile state | Staged engine + `MemoryLog` / `MemoryCommitLog` | Atomic publication within one engine, rollback, configurable isolation. Process exit loses it. |
[2026-10-25T17:50:53.586Z] [STDERR] | Early point-write conflict detection | Select pessimistic admission | Reserve individual written addresses until session end; competing writes fail immediately. [Configuration and costs](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md). |
[2026-10-25T17:50:53.588Z] [STDERR] | Durable single writer | Staged engine + exclusive file log, require durable flush | One authoritative, checksummed logical revision is appended and flushed before publication. Storage must honor flush; one writer owns the log. |
[2026-10-25T17:50:53.589Z] [STDERR] | Bounded time travel | Set Rust `HistoryPolicy::Last(n)`, C# `HistoryLimit = n`, JS `history: n` | Retain up to n revisions including current. Active sessions and previously returned snapshots pin their versions independently. |

Accord chooses transaction paths using quorum responses, dependencies, timestamps and topology epochs. Our atomic catalog provides one serialization point; it does not supply Accord's leaderless protocol or its latency properties. |\n\n## Existing reusable components\n\nThe project already depends on `doublets` / `Platform.Data.Doublets` for raw\nlinks, allocation, uniqueness, and cascade policies. Its storage traits and\n`INamedTypesLinks` are extension seams. `FileTransitionLog`, advisory locks,\nTCP `RemoteLinks`, and the JS client transport contract should be reused.\nThe optional staged layer can compose validation, history, and replication\nwithout imposing their allocations or I/O on a bare in-memory cache.\n\nFor production consensus, existing maintained implementations such as\n[etcd/raft](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft),\n[OpenRaft](https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft), and\n[DotNext Raft](https://dotnet.github.io/dotNext/features/cluster/raft.html)\nprovide election and log-replication machinery. They are not interchangeable\nwith a replica acknowledgement counter. JavaScript's client transport should\nadvertise backend guarantees rather than inventing them client-side.\n\n## Source observations, pinned for reproducibility\n\nSource was downloaded through GitHub's contents API; the functions below were\nread. [Ownership, failure outcomes and costs](ENGINE-GROUP-COMMIT.md). |\n\n`supports_durable_flush` / `SupportsDurableFlush` / `supportsDurableFlush` is\nan adapter contract. Memory logs declare false. An unknown adapter defaults to\nfalse in Rust; explicit durability requirements reject it. A durable external\nadapter must actually flush its storage before returning. Replicated durability\nrequires durable primary and, conservatively, every eligible follower when\nmore than one acknowledgement is requested. A copy count alone says nothing\nabout independent failure domains, fencing, power-loss protection, or elections.\n\n## Concurrency and isolation\n\nOptimistic admission permits multiple sessions. Validation and publication use\none engine mutex, so two commits cannot validate the same state concurrently.\nExclusive admission fails immediately when another session is active; rollback,\ndrop/dispose, and completed attempts release admission. A session belongs to\none caller; share engine handles between threads instead of sharing a session.\n\nOptional [pessimistic point writes](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md) reserve written addresses\nand reject competing writes before staging. Independent addresses remain concurrent;\nisolation and serializable validation remain separately selected. Cluster engines\nreject this local-only strategy.\n\n| Isolation | Reads | Conflict checks |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Read committed | Each operation sees current committed state plus its own writes | A written address changed after begin aborts. Reads can change and scans can gain rows. |\n| Snapshot | Begin-time immutable state plus own writes | Same write/write check. Disjoint write skew is allowed. |\n| Serializable, revision validation (default) | Begin-time immutable state plus own writes | Any intervening database revision aborts the session, including scans and read-only commits. This conservative check prevents predicate anomalies but can abort unrelated work. |\n\nOptional serializable read-set validation accepts disjoint point reads/writes while\nchecking their observed addresses, including missing rows. Scans and name searches\nstill check the whole revision. It requires serializable isolation; default\nrevision validation is unchanged. See [configuration and tradeoffs](ENGINE-VALIDATION.md).\n\nThere are no dirty reads or dirty writes between sessions of the same engine.\nThese properties do not apply to independent writers or direct mutation of an\nadapter behind the engine. Retry conflicts with a **new** session. A failed\ncommit attempt closes its session and discards its staged writes. Allocations\ncan leave gaps after rollback. An optional references, unique pairs or unique\nnames constraint validates the whole proposed state at commit. Raw mutation\nnever silently merges duplicate pairs or cascades deletes: select an existing\nusages/uniqueness decorator if that policy is wanted. Legacy CLI backends retain\ntheir established merge and cascading behavior.\n\n## Commit, recovery and errors\n\nA write commit encodes the next logical revision, appends its record, flushes\nthe log, then publishes the immutable state. The log is authoritative; there\nis no separately acknowledged data checkpoint. This avoids mixed mapped data\nand journal visibility. Full revision records are deliberately simple, not a\nspace-efficient WAL implementation. The optional [delta journal](ENGINE-DELTA.md)\ncompresses consecutive full snapshots. Optional [change records](ENGINE-CHANGE-RECORDS.md)\nserialize changed rows. Both preserve this logical commit boundary.\n\nAn append or flush error is an **indeterminate commit**: data may have reached\nthe log even if the caller got an error. The engine then rejects further\nwrites and engine snapshots. Close/reopen using the same authoritative log to\ndiscover the outcome. Do not blindly retry an uncertain business operation;\nexclusive admission and optimistic whole-revision serializable validation do not build\nper-row generations. A continuously overlapping set of sessions can still retain\nmany changed addresses; end sessions promptly. Pessimistic admission additionally\ntracks reserved write addresses and generations under all isolation levels; its\n[separate cost description](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md) explains ownership and cleanup.\nRecovery reads the full log; retention bounds in-memory history, not log size.\nOptional single-span delta encoding reduces physical bytes for localized changes\nand adds an O(N) comparison for full records; changes pass through without that\ncomparison. Neither compacts history. Replication catch-up compares prefixes\nand copies missing logical records.\nOptional [caller-selected group commit](ENGINE-GROUP-COMMIT.md) shares one flush\nacross independent sessions while buffering their selected logical records.\nThere is no automatic grouping scheduler or background compaction. These limits\nmatter for a large or frequently written database.\n\n| Competitor configuration | Closest available configuration | Material difference |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| SQLite WAL with synchronous commit | Exclusive file log + staged engine, serializable | Logical snapshot/change records instead of page WAL, conservative validation, no SQLite locking/checkpoint implementation or performance equivalence. |\n| PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED / REPEATABLE READ | Read committed / snapshot | Similar visibility choices; no SQL planner, row locks or PostgreSQL vacuum. |\n| PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE | Serializable revision/read-set validation | Whole-revision scans or point dependencies replace SSI dependency tracking; unrelated predicates can still conflict. |\n| FoundationDB conflict sets | Serializable read-set validation | Local address sets and whole-revision scans; no range index, distributed resolver, snapshot-read bypass or FoundationDB protocol. |\n| RocksDB optimistic transactions | Optimistic admission + snapshot/serializable | No LSM tree, key-range locks, parallel validation, compaction or RocksDB performance parity. |\n| RocksDB pessimistic transactions | Pessimistic point writes + selected isolation | Immediate busy errors, engine-local ownership and snapshot validation; no waiting, deadlock detector, range locks, LSM tree or performance equivalence. |\n| InnoDB synchronous redo/group commit | Durable staged journal + opt-in independent-session group commit | Shared flush with separate revisions; no page WAL, buffer pool, automatic grouping scheduler or doublewrite repair. Full journals in one group limit data/write scale. |\n| TiKV distributed transactions | Selected-shard atomic groups + partitioned journal stores | Independent data groups and atomic catalog publication; no TiKV lock/timestamp protocol, LSM storage or Region rebalancing. |\n| Iceberg optimistic metadata publication | PartitionedJournalStore | Immutable journal objects plus atomic pointer CAS; different data/wire formats, full journal transfers, no manifest tree or garbage collector. |\n\nSee [the pinned source study](case-studies/issue-138/RESEARCH.md),\n[acceptance inventory](case-studies/issue-138/REQUIREMENTS.md), and\n[portable revision vectors](protocol/engine-revision-vectors.json). Independent writes can proceed; a competing write returns busy\nimmediately. See [ownership, retries and costs](../../docs/ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md).\n\n`await engine.commitGroup([first, second])` drains and consumes independent\nsessions, preserving each accepted write's revision while sharing one adapter\nflush. [2026-10-25T18:48:31.971Z] [STDERR] ### 5.4.5. Foreign Keys
[2026-10-25T18:48:31.978Z] [STDERR] A foreign key constraint specifies that the values in a column (or a group of columns) must match the values appearing in some row of another table. We say this maintains the referential integrity between two related tables.
[2026-10-25T18:48:31.982Z] [STDERR] Say you have the product table that we have used several times already:
[2026-10-25T18:48:31.992Z] [STDERR]     CREATE TABLE products (
[2026-10-25T18:48:31.998Z] [STDERR]         product_no integer PRIMARY KEY,
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.001Z] [STDERR]         name text,
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.004Z] [STDERR]         price numeric
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.006Z] [STDERR]     );
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.009Z] [STDERR] Let's also assume you have a table storing orders of those products. We want to ensure that the orders table only contains orders of products that actually exist. So we define a foreign key constraint in the orders table that references the products table:
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.011Z] [STDERR]     CREATE TABLE orders (
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.015Z] [STDERR]         order_id integer PRIMARY KEY,
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.017Z] [STDERR]         product_no integer REFERENCES products (product_no),
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.020Z] [STDERR]         quantity integer
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.023Z] [STDERR]     );
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.024Z] [STDERR] Now it is impossible to create orders with non-NULL `product_no` entries that do not appear in the products table.
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.028Z] [STDERR] We say that in this situation the orders table is the referencing table and the products table is the referenced table. Similarly, there are referencing and referenced columns.
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.029Z] [STDERR] You can also shorten the above command to:
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.032Z] [STDERR]     CREATE TABLE orders (
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.036Z] [STDERR]         order_id integer PRIMARY KEY,
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.038Z] [STDERR]         product_no integer REFERENCES products,
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.039Z] [STDERR]         quantity integer
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.041Z] [STDERR]     );
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.043Z] [STDERR] because in absence of a column list the primary key of the referenced table is used as the referenced column(s).
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.045Z] [STDERR] You can assign your own name for a foreign key constraint, in the usual way.
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.047Z] [STDERR] A foreign key can also constrain and reference a group of columns. As usual, it then needs to be written in table constraint form. Here is a contrived syntax example:
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.048Z] [STDERR]     CREATE TABLE t1 (
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.049Z] [STDERR]       a integer PRIMARY KEY,
[2026-10-25T18:48:32.051Z] [STDERR]       b integer,

Data files and table formats are not copied. |\n| [MySQL/InnoDB redo architecture](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/PAGE_INNODB_REDO_LOG.html), [doublewrite](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/innodb-doublewrite-buffer.html) | [log0write.cc](https://github.com/mysql/mysql-server/blob/561753af986c3c006c4b6c7caa8359748fb55b22/storage/innobase/log/log0write.cc#L1058) | A requested log position, OS-written position and durable position are distinct. Group commit and page repair are separate optional designs, not supplied by revision compression. |\n| [MongoDB write concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern/) | [replication_coordinator_impl.cpp](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/7a45cb24e938fa1a18dad3b1969444d5d80f8d09/src/mongo/db/repl/replication_coordinator_impl.cpp#L2194) | Durable acknowledgements and applied replica state differ. Our fixed-primary log replication does not implement Dynamo repair or timestamp conflict resolution. |\n| [Cassandra 6.0 / Accord](https://cassandra.apache.org/_/events/20261011-community-over-code-glasgow.html) | [transaction dispatch](https://github.com/apache/cassandra/blob/05853eaeab006bd1e834331ac8b1dfdc464d1f31/src/java/org/apache/cassandra/service/StorageProxy.java#L1269), [CoordinateTransaction.java](https://github.com/apache/cassandra-accord/blob/ce855de13902e7e3ebfa4356d265f0c49be1bb8e/accord-core/src/main/java/accord/coordinate/CoordinateTransaction.java#L123) | Current Cassandra includes an Accord route as well as ordinary writes. Accord chooses transaction paths using quorum responses, dependencies, timestamps and topology epochs. Our atomic catalog provides one serialization point; it does not supply Accord's leaderless protocol or its latency properties. |\n\n## Existing reusable components\n\nThe project already depends on `doublets` / `Platform.Data.Doublets` for raw\nlinks, allocation, uniqueness, and cascade policies. Its storage traits and\n`INamedTypesLinks` are extension seams. `FileTransitionLog`, advisory locks,\nTCP `RemoteLinks`, and the JS client transport contract should be reused.\nThe optional staged layer can compose validation, history, and replication\nwithout imposing their allocations or I/O on a bare in-memory cache.\n\nFor production consensus, existing maintained implementations such as\n[etcd/raft](https://github.com/etcd-io/raft),\n[OpenRaft](https://github.com/databendlabs/openraft), and\n[DotNext Raft](https://dotnet.github.io/dotNext/features/cluster/raft.html)\nprovide election and log-replication machinery. They are not interchangeable\nwith a replica acknowledgement counter. JavaScript's client transport should\nadvertise backend guarantees rather than inventing them client-side.\n\n## Source observations, pinned for reproducibility\n\nSource was downloaded through GitHub's contents API; the functions below were\nread. Validation and publication use\none engine mutex, so two commits cannot validate the same state concurrently.\nExclusive admission fails immediately when another session is active; rollback,\ndrop/dispose, and completed attempts release admission. A session belongs to\none caller; share engine handles between threads instead of sharing a session.\n\nOptional [pessimistic point writes](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md) reserve written addresses\nand reject competing writes before staging. Independent addresses remain concurrent;\nisolation and serializable validation remain separately selected. Cluster engines\nreject this local-only strategy.\n\n| Isolation | Reads | Conflict checks |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Read committed | Each operation sees current committed state plus its own writes | A written address changed after begin aborts. Reads can change and scans can gain rows. |\n| Snapshot | Begin-time immutable state plus own writes | Same write/write check. Disjoint write skew is allowed. |\n| Serializable, revision validation (default) | Begin-time immutable state plus own writes | Any intervening database revision aborts the session, including scans and read-only commits. This conservative check prevents predicate anomalies but can abort unrelated work. |\n\nOptional serializable read-set validation accepts disjoint point reads/writes while\nchecking their observed addresses, including missing rows. Scans and name searches\nstill check the whole revision. It requires serializable isolation; default\nrevision validation is unchanged. See [configuration and tradeoffs](ENGINE-VALIDATION.md).\n\nThere are no dirty reads or dirty writes between sessions of the same engine.\nThese properties do not apply to independent writers or direct mutation of an\nadapter behind the engine. Retry conflicts with a **new** session. A failed\ncommit attempt closes its session and discards its staged writes. Allocations\ncan leave gaps after rollback. An optional references, unique pairs or unique\nnames constraint validates the whole proposed state at commit. Raw mutation\nnever silently merges duplicate pairs or cascades deletes: select an existing\nusages/uniqueness decorator if that policy is wanted. Legacy CLI backends retain\ntheir established merge and cascading behavior.\n\n## Commit, recovery and errors\n\nA write commit encodes the next logical revision, appends its record, flushes\nthe log, then publishes the immutable state. The log is authoritative; there\nis no separately acknowledged data checkpoint. This avoids mixed mapped data\nand journal visibility. Full revision records are deliberately simple, not a\nspace-efficient WAL implementation. The optional [delta journal](ENGINE-DELTA.md)\ncompresses consecutive full snapshots. Optional [change records](ENGINE-CHANGE-RECORDS.md)\nserialize changed rows. Both preserve this logical commit boundary.\nThe optional [SQLite journal](ENGINE-SQLITE.md) stores those records inside\nSQLite page-WAL transactions and exposes physical checkpoint maintenance.\n\nAn append or flush error is an **indeterminate commit**: data may have reached\nthe log even if the caller got an error. The engine then rejects further\nwrites and engine snapshots. Close/reopen using the same authoritative log to\ndiscover the outcome. Do not blindly retry an uncertain business operation;\nuse an application idempotency key or inspect recovered state first. JS reports\n`LinksError.outcome === 'unknown'`; validation conflicts are `failed`.\nReplication does not change these rules. Followers can contain an unacknowledged\ncommit and must not be promoted automatically.\n\nThe exclusive file adapters discard an incomplete final line on open and before\nread, append or flush after a writer I/O error. Failed repair keeps further\noperations fenced until repair succeeds. Complete records remain intact, even\nwhen an error followed their write; this does not authorize retrying an uncertain\nbusiness operation. A repair scans backwards with an 8 KiB buffer. Successful\noperations only check a flag, with no rescan. C# disables its managed write\nbuffer so failed buffered bytes cannot reappear during repair; append therefore\nperforms a file write immediately. These costs belong to the selected file log.\nComplete corrupt records are rejected. Recovery checks checksum, UTF-8 names,\naddress bounds, unique addresses, contiguous revisions, nondecreasing allocator\nand selected constraints.\nChecksums detect accidental corruption, not malicious tampering. Establish the\ndatabase directory and protect its metadata before depending on power-loss\nrecovery. Filesystem/device failure outside the adapter's flush contract is not\nproven by ordinary process crash tests.\n\nThe legacy transaction decorators have a different architecture: their commit\nmarker is flushed before acknowledging commit, data is flushed before an applied\nmarker, and replay errors propagate. They still mutate the underlying store\nwhile a transaction is open; use the staged engine for session isolation.\nTheir complete journal records undo and version ordinary named writes, including\nunique-name moves and names removed by deletion. Name-only versions, archive\nreplay and movement recovery use the complete payload; row-only snapshots retain\ntheir original API. Staged sessions include names in atomic revisions.\nSized and chunked retention discard completed rollback records without replaying\ntheir writes. Optional diagnostic I/O failures preserve\nthe operation's outcome; storage and journal errors retain their error semantics.\n\nLegacy Rust transaction IDs exclude every recovered commit and abort decision,\neven if the wall clock repeats after a process restart. Explicit and automatic\nowners use the same allocation check. It uses the existing decision hash sets:\nexpected O(1) per candidate, with O(K) extra candidates when a restarted counter\nmeets K historical IDs at the same timestamp. The admission check\ncosts O(1), with no journal scan or allocation on success.\n\nAfter a legacy journal commit is known durable, a failed synchronous checkpoint\nkeeps the transaction owner and blocks later row and named writes. The C# decorator's `Rollback()` also\nretries an automatic operation's checkpoint. Cleanup finishes the durable\ncommit decision; it cannot undo it. The separate\nretained-journal diff-resolution cost above still applies. Finite stack tests\nuse a metadata-only adapter to isolate traversal; real-name semantic tests\nverify actual native reopenings. WASM controls verify logical behavior without\nclaiming a native stack overflow or filesystem durability there.\n\nRecovery replays the complete committed suffix after its first missing applied\nmarker, including later records that already have markers. It flushes the final\nredo and pending undo before filling that gap, keeping an anchor for another\nrestart if recovery fails before the final data flush.\nBoth Rust and C# reject public recovery while an open transaction owns live\nstate; finish its cleanup first. Bare `ensure_link_created` keeps its existing cost.\n\n## Branches and merge recovery\n\nA fork copies the parent's current committed rows into revision 1 of an empty,\nindependent journal. Choose its concurrency, isolation, constraints and retention\nseparately. Unfinished sessions on either engine remain private. Branch addresses\nare local: independently allocating the same address with different values\ncreates a merge conflict. Equal complete rows converge; no address remapping is\nperformed. Use disjoint address ranges or externally assigned addresses when\nindependent branches must allocate without collisions.\n\nMerge compares each changed complete row with its saved base and the current\nparent. Disjoint changes combine; identical changes converge; divergent edits,\ndelete/update conflicts and name changes to the same row conflict. The parent\nvalidates its constraints and flushes one selected logical revision before publishing any\nmerged rows. Exclusive admission and existing session conflict checks still\napply. Repeating an unchanged successful merge adds no revision. A three-way\nmerge validates its resulting state, but does not retroactively serialize the\nindependent transactions that produced both histories.\n\nAfter a successful merge, persist `merge_base_record()` / `MergeBaseRecord` /\n`mergeBaseRecord()` with application metadata. To reopen, open the same logical\nparent and call `resume_branch` / `ResumeBranch` / `resumeBranch` with the branch\njournal and descriptor. The descriptor contains the complete committed branch\nbase, so in-memory history eviction does not invalidate it. Recovery verifies\nthat it matches an actual branch journal revision and validates the complete\njournal. The caller is responsible for associating it with the right parent;\nthe checksum is not an authenticated lineage identifier.\n\nAn older saved descriptor allows replay after a crash between parent commit and\ndescriptor persistence: already identical rows are accepted, while divergent\noverlap conflicts conservatively. An append/flush error during merge has an\nunknown outcome and poisons the parent; reopen it before outcome discovery or\nretry. Failure to seed a branch leaves the parent untouched, but the branch log\nmay contain the seed and must be inspected/reopened rather than blindly reused.\nFork and merge use the receiving engine's selected flat/shared map and the same\nO(N) record format. Mixed representation forks convert their initial rows.\n\n## Distributed ownership and horizontal scale\n\nReplicated logs have a fixed, externally fenced primary and fixed followers.\nA follower must be an exact prefix of the primary; divergent or ahead followers\nare rejected. Catch-up appends only missing records, then flushes. Scheduling is\nexplicit, so a bare store pays no background replication cost. Adapter resources\nremain owned by the caller; close sessions and engines before releasing them.\n\nA shared-storage deployment must enforce one writer through the file adapter's\nadvisory lock or an external fencing mechanism that every writer respects.\nLocal advisory locks are not a distributed lease and must not be assumed to\nwork on an arbitrary network filesystem. A shared-nothing deployment gives\nindependent logs and failure domains to followers and each independent shard.\nPartition tenants/keys into separate engines to scale aggregate independent\nwork horizontally. Addresses are local to a shard; use `(shard, address)` in\napplication references and keep an atomic transaction within one shard.\n\nSafe automatic primary election, changing membership, consensus, cross-shard\natomic transactions, and a routing/network service are not supplied by these\nlog decorators. They require protocols beyond acknowledgement counting. Existing\n`RemoteLinks` TCP stores carry individual links operations; they do not create a\ntransaction boundary across connections. Do not infer any of those guarantees\nfrom a replicated in-memory test.\n\n## Costs and comparison\n\nThe default flat representation clones current rows for each write commit and\nwrites a complete logical revision. Candidate creation costs O(N); applying W\nwrites costs O(W log N), followed by the selected revision encoding. Flat scans\nmaterialize their view and history can retain O(HN) map entries. Optional\n[shared immutable state](ENGINE-SHARED-STATE.md) replaces those map copies with\nan O(1) root and O(W log N) changed paths, preserving earlier snapshots and\nsharing unchanged entries during recovery. Optional [change records](ENGINE-CHANGE-RECORDS.md)\nserialize changed rows. Selected constraints and scans still visit the full state. The allocator is shared. Optimistic read-committed\nand snapshot sessions, plus serializable read-set sessions, track per-address changes only while another session can\nbe stale, retaining deleted-address tombstones to detect delete/recreate races.\nThe final session validates before reclaiming that map. Opening an engine,\nexclusive admission and optimistic whole-revision serializable validation do not build\nper-row generations. A continuously overlapping set of sessions can still retain\nmany changed addresses; end sessions promptly. Pessimistic admission additionally\ntracks reserved write addresses and generations under all isolation levels; its\n[separate cost description](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md) explains ownership and cleanup.\nRecovery reads the full log; retention bounds in-memory history, not log size.\nOptional single-span delta encoding reduces physical bytes for localized changes\nand adds an O(N) comparison for full records; changes pass through without that\ncomparison. Neither compacts history. Replication catch-up compares prefixes\nand copies missing logical records.\nOptional [caller-selected group commit](ENGINE-GROUP-COMMIT.md) shares one flush\nacross independent sessions while buffering their selected logical records.\nThere is no automatic grouping scheduler or background compaction. These limits\nmatter for a large or frequently written database.\n\n| Competitor configuration | Closest available configuration | Material difference |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| SQLite WAL with synchronous commit | Optional SQLite log + staged engine, selected isolation | Reuses SQLite page WAL/FULL and checkpointing; logical links revisions still replay the retained journal. No SQL planner or independent-engine MVCC/performance equivalence. |\n| PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED / REPEATABLE READ | Read committed / snapshot | Similar visibility choices; no SQL planner, row locks or PostgreSQL vacuum. |\n| PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE | Serializable revision/read-set validation | Whole-revision scans or point dependencies replace SSI dependency tracking; unrelated predicates can still conflict. |\n| FoundationDB conflict sets | Serializable read-set validation | Local address sets and whole-revision scans; no range index, distributed resolver, snapshot-read bypass or FoundationDB protocol. |\n| RocksDB optimistic transactions | Optimistic admission + snapshot/serializable | No LSM tree, key-range locks, parallel validation, compaction or RocksDB performance parity. |\n| RocksDB pessimistic transactions | Pessimistic point writes + selected isolation | Immediate busy errors, engine-local ownership and snapshot validation; no waiting, deadlock detector, range locks, LSM tree or performance equivalence. |\n| InnoDB synchronous redo/group commit | Durable staged journal + opt-in independent-session group commit | Shared flush with separate revisions; optional SQLite supplies its pager/WAL. No InnoDB buffer pool, automatic grouping scheduler or doublewrite repair. Shared state and change encoding independently reduce localized copy/serialization costs. |\n| MongoDB durable write concern | Synchronous durable replica acknowledgements + outcome discovery | No MongoDB election/oplog protocol, tagged concerns or causal replica reads. A lost acknowledgement can follow a committed write. |\n| Cassandra ordinary quorum writes | Fixed-primary synchronous replica log | No leaderless writes, timestamp reconciliation, hints or anti-entropy. Counting replicas does not provide these guarantees. |\n| Cassandra Accord transactions | Selected-shard atomic catalog publication | One catalog serialization point, without Accord's dependency/epoch protocol or WAN latency properties. |\n| Redis asynchronous replication | Async replicated log | Explicit caller scheduling and complete journal prefixes; no Redis network/replication service. |\n| Redis WAIT / WAITAOF style acknowledgement | Synchronous copies with durable adapters | Acknowledgements count flushes according to adapter contract, not consensus or automatic failover. |\n| etcd consensus transactions | ClusterEngine + EtcdJournalStore | Linearizable selected-shard snapshots and atomic CAS; etcd supplies consensus. Full journals in one group limit data/write scale. |\n| TiKV distributed transactions | Selected-shard atomic groups + partitioned journal stores | Independent data groups and atomic catalog publication; no TiKV lock/timestamp protocol, LSM storage or Region rebalancing. |\n| Iceberg optimistic metadata publication | PartitionedJournalStore | Immutable journal objects plus atomic pointer CAS; different data/wire formats, full journal transfers, no manifest tree or garbage collector. |\n\nSee [the pinned source study](case-studies/issue-138/RESEARCH.md),\n[acceptance inventory](case-studies/issue-138/REQUIREMENTS.md), and\n[portable revision vectors](protocol/engine-revision-vectors.json). Tests and\ncoverage evidence must be read at their measured scope; neither a passing suite\nnor a configuration analogy proves every ACID failure mode.\n\n## Run the examples\n\n```sh\ncargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_strategies\ncargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_strategies -- /existing-directory/links.journal\ndotnet run --project examples/engine-csharp -- /existing-directory/links.journal\nwasm-pack build --target web --out-dir ../../js/pkg rust/wasm\nnode js/client/examples/engine.mjs /existing-directory/links.journal\n```\n\nAdd `--read-set` to any of these engine examples to select serializable point\nvalidation and demonstrate two independent edits committing. It composes with\n`--delta`, `--shared`, `--changes`, `--pessimistic` and the optional journal path.\n\nUse a separate journal per simultaneously running writer. To verify portable\nrecovery, stop one example before opening its journal with another language.\nEvery implementation accepts the same `engine1` and selected `engine2` records; u32 consumers reject\naddresses outside their range. C# and Rust support wider unsigned addresses.\n\nThe JS filesystem adapter is imported separately from\n`@link-foundation/link-cli-client/engine-file-log`; the universal browser entry\npoint has no Node imports. It uses an atomic `journal.writer` directory to fence\nwriters. After an abrupt process exit, first verify/fence the old owner and then\nremove that directory explicitly. It deliberately does not guess whether a\nremote owner is dead or automatically break a stale lock. Native file adapters\nuse the existing advisory file-lock implementation, released by the OS at exit.\nThese lock formats differ: a JS writer directory does not fence a native writer's\nadvisory lock. Never open the same journal concurrently through different\nadapters; mixed-language deployments need one externally enforced writer fence.\nReplicas must be independent storage instances and failure domains. C# and JS\nreject repeated object identities, but different wrappers can still alias the\nsame underlying storage; the adapter owner must prevent that aliasing.\n\nJS/WASM custom adapters implement `read(): string` (a JSON array of record\nstrings), `append(record): void`, `flush(): void`, and a boolean\n`supportsDurableFlush`. Append and flush must complete synchronously and return\nundefined. A Promise cannot provide this boundary and is rejected. Browser\nIndexedDB and other asynchronous storage require a server-side engine or a\nseparate asynchronous transaction interface; an exported in-memory journal is\nnot a durable commit. Caller-owned adapters outlive all sessions that use them.\n\n## Coordinated network groups\n\n[ClusterEngine](ENGINE-CLUSTERS.md) composes the same links API with an atomic\njournal store. The optional etcd adapter supplies linearizable snapshots, atomic\npublication across selected shards, and consensus failover. It bounds network\npayloads and preserves unknown outcomes. Full journals in one coordinator group\nlimit scale. `PartitionedJournalStore` moves immutable journals to independently\nrouted data groups and retains atomic pointer publication in the catalog. See the\ndeployment and costs guide for topology, object retention and throughput limits.\n\nC# named, typed and simple file constructors release their owned data handle\nif names construction fails. A failed constructor over a caller-supplied store\nleaves that store usable. Partially initialized names mappings are released on\nboth raw-facade and names-content errors; no GC/finalizer wait is required.\n\nThe legacy transaction decorators retain every observed undo record before\nappending a logical operation's journal batch. An append failure makes an\nexplicit transaction rollback-only: roll it back before writing again. Automatic\noperations attempt rollback immediately. If cleanup fails, the error remains\nvisible and the transaction stays pending; retry `Rollback()` on the C# decorator\nor `rollback()` in Rust after repairing the storage failure. Rust mapped stores\nforward upstream cascade callbacks, including uniqueness merges and dependent\ndeletes. These in-process undo guarantees do not close the legacy crash window\nbetween in-place mutation and its journal append; use the staged engine when\nunpublished mutations must stay outside the authoritative store.\n\nBeginning rollback also makes the legacy transaction rollback-only before any\nundo or persistence step. An error during undo, data flush, rollback-marker append\nor journal flush retains that abort decision. Repair the failure and retry\nrollback; commit and new writes remain rejected until cleanup succeeds.\n\nRust mapped creation also forwards allocation, update and uniqueness callbacks.\nResolving a duplicate can return an existing address after deleting a temporary\nrow; rollback must preserve the existing row and its dependents. A rejected\ncreation can leave an allocated temporary row, so its observations are retained\neven on error. The default `LinksStorage::create_link_observed` is for atomic\nsingle-row creation; adapters with partial writes or cascades must override it.\n\nLegacy signed journal sequence numbers never wrap. Already-exhausted logs reject\nwrites before mutation. If an observed cascade needs more numbers than remain,\nall its undo state stays in pending memory, outside numbered history and the\njournal; automatic operations attempt rollback and explicit transactions require\nrollback. A rejected callback batch does not consume numbers; preparatory\nnested writes may already have consumed valid numbers and are undone with the\noperation. As with other legacy observed writes, this does not close the crash\nwindow before the batch is journaled.\n# Acceptance inventory\n\nNo required sub-issues were returned by GitHub's sub-issue API. [2026-10-25T18:55:05.953Z] [STDERR] +let options = EngineOptions {

[2026-10-25T18:55:05.965Z] [STDERR] +};
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.966Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.967Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.972Z] [STDERR] +```csharp
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.977Z] [STDERR] +var options = new EngineOptions {
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.978Z] [STDERR] +    Constraints = new[] { EngineConstraint.References, EngineConstraint.UniquePairs, EngineConstraint.UniqueNames },
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.982Z] [STDERR] +    ConstraintValidation = ConstraintValidation.Indexed
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.987Z] [STDERR] +};
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.988Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.989Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.990Z] [STDERR] +```js
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.994Z] [STDERR] +const options = {
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.995Z] [STDERR] +  constraints: ['references', 'unique-pairs', 'unique-names'],
[2026-10-25T18:55:05.999Z] [STDERR] +  constraintValidation: 'indexed',
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.000Z] [STDERR] +}; // Pass to WasmEngine, or a cluster's workspace options.
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.005Z] [STDERR] +```
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.009Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.011Z] [STDERR] +Both strategies enforce the same final-state rules. Zero is an absent reference;
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.022Z] [STDERR] +other source/target values must address existing rows. Self-references and cycles
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.023Z] [STDERR] +are valid. Pairs compare both endpoints; names compare exact strings. Missing
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.025Z] [STDERR] +names do not participate; empty names do. Names are not normalized. Neither
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.026Z] [STDERR] +strategy cascades deletions or merges duplicate pairs. If several constraints
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.027Z] [STDERR] +fail, which error is reported first is unspecified.
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.028Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.031Z] [STDERR] +## Algorithm and ownership
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.032Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.037Z] [STDERR] +The engine gate protects validation and publication. Optional persistent ordered
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.039Z] [STDERR] +maps hold pair-to-owner, name-to-owner and address-to-incoming-reference-count
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.042Z] [STDERR] +indexes. Only selected constraints retain a map. The reference count includes
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.047Z] [STDERR] +both endpoint positions, including two occurrences in the same row. Valid bases
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.048Z] [STDERR] +and complete changed-address sets let a deletion detect references from unchanged
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.053Z] [STDERR] +rows without scanning them.
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.054Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.056Z] [STDERR] +A candidate clones index roots, removes all changed old keys, then adds changed
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.061Z] [STDERR] +new keys. This order permits pair swaps and name transfers in one commit. A
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.062Z] [STDERR] +name-only edit reuses the pair/reference roots. Changed rows must reference
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.067Z] [STDERR] +existing final rows; deleted addresses must have zero final incoming count.
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.068Z] [STDERR] +Rejected candidates discard private roots. Journal append and flush precede
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.072Z] [STDERR] +publishing both rows and indexes. Group preparation retains private roots, and
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.073Z] [STDERR] +an uncertain physical write preserves the original committed roots while fencing
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.075Z] [STDERR] +the engine. Reopen discovers the persisted prefix and rebuilds its indexes.
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.078Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.081Z] [STDERR] +Recovery still validates every historical record under the selected constraints;
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.086Z] [STDERR] +a later repair cannot hide an invalid earlier record. Final indexes are built
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.087Z] [STDERR] +once after replay. The wire format does not record this local validation choice,
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.092Z] [STDERR] +so scan and indexed engines can reopen each other's valid journals. Branches
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.093Z] [STDERR] +validate their own configured constraints; parent merge validates the parent's
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.097Z] [STDERR] +constraints. Cluster workspaces retain whole selected-shard generation comparison
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.098Z] [STDERR] +and atomic catalog publication; these local indexes add no distributed locks.
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.101Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.103Z] [STDERR] +## Costs and composition
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.132Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.134Z] [STDERR] +Let N be live rows and W the number of changed addresses. Ordered operations are
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.138Z] [STDERR] +O(log N), with additional string comparison/copy costs for names.
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.140Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.144Z] [STDERR] +| Selection | Work and retained memory |
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.146Z] [STDERR] +| --- | --- |
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.150Z] [STDERR] +| No constraints, either strategy | No index maps or constraint scan |
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.151Z] [STDERR] +| Scan | Visits all rows per selected constraint. Rust uniqueness uses temporary ordered sets; C# uses temporary hash sets. Reference validation uses row lookups. No retained validation index. |
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.156Z] [STDERR] +| Indexed open/replay | Historical complete constraint validation, followed by O(N log N) final index construction |
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.158Z] [STDERR] +| Indexed write | O(W log N) row/index operations and O(W) changed-address buffer, shared with change-record encoding when selected |
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.163Z] [STDERR] +| Indexed retained roots | O(N) entries per selected constraint; pair/name owners and nonzero incoming reference counts; names retain their bytes |
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.164Z] [STDERR] +| Indexed group | Private roots and changed paths per provisional revision, retained until the shared flush result |
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.169Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.170Z] [STDERR] +Rust reuses `rpds::RedBlackTreeMapSync`; C# reuses
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.172Z] [STDERR] +`System.Collections.Immutable.ImmutableSortedDictionary`. Both share unchanged
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.182Z] [STDERR] +nodes. Scan remains useful when retained index memory is undesirable or writes
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.189Z] [STDERR] +already replace most rows. Indexed validation does not remove flat-map candidate
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.198Z] [STDERR] +copies, complete snapshot encoding, branch comparison scans, full journal replay
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.204Z] [STDERR] +or physical I/O. Select shared state and change records separately to reduce
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.205Z] [STDERR] +those two other local commit costs. Retained history and concurrent sessions
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.208Z] [STDERR] +have their existing costs.
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.211Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.213Z] [STDERR] +Run `cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_constraint_cost`
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.220Z] [STDERR] +for a finite allocation example. Eight one-name commits with all constraints,
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.221Z] [STDERR] +shared state and change records request 54,805 versus 17,845 allocation bytes
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.226Z] [STDERR] +at 128 rows, and 329,269 versus 20,117 at 1,024 rows (scan versus indexed in the
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.227Z] [STDERR] +recorded native Debug run). Setup/recovery is excluded. These are allocation
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.246Z] [STDERR] +requests, including reallocations, rather than live memory, timing or durability
[2026-10-25T18:55:06.252Z] [STDERR] +measurements; toolchains can change the exact totals. C# deterministic controls

[2026-10-25T18:55:06.266Z] [STDERR] +
