Zero is an absent reference;\n+other source/target values must address existing rows. Self-references and cycles\n+are valid. Pairs compare both endpoints; names compare exact strings. Missing\n+names do not participate; empty names do. Names are not normalized. Neither\n+strategy cascades deletions or merges duplicate pairs. If several constraints\n+fail, which error is reported first is unspecified.\n+\n+## Algorithm and ownership\n+\n+The engine gate protects validation and publication. Optional persistent ordered\n+maps hold pair-to-owner, name-to-owner and address-to-incoming-reference-count\n+indexes. Only selected constraints retain a map. The reference count includes\n+both endpoint positions, including two occurrences in the same row. Valid bases\n+and complete changed-address sets let a deletion detect references from unchanged\n+rows without scanning them.\n+\n+A candidate clones index roots, removes all changed old keys, then adds changed\n+new keys. This order permits pair swaps and name transfers in one commit. A\n+name-only edit reuses the pair/reference roots. Changed rows must reference\n+existing final rows; deleted addresses must have zero final incoming count.\n+Rejected candidates discard private roots. Journal append and flush precede\n+publishing both rows and indexes. Group preparation retains private roots, and\n+an uncertain physical write preserves the original committed roots while fencing\n+the engine. Reopen discovers the persisted prefix and rebuilds its indexes.\n+\n+Recovery still validates every historical record under the selected constraints;\n+a later repair cannot hide an invalid earlier record. Final indexes are built\n+once after replay. The wire format does not record this local validation choice,\n+so scan and indexed engines can reopen each other's valid journals. Branches\n+validate their own configured constraints; parent merge validates the parent's\n+constraints. Cluster workspaces retain whole selected-shard generation comparison\n+and atomic catalog publication; these local indexes add no distributed locks.\n+\n+## Costs and composition\n+\n+Let N be live rows and W the number of changed addresses. Ordered operations are\n+O(log N), with additional string comparison/copy costs for names.\n+\n+| Selection | Work and retained memory |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| No constraints, either strategy | No index maps or constraint scan |\n+| Scan | Visits all rows per selected constraint. Rust uniqueness uses temporary ordered sets; C# uses temporary hash sets. Reference validation uses row lookups. No retained validation index. |\n+| Indexed open/replay | Historical complete constraint validation, followed by O(N log N) final index construction |\n+| Indexed write | O(W log N) row/index operations and O(W) changed-address buffer, shared with change-record encoding when selected |\n+| Indexed retained roots | O(N) entries per selected constraint; pair/name owners and nonzero incoming reference counts; names retain their bytes |\n+| Indexed group | Private roots and changed paths per provisional revision, retained until the shared flush result |\n+\n+Rust reuses `rpds::RedBlackTreeMapSync`; C# reuses\n+`System.Collections.Immutable.ImmutableSortedDictionary`. Both share unchanged\n+nodes. Scan remains useful when retained index memory is undesirable or writes\n+already replace most rows. Indexed validation does not remove flat-map candidate\n+copies, complete snapshot encoding, branch comparison scans, full journal replay\n+or physical I/O. Select shared state and change records separately to reduce\n+those two other local commit costs. Retained history and concurrent sessions\n+have their existing costs.\n+\n+Run `cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_constraint_cost`\n+for a finite allocation example. Eight one-name commits with all constraints,\n+shared state and change records request 54,805 versus 17,845 allocation bytes\n+at 128 rows, and 329,269 versus 20,117 at 1,024 rows (scan versus indexed in the\n+recorded native Debug run). Setup/recovery is excluded. These are allocation\n+requests, including reallocations, rather than live memory, timing or durability\n+measurements; toolchains can change the exact totals. C# deterministic controls\n+forbid candidate enumeration and bound one-row preparation to seven row lookups\n+at both 8 and 512 rows. Native controls verify unchanged root identity.\n+\n+The SQLite interoperability examples accept `--indexed-constraints`. They select\n+only the references constraint, since successive providers intentionally repeat\n+pairs and names. The workflow runs all sixteen scan/indexed, flat/shared,\n+snapshot/changes and plain/delta compositions, reopening each database through\n+Rust, C#, Node, Bun and Deno. Fresh exact-head CI remains required after\n229:coverage and the remaining distributed/competitor requirements stay unfinished.\n# Optional indexed constraint validation\n\nChoose `Scan` (the default) or `Indexed` independently of constraints, isolation,\nadmission, history, state structure, logical encoding and physical journal:\n\n```rust\nuse link_cli::engine::{Constraint, ConstraintValidation, EngineOptions};\nlet options = EngineOptions {\n    constraints: vec![Constraint::References, Constraint::UniquePairs, Constraint::UniqueNames],\n    constraint_validation: ConstraintValidation::Indexed,\n    ..Default::default()\n};\n```\n\n```csharp\nvar options = new EngineOptions {\n    Constraints = new[] { EngineConstraint.References, EngineConstraint.UniquePairs, EngineConstraint.UniqueNames },\n    ConstraintValidation = ConstraintValidation.Indexed\n};\n```\n\n```js\nconst options = {\n  constraints: ['references', 'unique-pairs', 'unique-names'],\n  constraintValidation: 'indexed',\n}; // Pass to WasmEngine, or a cluster's workspace options.\n```\n\nBoth strategies enforce the same final-state rules. Zero is an absent reference;\nother source/target values must address existing rows. Self-references and cycles\nare valid. Pairs compare both endpoints; names compare exact strings. Missing\nnames do not participate; empty names do. Names are not normalized. Neither\nstrategy cascades deletions or merges duplicate pairs. If several constraints\nfail, which error is reported first is unspecified.\n\n## Algorithm and ownership\n\nThe engine gate protects validation and publication. Optional persistent ordered\nmaps hold pair-to-owner, name-to-owner and address-to-incoming-reference-count\nindexes. Only selected constraints retain a map. The reference count includes\nboth endpoint positions, including two occurrences in the same row. Valid bases\nand complete changed-address sets let a deletion detect references from unchanged\nrows without scanning them.\n\nA candidate clones index roots, removes all changed old keys, then adds changed\nnew keys. This order permits pair swaps and name transfers in one commit. A\nname-only edit reuses the pair/reference roots. Changed rows must reference\nexisting final rows; deleted addresses must have zero final incoming count.\nRejected candidates discard private roots. Journal append and flush precede\npublishing both rows and indexes. Group preparation retains private roots, and\nan uncertain physical write preserves the original committed roots while fencing\nthe engine. Reopen discovers the persisted prefix and rebuilds its indexes.\n\nRecovery still validates every historical record under the selected constraints;\na later repair cannot hide an invalid earlier record. Final indexes are built\nonce after replay. The wire format does not record this local validation choice,\nso scan and indexed engines can reopen each other's valid journals. Branches\nvalidate their own configured constraints; parent merge validates the parent's\nconstraints. Cluster workspaces retain whole selected-shard generation comparison\nand atomic catalog publication; these local indexes add no distributed locks.\n\n## Costs and composition\n\nLet N be live rows and W the number of changed addresses. Ordered operations are\nO(log N), with additional string comparison/copy costs for names.\n\n| Selection | Work and retained memory |\n| --- | --- |\n| No constraints, either strategy | No index maps or constraint scan |\n| Scan | Visits all rows per selected constraint. Rust uniqueness uses temporary ordered sets; C# uses temporary hash sets. Reference validation uses row lookups. No retained validation index. |\n| Indexed open/replay | Historical complete constraint validation, followed by O(N log N) final index construction |\n| Indexed write | O(W log N) row/index operations and O(W) changed-address buffer, shared with change-record encoding when selected |\n| Indexed retained roots | O(N) entries per selected constraint; pair/name owners and nonzero incoming reference counts; names retain their bytes |\n| Indexed group | Private roots and changed paths per provisional revision, retained until the shared flush result |\n\nRust reuses `rpds::RedBlackTreeMapSync`; C# reuses\n`System.Collections.Immutable.ImmutableSortedDictionary`. Both share unchanged\nnodes. Scan remains useful when retained index memory is undesirable or writes\nalready replace most rows. Indexed validation does not remove flat-map candidate\ncopies, complete snapshot encoding, branch comparison scans, full journal replay\nor physical I/O. Select shared state and change records separately to reduce\nthose two other local commit costs. Retained history and concurrent sessions\nhave their existing costs.\n\nRun `cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --example engine_constraint_cost`\nfor a finite allocation example. Eight one-name commits with all constraints,\nshared state and change records request 54,805 versus 17,845 allocation bytes\nat 128 rows, and 329,269 versus 20,117 at 1,024 rows (scan versus indexed in the\nrecorded native Debug run). Setup/recovery is excluded. These are allocation\nrequests, including reallocations, rather than live memory, timing or durability\nmeasurements; toolchains can change the exact totals. C# deterministic controls\nforbid candidate enumeration and bound one-row preparation to seven row lookups\nat both 8 and 512 rows. Native controls verify unchanged root identity.\n\nThe SQLite interoperability examples accept `--references` to select scanned\nreference checks, or `--indexed-constraints` to select indexed reference checks.\nThey select only this constraint, since successive providers intentionally repeat\npairs and names. The workflow selects references in all sixteen scan/indexed, flat/shared,\nsnapshot/changes and plain/delta compositions, reopening each database through\nRust, C#, Node, Bun and Deno. References)\n    where T : struct, IBinaryInteger<T>, IUnsignedNumber<T>, IMinMaxValue<T>\n{\n    internal static ConstraintIndex<T>? Build(EngineOptions options, IReadOnlyDictionary<T, EngineRow<T>> rows)\n    {\n        if (options.ConstraintValidation != ConstraintValidation.Indexed || options.Constraints.Count == 0) return null;\n        var index = new ConstraintIndex<T>(\n            options.Constraints.Contains(EngineConstraint.UniquePairs) ? ImmutableSortedDictionary<(T, T), T>.Empty : null,\n            options.Constraints.Contains(EngineConstraint.UniqueNames) ? ImmutableSortedDictionary.Create<string, T>(StringComparer.Ordinal) : null,\n            options.Constraints.Contains(EngineConstraint.References) ? ImmutableSortedDictionary<T, int>.Empty : null);\n        return index.Prepare(ImmutableSortedDictionary<T, EngineRow<T>>.Empty, rows, rows.Keys.ToArray());\n    }\n\n    internal ConstraintIndex<T> Prepare(IReadOnlyDictionary<T, EngineRow<T>> before,\n        IReadOnlyDictionary<T, EngineRow<T>> after, IReadOnlyList<T> changed)\n    {\n        var pairs = Pairs; var names = Names; var references = References;\n        // All old keys leave before any new keys enter, permitting atomic swaps.\n        foreach (var id in changed)\n        {\n            bool present = after.TryGetValue(id, out var next);\n            if (!before.TryGetValue(id, out var old)) continue;\n            if (!present || Pair(old) != Pair(next))\n            {\n                pairs = pairs?.Remove(Pair(old));\n                references = ChangeReferences(references, old, false);\n            }\n            if (old.Name != (present ? next.Name : null) && old.Name is { } name) names = names?.Remove(name);\n        }\n        foreach (var id in changed)\n        {\n            bool present = before.TryGetValue(id, out var old);\n            if (!after.TryGetValue(id, out var next)) continue;\n            if (!present || Pair(old) != Pair(next))\n            {\n                if (pairs is not null)\n                {\n                    if (pairs.TryGetValue(Pair(next), out var owner) && owner != id) throw new InvalidOperationException(\"Constraint: duplicate pair.\");\n                    pairs = pairs.SetItem(Pair(next), id);\n                }\n                references = ChangeReferences(references, next, true);\n            }\n            if (next.Name != (present ? old.Name : null) && next.Name is { } name && names is not null)\n            {\n                if (names.TryGetValue(name, out var owner) && owner != id) throw new InvalidOperationException(\"Constraint: duplicate name.\");\n                names = names.SetItem(name, id);\n            }\n        }\n        if (references is not null)\n            foreach (var id in changed)\n            {\n                if (after.TryGetValue(id, out var row))\n                {\n                    if ((row.Link.Source != T.Zero && !after.ContainsKey(row.Link.Source)) || (row.Link.Target != T.Zero && !after.ContainsKey(row.Link.Target)))\n                        throw new InvalidOperationException(\"Constraint: dangling link reference.\");\n                }\n                else if (references.ContainsKey(id)) throw new InvalidOperationException(\"Constraint: dangling link reference.\");\n            }\n        return new(pairs, names, references);\n    }\n\n    private static (T, T) Pair(EngineRow<T> row) => (row.Link.Source, row.Link.Target);\n    private static ImmutableSortedDictionary<T, int>? ChangeReferences(ImmutableSortedDictionary<T, int>? references, EngineRow<T> row, bool add)\n    {\n        if (references is null) return null;\n        foreach (var id in new[] { row.Link.Source, row.Link.Target })\n        {\n            if (id == T.Zero) continue;\n            references.TryGetValue(id, out int count);\n            references = add ? references.SetItem(id, checked(count + 1)) : count > 1 ? references.SetItem(id, count - 1) : references.Remove(id);\n        }\n        return references;\n    }\n}\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Every selected shard's generation is checked, including read-only\nshards. This gives conservative serializable transactions within a selected\ngroup. Network sessions currently support optimistic admission\nand serializable validation; requests for other policies fail explicitly.\n\n## Backends and costs\n\nThe replaceable `AtomicJournalStore` / `IAtomicJournalStore` contract requires\nlinearizable grouped reads, never-reused modification generations, atomic\ncomparison of every selected key, and atomic publication of all changed keys.\nZero denotes an absent key. A custom store must not silently weaken this contract.\nThe supplied `EtcdJournalStore` uses etcd's v3 HTTP JSON gateway. One Txn reads the\ngroup; one Txn validates and publishes. Tune\nbyte bounds together with etcd's server request/quota limits. These limits are\nchecked in addition to engine journal integrity, allocator and constraint checks.\nThis is suitable for small datasets and coordination; it is not a high-throughput\nbulk storage design. One consensus group replicates every journal and limits\naggregate write throughput. More workers and separate shard namespaces spread\nprocessing. Use the optional partitioned decorator below to move journal data\nout of the catalog into independent stores and consensus groups.\n\n## Independent data stores\n\n`PartitionedJournalStore` implements the same atomic journal store contract in\nRust, C# and JS. Supply a catalog, a map of named data stores, and a function\nmapping each shard name to a data-store name. The stores can use separate etcd\ndeployments, disks, memberships and quotas. No application filesystem is shared.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  Workers[Application workers] --> Catalog[Atomic catalog: shard pointers]\n  Workers --> East[East group: immutable journals]\n  Workers --> West[West group: immutable journals]\n  Catalog -. points to .-> East\n  Catalog -. points to .-> West\n```\n\nAt begin, the decorator reads all selected catalog pointers in one linearizable\nsnapshot, then loads their immutable data objects. At commit it creates the\nchanged objects in their routed stores, verifies their complete contents, then\natomically compares every selected catalog generation and publishes the pointers.\nA failed comparison publishes none of the group. A data failure before catalog\npublication leaves only unreferenced objects. An unknown catalog response still\nrequires a fresh read. No data or catalog mutation is automatically retried.\n\nThe portable pointer is four strings: `blob1`, partition name, object key, and\nobject modification generation. This detects accidental\ncorruption and namespace misuse; it does not authenticate an untrusted backend.\nCatalog and data namespaces must be dedicated to this protocol. Keep each\npartition name bound to its original storage namespace, even when changing the\nrouter for future writes. Never delete or mutate objects: old readers may still\nhold pointers. This version retains old and orphan objects, so provision quotas\nand monitor growth. No concurrent garbage collector is supplied.\n\nThe catalog carries O(selected shards) bounded metadata per operation. Split unrelated transaction domains into independent catalogs\nto scale metadata throughput; one transaction cannot span independent catalogs.\nThis does not promise linear throughput scaling or provide LSM compaction.\n`requireDurableFlush` requires the catalog and every configured data store to\ndeclare durable persistence. The wire\nformat and engine implementation here are independent of Iceberg's table format.\n\n## Configuration and ownership\n\nRust enables HTTP/TLS dependencies only with Cargo feature `etcd`.\n`EtcdJournalStore::with_agent` accepts a configured `ureq::Agent`; `headers`\naccepts authorization headers. The default agent uses a finite ten-second global\ndeadline, HTTPS root validation and no redirects. Configure private trust roots,\nclient certificates and proxies through the agent. Cluster engines retain their\nstore through an `Arc<Mutex<_>>`; transactions own private engine handles.\n\nC# accepts an optional `HttpClient`, enabling custom TLS, authentication headers\nand proxies. Safe-integer numbers are\naccepted as input. Anything a `number` cannot hold exactly, or the backend\ncannot store, is refused before sending with `AddressRangeError`. The servers\nand the WebAssembly store use `u32` addresses (`capabilities.maxAddress` is\n2^32 - 1). The client itself is not limited to 32 bits: the unit tests drive a\n64-bit backend with addresses above 2^53.\n\n**Errors** are `LinksError` subclasses. Each carries `outcome`, which tells\nyou what you can know about the request:\n\n- `not-sent`: the request never left the client (abort or deadline before\n  sending, a limit, an address out of range, a closed connection, a missing\n  capability).\n- `failed`: the backend answered `(error: ...)` (`RemoteError`). Nothing\n  changed.\n- `unknown`: the request was sent but its answer is lost (abort or deadline\n  while in flight, a lost connection, an oversized reply). Read the store\n  back before retrying.\n\nOther subclasses: `ProtocolMismatchError` (the peer is not a links server, or\nit refuses the text protocol), `MalformedMessageError`, `LimitExceededError`,\n`ConnectionClosedError`, `AbortError` and `DeadlineExceededError`.\n\n**Cancellation.** `signal` is an `AbortSignal`. `deadline` is absolute (a\n`Date` or epoch milliseconds), and `timeout` becomes `Date.now() + timeout`;\nrequests, memory and disk use.\n\nVersioning follows semver. The wire protocol is versioned separately as\n`capabilities.protocol` (`links-text/1`). See\n[docs/case-studies/issue-108](../../docs/case-studies/issue-108/README.md) for\nthe design and the measurements.\n\n### Optional isolated engine\n\n`WasmEngine` wraps the compiled Rust staged engine with the same asynchronous\nlinks methods on each session. Create a session with `engine.begin()`, issue\nseveral requests, then `await session.commit()` or `await session.rollback()`.\nClosing an uncommitted session rolls it back. Commit shares the request queue,\nso it cannot overtake an earlier write. Defaults are optimistic admission,\nserializable revision validation, no historical retention and a volatile memory log.\nUse `{ serializableValidation: 'read-set' }` for serializable independent point\nedits; scans still validate the entire revision. It composes with log/history\nchoices. See [validation configuration and costs](../../docs/ENGINE-VALIDATION.md).\n\nUse `{ concurrency: 'pessimistic' }` to reserve written addresses until the\nsession ends. Independent writes can proceed; a competing write returns busy\nimmediately. [2026-10-25T19:43:26.821Z] [STDERR] +# Optional immutable journal object cache
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.822Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.824Z] [STDERR] +`PartitionedJournalStore` can retain verified immutable journal objects locally.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.825Z] [STDERR] +The default budget is zero. Enable a payload budget independently of engine
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.826Z] [STDERR] +isolation, validation, history, revision encoding, physical journal and routing.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.827Z] [STDERR] +The catalog and data stores retain their existing atomic journal interfaces.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.829Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.831Z] [STDERR] +| Language | Configuration |
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.832Z] [STDERR] +| --- | --- |
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.834Z] [STDERR] +| Rust | `PartitionedJournalStore::new(catalog, partitions, route)?.with_object_cache(65536)` |
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.836Z] [STDERR] +| C# | `new PartitionedJournalStore(catalog, partitions, route, cacheBytes: 65536)` |
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.838Z] [STDERR] +| JS/TS | `new PartitionedJournalStore(catalog, partitions, route, { cacheBytes: 65536 })` |
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.840Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.842Z] [STDERR] +Rust accepts `usize`. C# rejects negative budgets; JS requires a nonnegative safe
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.843Z] [STDERR] +integer. Changing the Rust builder's budget drops its previous cache. Append
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.846Z] [STDERR] +`--cache` to a partitioned [cluster example](ENGINE-CLUSTERS.md) to select a
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.849Z] [STDERR] +65,536-byte payload budget and repeat committed reads in all three languages.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.850Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.854Z] [STDERR] +Every read first obtains a fresh, linearizable catalog snapshot. Cache identity
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.855Z] [STDERR] +includes the configured partition name, immutable object address and exact object
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.857Z] [STDERR] +generation. A hit returns the current catalog generation and an independent
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.858Z] [STDERR] +record array. Caller changes cannot alter retained records. A miss reads the
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.860Z] [STDERR] +object, verifies its generation and content address, then retains an owned copy
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.861Z] [STDERR] +if it fits. Failed reads and invalid objects are never cached. An oversized
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.862Z] [STDERR] +object remains readable and does not evict previously retained objects.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.864Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.866Z] [STDERR] +The budget counts one byte per object, one per record, and each record's UTF-8
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.869Z] [STDERR] +byte length. Thus `[]` costs 1, `[""]` costs 2, `["é"]` costs 4 and `["😀"]`
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.875Z] [STDERR] +costs 6. Positive overhead bounds even empty objects and records. Least recently
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.881Z] [STDERR] +used objects are evicted until the new object fits; hits promote an object.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.883Z] [STDERR] +Zero allocates no LRU container or retained object copy. C# coordinates cache
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.885Z] [STDERR] +metadata under a local gate and performs external I/O outside it; overlapping
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.886Z] [STDERR] +C#/JS misses can download the same object twice but account for one retained
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.887Z] [STDERR] +copy. Rust's mutable store access serializes fills.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.889Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.892Z] [STDERR] +This budget describes retained payload accounting, not total process memory.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.894Z] [STDERR] +Keys, hash tables, LRU nodes, allocator capacity, temporary downloads and
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.896Z] [STDERR] +caller-owned copies add memory. Eviction can retain container capacity. Rust
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.897Z] [STDERR] +clones string bytes on a hit; C#/JS copy arrays of immutable strings. Each engine
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.899Z] [STDERR] +begin still decodes/replays its complete selected journal. A hit saves the data
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.901Z] [STDERR] +request, transfer and address verification, not that replay or every allocation.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.905Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.908Z] [STDERR] +Catalog comparison and publication always stay fresh. Staging always rereads
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.909Z] [STDERR] +and compares complete object contents, including for an already cached object;
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.912Z] [STDERR] +it never trusts a cache hit to accept a hash collision. Rejected publication
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.915Z] [STDERR] +keeps the original catalog state. A lost publication response still needs a
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.917Z] [STDERR] +fresh catalog read to discover the outcome. The cache adds no distributed lock,
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.918Z] [STDERR] +new durability guarantee, wire format or automatic mutation retry.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.919Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.921Z] [STDERR] +Keep every partition name bound to the same storage namespace and never rewrite
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.923Z] [STDERR] +or delete its immutable objects. A hit reuses previously verified contents: it
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.924Z] [STDERR] +can succeed during a data-store outage, and cannot detect later out-of-protocol
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.925Z] [STDERR] +tampering with that object. The catalog must still be available. FNV addressing
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.927Z] [STDERR] +does not authenticate hostile stores. Old readers can retain pointers after
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.928Z] [STDERR] +publication; no garbage collector or reclamation proof is supplied. The cache
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.931Z] [STDERR] +does not bound persistent old/orphan objects or reduce complete updated-journal
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.933Z] [STDERR] +writes. Those storage and scaling requirements remain open.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.936Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.937Z] [STDERR] +The Rust implementation reuses [`lru` 0.19.0](https://github.com/jeromefroe/lru-rs),
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.938Z] [STDERR] +with default features disabled to use standard hashing. Its ordering is bounded
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.940Z] [STDERR] +by this wrapper's payload accounting. C# uses standard `Dictionary` and
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.941Z] [STDERR] +`LinkedList`; JS uses standard insertion-ordered `Map`. No native package enters
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.942Z] [STDERR] +the universal JS entry point. See the [source review](case-studies/issue-138/RESEARCH.md).
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.943Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.945Z] [STDERR] +Portable Rust contracts also execute in actual WASM. Rust, C# and JS test fresh
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.946Z] [STDERR] +catalogs, ownership, default/zero/oversized budgets, exact UTF-8 costs, empty
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.948Z] [STDERR] +objects, partition/generation separation, LRU promotion, failed fetch/repair,
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.950Z] [STDERR] +staging checks and rejected/uncertain publication. Each language compares 768
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.952Z] [STDERR] +reads against a finite independent ordering/cost oracle. C#/JS additionally
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.953Z] [STDERR] +force overlapping misses and verify retained accounting. The real-etcd harness
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.954Z] [STDERR] +uses separate catalog/east/west consensus groups and request counters: a second
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.955Z] [STDERR] +WASM engine begin reads the catalog once with zero repeated data requests.
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.957Z] [STDERR] +Run `bash experiments/issue-138/validate-object-cache.sh` after setting up its
[2026-10-25T19:43:26.958Z] [STDERR] +documented validation tools and downloading the etcd binary.

[2026-10-25T19:43:27.039Z] [STDERR] +## Immutable object reuse and bounded caching (2026-10-25)
[2026-10-25T19:43:27.040Z] [STDERR] +

[2026-10-25T19:43:27.043Z] [STDERR] +optimistic concurrency, manifests and snapshots: immutable files can be reused
[2026-10-25T19:43:27.045Z] [STDERR] +across atomically published metadata versions. Inference for this protocol:
[2026-10-25T19:43:27.046Z] [STDERR] +already verified objects can be retained while catalog snapshots remain fresh.

[2026-10-25T19:43:27.049Z] [STDERR] +It does not supply manifests, incremental transfer or snapshot-aware reclamation.

[2026-10-25T19:43:27.057Z] [STDERR] +`unbounded` (258–260), sentinel construction (300–319), `put` and replacement
[2026-10-25T19:43:27.060Z] [STDERR] +(342–440), promotion in `get` (459–475), removal (1293–1318), and `pop_lru`
[2026-10-25T19:43:27.062Z] [STDERR] +(1377–1383). The maintained component owns hash/list ordering, including its

Choose its concurrency, isolation, constraints and retention\nseparately. Unfinished sessions on either engine remain private. Branch addresses\nare local: independently allocating the same address with different values\ncreates a merge conflict. Equal complete rows converge; no address remapping is\nperformed. Use disjoint address ranges or externally assigned addresses when\nindependent branches must allocate without collisions.\n\nMerge compares each changed complete row with its saved base and the current\nparent. Disjoint changes combine; identical changes converge; divergent edits,\ndelete/update conflicts and name changes to the same row conflict. The parent\nvalidates its constraints and flushes one selected logical revision before publishing any\nmerged rows. Exclusive admission and existing session conflict checks still\napply. Repeating an unchanged successful merge adds no revision. A three-way\nmerge validates its resulting state, but does not retroactively serialize the\nindependent transactions that produced both histories.\n\nAfter a successful merge, persist `merge_base_record()` / `MergeBaseRecord` /\n`mergeBaseRecord()` with application metadata. To reopen, open the same logical\nparent and call `resume_branch` / `ResumeBranch` / `resumeBranch` with the branch\njournal and descriptor. The descriptor contains the complete committed branch\nbase, so in-memory history eviction does not invalidate it. Recovery verifies\nthat it matches an actual branch journal revision and validates the complete\njournal. The caller is responsible for associating it with the right parent;\nthe checksum is not an authenticated lineage identifier.\n\nAn older saved descriptor allows replay after a crash between parent commit and\ndescriptor persistence: already identical rows are accepted, while divergent\noverlap conflicts conservatively. An append/flush error during merge has an\nunknown outcome and poisons the parent; reopen it before outcome discovery or\nretry. Failure to seed a branch leaves the parent untouched, but the branch log\nmay contain the seed and must be inspected/reopened rather than blindly reused.\nFork and merge use the receiving engine's selected flat/shared map and the same\nO(N) record format. Mixed representation forks convert their initial rows.\n\n## Distributed ownership and horizontal scale\n\nReplicated logs have a fixed, externally fenced primary and fixed followers.\nA follower must be an exact prefix of the primary; divergent or ahead followers\nare rejected. Catch-up appends only missing records, then flushes. Scheduling is\nexplicit, so a bare store pays no background replication cost. Adapter resources\nremain owned by the caller; close sessions and engines before releasing them.\n\nA shared-storage deployment must enforce one writer through the file adapter's\nadvisory lock or an external fencing mechanism that every writer respects.\nLocal advisory locks are not a distributed lease and must not be assumed to\nwork on an arbitrary network filesystem. A shared-nothing deployment gives\nindependent logs and failure domains to followers and each independent shard.\nPartition tenants/keys into separate engines to scale aggregate independent\nwork horizontally. Addresses are local to a shard; use `(shard, address)` in\napplication references and keep an atomic transaction within one shard.\n\nSafe automatic primary election, changing membership, consensus, cross-shard\natomic transactions, and a routing/network service are not supplied by these\nlog decorators. They require protocols beyond acknowledgement counting. Existing\n`RemoteLinks` TCP stores carry individual links operations; they do not create a\ntransaction boundary across connections. Do not infer any of those guarantees\nfrom a replicated in-memory test.\n\n## Costs and comparison\n\nThe default flat representation clones current rows for each write commit and\nwrites a complete logical revision. Candidate creation costs O(N); applying W\nwrites costs O(W log N), followed by the selected revision encoding. Flat scans\nmaterialize their view and history can retain O(HN) map entries. Optional\n[shared immutable state](ENGINE-SHARED-STATE.md) replaces those map copies with\nan O(1) root and O(W log N) changed paths, preserving earlier snapshots and\nsharing unchanged entries during recovery. Optional [change records](ENGINE-CHANGE-RECORDS.md)\nserialize changed rows. Selected constraints and scans still visit the full state. The allocator is shared. Optimistic read-committed\nand snapshot sessions, plus serializable read-set sessions, track per-address changes only while another session can\nbe stale, retaining deleted-address tombstones to detect delete/recreate races.\nThe final session validates before reclaiming that map. Opening an engine,\nexclusive admission and optimistic whole-revision serializable validation do not build\nper-row generations. A continuously overlapping set of sessions can still retain\nmany changed addresses; end sessions promptly. Pessimistic admission additionally\ntracks reserved write addresses and generations under all isolation levels; its\n[separate cost description](ENGINE-PESSIMISTIC.md) explains ownership and cleanup.\nRecovery reads the full log; retention bounds in-memory history, not log size.\nOptional single-span delta encoding reduces physical bytes for localized changes\nand adds an O(N) comparison for full records; changes pass through without that\ncomparison. Neither compacts history. Replication catch-up compares prefixes\nand copies missing logical records.\nOptional [caller-selected group commit](ENGINE-GROUP-COMMIT.md) shares one flush\nacross independent sessions while buffering their selected logical records.\nThere is no automatic grouping scheduler or background compaction. These limits\nmatter for a large or frequently written database.\n\n| Competitor configuration | Closest available configuration | Material difference |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| SQLite WAL with synchronous commit | Optional SQLite log + staged engine, selected isolation | Reuses SQLite page WAL/FULL and checkpointing; logical links revisions still replay the retained journal. C# and JS\nreject repeated object identities, but different wrappers can still alias the\nsame underlying storage; the adapter owner must prevent that aliasing.\n\nJS/WASM custom adapters implement `read(): string` (a JSON array of record\nstrings), `append(record): void`, `flush(): void`, and a boolean\n`supportsDurableFlush`. Append and flush must complete synchronously and return\nundefined. A Promise cannot provide this boundary and is rejected. Browser\nIndexedDB and other asynchronous storage require a server-side engine or a\nseparate asynchronous transaction interface; an exported in-memory journal is\nnot a durable commit. Caller-owned adapters outlive all sessions that use them.\n\n## Coordinated network groups\n\n[ClusterEngine](ENGINE-CLUSTERS.md) composes the same links API with an atomic\njournal store. An oversized\nobject remains readable and does not evict previously retained objects.\n\nThe budget counts one byte per object, one per record, and each record's UTF-8\nbyte length. [2026-10-25T20:29:19.700Z] [STDERR] *** Add File: /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1792924568628/docs/UNICODE-SEQUENCE-INTEGRITY.md
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.702Z] [STDERR] +# Unicode sequence graph integrity
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.705Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.707Z] [STDERR] +Unicode strings in ordinary named storage use typed symbol leaves and binary
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.712Z] [STDERR] +sequence links. A sequence is a graph: unchanged subtrees can appear more than
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.716Z] [STDERR] +once. Each occurrence contributes its symbols, in source-before-target order.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.718Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.718Z] [STDERR] +Rust and C# now detect a sequence node appearing twice on the active traversal
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.723Z] [STDERR] +path. Self-cycles and cycles through either child fail with a decoding error.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.726Z] [STDERR] +Missing children also fail; they cannot silently drop part of a Rust string.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.728Z] [STDERR] +Repeated valid subtrees remain valid. Traversal uses an explicit stack, so a
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.729Z] [STDERR] +deep finite sequence does not consume one call-stack frame per graph level.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.731Z] [STDERR] +Each call owns its path and stack; a failed decode leaves no traversal state
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.735Z] [STDERR] +for the next read. Name decoding propagates these failures.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.738Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.742Z] [STDERR] +| Surface | Behavior |
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.744Z] [STDERR] +| --- | --- |
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.750Z] [STDERR] +| Rust `UnicodeStringStorage::get_string` | Returns `Err` for cyclic/missing sequence graphs and existing UTF-16 errors. |
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.752Z] [STDERR] +| Rust `unicode_sequence_code_units` | Returns `Err` for cyclic/missing graphs; retains raw UTF-16 code units, including lone surrogates. |
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.755Z] [STDERR] +| Rust `RightSequenceWalker::try_walk` | Checked `Result<Vec<u32>>`, preserving every leaf occurrence. |
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.759Z] [STDERR] +| Rust `RightSequenceWalker::walk` | Existing Vec signature; valid graphs retain their output, malformed graphs panic with guidance to use `try_walk`. |
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.762Z] [STDERR] +| C# `GetString` / `UnicodeSequenceToStringConverter.Convert` | Throw `InvalidDataException` for cycles or missing sequence nodes; retain existing UTF-16 string behavior. |
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.764Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.772Z] [STDERR] +C# keeps `Platform.Data.Doublets.Sequences`' maintained Unicode converter and
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.778Z] [STDERR] +supplies validation through its existing `ISequenceWalker<T>` interface. This
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.785Z] [STDERR] +does not fork the converter or change the stored representation. Rust keeps
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.790Z] [STDERR] +its existing typed matcher, converters and public compatibility wrapper.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.793Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.796Z] [STDERR] +Active-path metadata costs O(depth), in addition to the existing stack and
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.801Z] [STDERR] +decoded output. The walker expands shared subtrees for each occurrence rather
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.804Z] [STDERR] +than skipping previously visited nodes. This is graph-integrity validation,
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.808Z] [STDERR] +not a decoded-output budget: a compact valid DAG can represent large output.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.811Z] [STDERR] +No new physical repair or power-loss guarantee is supplied. Existing converter
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.816Z] [STDERR] +memoization remains unchanged; cached results do not traverse the graph again.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.819Z] [STDERR] +This check applies when decoding actually traverses stored links.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.824Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.829Z] [STDERR] +The native before tests use bounded child processes. Linux Rust children have
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.832Z] [STDERR] +128 MiB address-space/two-second CPU limits and a ten-second parent deadline;
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.843Z] [STDERR] +C# children cap the managed heap at 128 MiB on every platform, add Linux CPU
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.846Z] [STDERR] +limits, disable dumps and have a ten-second parent deadline. Children are
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.849Z] [STDERR] +reaped. Actual-WASM portable contracts execute the same graph cases through
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.852Z] [STDERR] +the maintained wasm-bindgen test runner. The universal JS API has no direct
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.854Z] [STDERR] +typed sequence-graph decoder; its existing actual-WASM client conformance is
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.856Z] [STDERR] +checked without adding an unrelated public API.
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.859Z] [STDERR] +
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.861Z] [STDERR] +Tests cover both directions of self/two-node cycles, repeated rejection,
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.867Z] [STDERR] +healthy following reads, malformed name propagation, Unicode order, repeated
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.876Z] [STDERR] +shared subtrees, 2,048-level valid sequences, missing children, existing UTF-16
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.883Z] [STDERR] +policies and repeated native file reopening. See the
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.894Z] [STDERR] +[work plan](case-studies/issue-138/UNICODE-GRAPH-PLAN.md),
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.905Z] [STDERR] +[before evidence](../dev/log/issues/138/pulls/139/unicode-graph-before.txt)
[2026-10-25T20:29:19.919Z] [STDERR] +and `experiments/issue-138/validate-unicode-graph.sh`.

A sequence is a graph: unchanged subtrees can appear more than\n+once. Each occurrence contributes its symbols, in source-before-target order.\n+\n+Rust and C# now detect a sequence node appearing twice on the active traversal\n+path. Self-cycles and cycles through either child fail with a decoding error.\n+Missing children also fail; they cannot silently drop part of a Rust string.\n+Repeated valid subtrees remain valid. Traversal uses an explicit stack, so a\n+deep finite sequence does not consume one call-stack frame per graph level.\n+Each call owns its path and stack; a failed decode leaves no traversal state\n+for the next read.
